Step 02.05 — Confirm the four Z rails are already cleaned and greased
docs.text:
Step 5 of 44 · Chapter 02 — Z drives, Z idlers, Z rails, deck panel

Do:

  1. Unbag the four rails marked Z0–Z3; check labels and carriage tape.
  2. Run each carriage end to end: smooth and silent, not dry or notchy.
  3. Work over the bench, never the floor: a dropped carriage is scrap.

Parts:

  • MGN9H 400 mm rails ×4 (the four labelled Z0–Z3 in Ch 00)

Check

Four labelled rails on the bench, carriages taped or stoppered, each smooth and silent over full travel, no grease on any rail's outside.

What you're looking at

Manual p.24 shows a linear rail and its carriage. These four MGN9H rails are the vertical tracks the gantry's corners ride on. They were degreased and packed with grease in Ch 00, because that job needs the back of the rail. See the glossary.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: the kit does not include grease, and the rails ship with a shipping oil rather than a lubricant. If you do have to prep a rail here, use NLGI 0 or NLGI 1 — Super Lube 21030, Mobilux EP1/EP2, or white lithium — never a thin oil or a PTFE dry lube. src

Tip

If a rail was missed, do Ch 00 Steps 00.18–00.20 on it now and let it dry completely before it goes near the frame.

Source: Voron manual p.24 · LDO rail grease guide · LDO Build Notes (Rev D)

← PreviousStep 02.04 — Seat the heat-set inserts in the Z drive parts

Next →Step 02.06 — Fit the first Z rail, centred, with the MGN9 guides

docs.title: Step 02.06 — Fit the first Z rail, centred, with the MGN9 guides
Step 02.06 — Fit the first Z rail, centred, with the MGN9 guides
docs.text:
Step 6 of 44 · Chapter 02 — Z drives, Z idlers, Z rails, deck panel

Do:

  1. Slip a MGN9_rail_guide over each rail end.
  2. Pre-load nine M3 T-nuts in the front-left vertical's rear-looking face.
  3. Rest the rail on a 3 mm hex key and start nine screws finger-tight in holes 2, 4 … 18.

Parts:

  • MGN9H 400 mm rail ×1
  • M3×8 SHCS ×9
  • M3 roll-in T-nut ×9
  • MGN9_rail_guide_x2 jigs ×2
  • a 3 mm hex key as the feeler

Check

Rail centred on the front-left vertical's rear-looking face, sitting on the 3 mm key, all nine screws started, both end holes empty.

What you're looking at

Manual p.25 shows a rail going onto a vertical extrusion, with the printed rail guides drawn in green. The guides straddle rail and extrusion and hold the rail centred on the 20 mm face while you start the screws.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: LDO's note "do not use the holes on the ends of the rails, use the second ones from the ends" is written against manual p.88; the survey generalises it to every rail (§4.4 #6). Use holes 2, 4 … 18 of a 20-hole rail on all four Z rails. src

Tip

Tape-mark the nine holes before you start. Test-fit each T-nut: if one jams, swap the nut, not the face. On the rear verticals the rail faces forward.

Tip

Peel the two end-stop bands from Step 00.17 only with the rail lying flat on the bench, never on edge or with the carriage near an end.

Source: Voron manual p.25 · LDO Build Notes (Rev D)

← PreviousStep 02.05 — Confirm the four Z rails are already cleaned and greased

Next →Step 02.07 — Tighten from the centre outward

docs.title: Step 02.07 — Tighten from the centre outward
Step 02.07 — Tighten from the centre outward
docs.text:
Step 7 of 44 · Chapter 02 — Z drives, Z idlers, Z rails, deck panel

Do:

  1. Tighten from the middle of the rail outward, alternating up and down. Snug, not gorilla-tight: an M3 into a T-nut will strip.
  2. If a tight spot shows, back the screws off and re-tighten from the centre.

Parts:

  • the rail from Step 02.06

Check

With the guides removed, the carriage feels identical at every point over the rail's full length. Any tight spot means the rail is not flush.

What you're looking at

Manual p.25 again: the same rail, now being tightened. Working outward from the middle presses the rail flat against the extrusion. Starting at one end walks a bow along the rail, and a bow is the tight spot you feel later.

Source: Voron manual p.25 · Voron manual p.24

← PreviousStep 02.06 — Fit the first Z rail, centred, with the MGN9 guides

Next →Step 02.08 — Secure the carriage before the printer is turned over

docs.title: Step 02.08 — Secure the carriage before the printer is turned over
Step 02.08 — Secure the carriage before the printer is turned over
docs.text:
Step 8 of 44 · Chapter 02 — Z drives, Z idlers, Z rails, deck panel

Do: Tape the carriage to the rail, or refit the plastic shipping stopper, so gravity cannot walk it off the end. The printer goes upside down at Step 02.11 and an untethered carriage slides off the bottom end.

Parts:

  • masking tape, or the rail's plastic shipping stoppers, or optional z_rail_stop_x4

Check

The carriage cannot move to the end of the rail under its own weight.

What you're looking at

Manual p.26: the carriage and the risk. The carriage rides on recirculating ball bearings retained only by the rail, so it must be tethered before the frame is inverted. A carriage that runs off the end spills its balls and is scrap.

Good stopping point · ~25 min since the last one

the first Z rail is centred, tightened centre-outward, verified smooth over full travel, and its carriage is taped. A rail is a self-contained unit; stop only with one finished, never with half its screws started.

Source: Voron manual p.26

← PreviousStep 02.07 — Tighten from the centre outward

Next →Step 02.09 — Install the remaining three Z rails

docs.title: Step 02.09 — Install the remaining three Z rails
Step 02.09 — Install the remaining three Z rails
docs.text:
Step 9 of 44 · Chapter 02 — Z drives, Z idlers, Z rails, deck panel

Do: Repeat Steps 02.06–02.08 on the other three verticals. Each rail faces the other rail on its own side: front-left faces rear-left, front-right faces rear-right. Keep the same 3 mm bottom gap and holes 2–18 on all four.

Parts:

  • MGN9H 400 mm rails ×3
  • M3×8 SHCS ×27
  • M3 roll-in T-nut ×27

Check

Four rails installed, the two rails on each side pointing at each other, all four bottom gaps equal, every carriage taped and running smoothly.

What you're looking at

Manual p.27: all four Z rails on their verticals. Read the graphic for the mounting face, not the pairing. The two left rails face each other across the machine's depth, and the two right rails do the same.

Caution

Manual p.27 says only "make sure the rails face each other as shown in the graphic" and leaves the pairing to the drawing. The official CAD at the pinned commit de7e89d says every Z rail's mounting face is normal to ±Y: the two rear rails face forward, the two front rails face rearward. Corrected 2026-09-05. src

Tip

The CAD is the 250 machine: MGN9 300 mm rails on 430 mm verticals. Yours are MGN9H 400 mm on 350 verticals; the mounting face is the same.

Source: Voron manual p.27 · CAD-render pilot §8 — Z rail orientation · Voron-2 CAD Voron_2.4r2_Assembly_STEP.zip @ de7e89d · CAD: Voron 2.4r2 STEP @ de7e89d

← PreviousStep 02.08 — Secure the carriage before the printer is turned over

Next →Step 02.10 — Optional: fit the LDO rail stops at the top of each Z rail

docs.title: Step 02.10 — Optional: fit the LDO rail stops at the top of each Z rail
Step 02.10 — Optional: fit the LDO rail stops at the top of each Z rail
docs.text:
Step 10 of 44 · Chapter 02 — Z drives, Z idlers, Z rails, deck panel

Do: If B05 is already printed, fit a stop to the top of each Z rail now, while the rails are accessible. If not, skip: the tape from Step 02.08 covers you until Ch 06.

Parts:

  • z_rail_stop_x4.stl ×4 (LDO repo, black) — printed in batch B05, which comes after this chapter in the timeline

Check

A stop on each of the four rails, or a decision to defer them to Ch 06 with the tape left in place.

What you're looking at

The grey render is the LDO rail stop, a printed clip that caps a rail's top end so a carriage cannot run off during the gantry install in Ch 06. It clips to the free top length above the carriage.

Tip

LDO also uses a rubber rail stopper under the Z joints as a gantry rest at manual p.114–116. That is Chapter 06 — do not confuse the two. src

Tip

The CAD rail is MGN9 300 mm on a 430 mm vertical, leaving ~107 mm bare above it. The stop clips to the rail end, not to a dimension.

Good stopping point · ~35 min since the last one

all four Z rails are on, facing each other, sharing the same ~3 mm bottom gap and hole pattern, every carriage taped or stoppered. The frame is still the right way up. Do not turn it over until the carriages are secured.

Source: LDO printed parts guide (Rev D) · LDO Build Notes (Rev D) · CAD render — assets/cad/PILOT.md · Video: Part 4 @1:27:15 · CAD: Voron 2.4r2 STEP @ de7e89d

← PreviousStep 02.09 — Install the remaining three Z rails

Next →Step 02.11 — Turn the printer upside down and pre-load the deck T-nuts

docs.title: Step 02.11 — Turn the printer upside down and pre-load the deck T-nuts
Step 02.11 — Turn the printer upside down and pre-load the deck T-nuts
docs.text:
Step 11 of 44 · Chapter 02 — Z drives, Z idlers, Z rails, deck panel

Do: Confirm every carriage is taped, then turn the frame upside down onto the flat reference surface. Slide four M5 T-nuts into the upward-facing slots of the two bed extrusions, two per extrusion, where the deck panel's holes will land.

Parts:

  • M5 roll-in T-nut ×4

Check

Frame sits flat and does not rock in this orientation; four T-nuts in, free to slide, none dropped inside an extrusion.

What you're looking at

Manual p.28: the frame inverted, with four M5 roll-in T-nuts dropped into the top slots of the two bed extrusions. The printer spends the next fifteen manual pages upside down because every Z drive bolts to the underside of the bottom frame rails.

Tip

Load the 16 drive-corner M5 T-nuts now too, four per bottom corner, two in each extrusion that meets there. Test-fit each slot: LDO's T-nut tolerance note applies. src

Source: Voron manual p.28

← PreviousStep 02.10 — Optional: fit the LDO rail stops at the top of each Z rail

Next →Step 02.12 — Caliper the deck panel and choose the support thickness

docs.title: Step 02.12 — Caliper the deck panel and choose the support thickness
Step 02.12 — Caliper the deck panel and choose the support thickness
docs.text:
Step 12 of 44 · Chapter 02 — Z drives, Z idlers, Z rails, deck panel

Do: Measure the actual thickness of your deck panel with the caliper, in three places. Do not resolve this from documents. Pick the clip set that matches what you measured; the clips go in at Step 02.14, after the panel.

Parts:

  • deck panel
  • caliper
  • deck_support_3mm_x8 ×8 (printed, B01)
  • deck_support_4mm_x8 only if the caliper says 4 mm — a 30-minute reprint

Check

Three readings agree within 0.1 mm, the number is in your build log, and eight clips of the matching thickness are on the bench.

What you're looking at

Manual p.29: the deck panel and its support clips. The deck panel is the acrylic floor separating the electronics bay below from the print chamber above. See the glossary. The printed clips twist into the extrusion slots and their ledges carry the panel's edges.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: LDO's build note for p.29–30 says the LDO deck panel is 4 mm nominal — use deck_support_4mm, but the Rev D 350 BOM lists it as 469×469×3 mm. The size-specific 350 BOM wins, so B01 prints the 3 mm** set. Measure, fit whichever matches, reprint the other if you have to. src · BOM

Source: Voron manual p.29 · LDO Build Notes (Rev D) · LDO 350 Rev D BOM · Video: Part 2 @0:56:54

← PreviousStep 02.11 — Turn the printer upside down and pre-load the deck T-nuts

Next →Step 02.13 — Drop the deck panel in, notch to the back

docs.title: Step 02.13 — Drop the deck panel in, notch to the back
Step 02.13 — Drop the deck panel in, notch to the back
docs.text:
Step 13 of 44 · Chapter 02 — Z drives, Z idlers, Z rails, deck panel

Do:

  1. Peel any protective film.
  2. Lower the panel into the bottom frame's opening, cut-out notch toward the back, flat on both bed extrusions.
  3. Line the four bolt holes up over the four T-nuts.

Parts:

  • deck panel ×1

Check

Notch at the back. Panel inside the frame opening, flat on both bed extrusions, flush with the frame face, no rock or gap.

What you're looking at

Manual p.28: the deck panel dropping onto the bed extrusions. The panel is cut 1 mm smaller than the bottom frame's opening, 469 mm on the 350, so it sits inside the frame on the two bed extrusions. The cut-out notch is the cable pass-through.

Source: Voron manual p.28 · LDO 350 Rev D BOM

← PreviousStep 02.12 — Caliper the deck panel and choose the support thickness

Next →Step 02.14 — Fit the deck support clips

docs.title: Step 02.14 — Fit the deck support clips
Step 02.14 — Fit the deck support clips
docs.text:
Step 14 of 44 · Chapter 02 — Z drives, Z idlers, Z rails, deck panel

Do:

  1. Push a clip's tab end-on into the inward-facing slot of a bottom-frame extrusion above the panel edge, then twist it 90° so the ledge lies over the panel.
  2. Two per side, evenly spaced (verify on bench).

Parts:

  • deck support clips ×8 (the thickness you chose in Step 02.12)

Check

Eight ledges over the panel edge, all the same thickness variant; the panel cannot be lifted out of the frame.

What you're looking at

Manual p.29: eight deck support clips going into the extrusion slots. Each deck_support is a small T-tab, about 20 × 14.5 × 5.8 mm, with a ledge. Inverted, these eight ledges are the only thing carrying the panel until Ch 09 bolts it.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: this step is not in the official manual at all. LDO adds it here: "This is a good time to install the deck supports." Doing it later means the deck comes out and the frame comes partly apart (§5.2 W4). src

Source: Voron manual p.29 · LDO Build Notes (Rev D) · Video: Part 2 @0:56:54

← PreviousStep 02.13 — Drop the deck panel in, notch to the back

Next →Step 02.15 — Line the four M5 T-nuts up under the deck holes and stop there

docs.title: Step 02.15 — Line the four M5 T-nuts up under the deck holes and stop there
Step 02.15 — Line the four M5 T-nuts up under the deck holes and stop there
docs.text:
Step 15 of 44 · Chapter 02 — Z drives, Z idlers, Z rails, deck panel

Do:

  1. Slide each T-nut directly under one of the four deck-panel holes, then leave them there.
  2. The two 35 mm DIN rails and the four M5×10 BHCS that clamp them go on in Ch 09 Step 09.5.

Parts:

  • the four M5 T-nuts already in the bed extrusions. No bolts and no DIN rails yet.

Check

Four T-nuts visible through the four deck holes, free to nudge but not lost inside an extrusion. Panel sitting flat, unbolted, notch to the back.

What you're looking at

Manual p.29: the four T-nuts sitting under the four holes in the deck, and nothing else. The bolts that go through those holes also clamp the two DIN rails that carry the electronics, so they belong to one step in Ch 09.

Tip

If a DIN rail's own slots will not line up when you get there, Ch 09 shortens the DIN rail rather than moving the panel. src

Source: Voron manual p.29 · LDO wiring guide § Installing the DIN Rails and Wire Ducts

← PreviousStep 02.14 — Fit the deck support clips

Next →Step 02.16 — Fix the printer's orientation in your head

docs.title: Step 02.16 — Fix the printer's orientation in your head
Step 02.16 — Fix the printer's orientation in your head
docs.text:
Step 16 of 44 · Chapter 02 — Z drives, Z idlers, Z rails, deck panel

Do: Put a strip of masking tape on the front bottom frame rail, the one the front ends of the two bed extrusions run into, and write "FRONT" on it.

Parts: none.

Check

Front face marked, and you can restate the Z0–Z3 map from Step 02.02 with the printer inverted.

What you're looking at

Manual p.30: the orientation cube the manual prints on every graphic from here on. With the printer inverted, front and back stop being obvious, and every "which corner" callout for the rest of the chapter is read against that marker.

Good stopping point · ~30 min since the last one

the printer is inverted and stable, the deck panel is in with its notch to the back and captured by eight support clips of the measured thickness, the four M5 T-nuts sit under the deck holes, and the FRONT tape is on. Leave the deck unbolted: those four bolts belong to Ch 09 Step 09.5.

Source: Voron manual p.30

← PreviousStep 02.15 — Line the four M5 T-nuts up under the deck holes and stop there

Next →Step 02.17 — Fit the 20T pulley to the 5×60 shaft, 33 mm out

docs.title: Step 02.17 — Fit the 20T pulley to the 5×60 shaft, 33 mm out
Step 02.17 — Fit the 20T pulley to the 5×60 shaft, 33 mm out
docs.text:
Step 17 of 44 · Chapter 02 — Z drives, Z idlers, Z rails, deck panel

Do:

  1. Slide the 20T pulley on so 33 mm of shaft protrudes on the long side.
  2. Rotate until you see the D-cut flat down a set-screw hole.
  3. Fit both set screws with a hex driver, not a ball-end.

Parts:

  • 5×60 mm shaft ×1
  • GT2 20T 9 mm pulley ×1
  • M4×4 set screws ×2 (pre-threadlocked)

Check

One set-screw hole showed the flat before the screws went in; 33 mm from the long shaft end to the pulley's toothed face.

What you're looking at

Manual p.32: the Z drive's shaft assembly. The 5 × 60 mm shaft is the drive's axle; the 20T pulley is what the long Z belt runs over. A set screw is a headless screw that clamps a pulley to a shaft.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: the kit's M4×4 set screws arrive with threadlocker pre-applied — do not add more. If a screw has clearly been used before or has no visible compound, add Loctite 243 and keep it off the printed parts. src

Source: Voron manual p.32 · LDO 350 Rev D BOM

← PreviousStep 02.16 — Fix the printer's orientation in your head

Next →Step 02.18 — Verify the pulley with the jig, then repeat ×4

docs.title: Step 02.18 — Verify the pulley with the jig, then repeat ×4
Step 02.18 — Verify the pulley with the jig, then repeat ×4
docs.text:
Step 18 of 44 · Chapter 02 — Z drives, Z idlers, Z rails, deck panel

Do: Check the pulley position against the printed pulley_jig, then build the other three shaft/pulley pairs the same way.

Parts:

  • pulley_jig.stl
  • the remaining three shafts and 20T pulleys
  • M4×4 set screws ×6

Check

Four shafts, four 20T pulleys, all at the same protrusion, all with a set screw on the flat, all eight set screws tight.

What you're looking at

Manual p.32 with the printed pulley_jig: a flat gauge with steps cut to the pulley heights the build uses. It repeats the 33 mm dimension across all four shafts without re-measuring, so the four corners lift on belts that all sit in the same plane.

Source: Voron manual p.32 · Voron-2 STLs/Tools

← PreviousStep 02.17 — Fit the 20T pulley to the 5×60 shaft, 33 mm out

Next →Step 02.19 — Build the bearing/pulley stack on each shaft

docs.title: Step 02.19 — Build the bearing/pulley stack on each shaft
Step 02.19 — Build the bearing/pulley stack on each shaft
docs.text:
Step 19 of 44 · Chapter 02 — Z drives, Z idlers, Z rails, deck panel

Do: Outward from the 20T pulley: a 625 bearing on its collar side; on the other side two M5 spacers, a 625, two spacers, 80T pulley, and the last 625 on the shaft end. Press by hand, inner race only.

Parts:

  • per drive — 625-2RS bearings ×3
  • GT2 80T pulley ×1
  • M5 precision spacer 1 mm ×4
  • the shaft from Step 02.17

Check

Your stack matches the p.33 graphic: both outer bearings spin free, no spacer trapped crooked, the 80T running true with no rim wobble.

What you're looking at

Manual p.33: the full stack on the shaft. Three 625-2RS bearings, plain 5 × 16 × 5 mm ball bearings, carry the shaft; the 80T pulley is what the short 188 mm belt drives, and the brass precision spacers set the spacing. See the glossary.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: the manual says "M5 Shim". The kit supplies brass M5 precision spacers instead — use those, everywhere in the manual from p.19 onward unless a note says otherwise. Four per drive, 16 for this chapter. src

Source: Voron manual p.33 · LDO Build Notes (Rev D) · Video: Part 2 @0:06:45

← PreviousStep 02.18 — Verify the pulley with the jig, then repeat ×4

Next →Step 02.20 — Threadlock the 80T pulley set screws and check your work

docs.title: Step 02.20 — Threadlock the 80T pulley set screws and check your work
Step 02.20 — Threadlock the 80T pulley set screws and check your work
docs.text:
Step 20 of 44 · Chapter 02 — Z drives, Z idlers, Z rails, deck panel

Do: Set the 80T pulley so a set screw meets the shaft's flat, fit both set screws with threadlocker, and tighten. Build all four stacks.

Parts:

  • M4×4 set screws ×2 per 80T pulley

Check

Four complete shaft assemblies, all matching the graphic, none able to slip when you twist the 80T pulley against the shaft by hand.

What you're looking at

Manual p.33: the 80T pulley's two set screws. This is the joint the entire weight of the gantry hangs on through the belt, and loose set screws are the most-reported failure on this machine, so both get threadlocker and one lands on the flat.

Source: Voron manual p.33 · Video: Part 1 @3:46:04

← PreviousStep 02.19 — Build the bearing/pulley stack on each shaft

Next →Step 02.21 — Fit the 188 mm closed belt loop over the 80T pulley

docs.title: Step 02.21 — Fit the 188 mm closed belt loop over the 80T pulley
Step 02.21 — Fit the 188 mm closed belt loop over the 80T pulley
docs.text:
Step 21 of 44 · Chapter 02 — Z drives, Z idlers, Z rails, deck panel

Do: Drop the closed belt loop over the 80T pulley, teeth inward, before the shaft goes into the housing. The loop has no join, so this is the only moment it can go on.

Parts:

  • Gates 2GT closed loop 6 mm × 188 mm ×1 per drive

Check

Loop seated in the 80T pulley's teeth, hanging free, not twisted.

What you're looking at

Manual p.34: the closed 188 mm belt loop dropped over the 80T pulley. It is a continuous loop with no join, so it has to be threaded on before the drive is closed.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: LDO publishes no deviation for the Z belt loop, the 16T/80T pulleys or the Z gear ratio — the Build Notes for p.22–51 cover only p.29–30 (deck supports) and p.39 (stepper wiring). The kit's Klipper config confirms the stock arrangement: [stepper_z] rotation_distance: 40, gear_ratio: 80:16. Use the 188 mm loops as supplied. src

Good stopping point · ~35 min since the last one

four complete shaft assemblies: 20T pulleys at 33 mm, bearing and precision-spacer stacks built, 80T pulleys threadlocked, and the 188 mm belt loops hung on. The bearings are only slid onto the shaft here, so nothing is mid-assembly. Do not start Step 02.22 until you can close a drive in one sitting.

Source: Voron manual p.34 · LDO Build Notes (Rev D) · LDO Klipper config leviathan-printer-rev-d-sbv2.cfg · Video: Part 1 @3:29:28

← PreviousStep 02.20 — Threadlock the 80T pulley set screws and check your work

Next →Step 02.22 — Seat the shaft assembly into z_drive_retainer (the shallow half)

docs.title: Step 02.22 — Seat the shaft assembly into z_drive_retainer (the shallow half)
Step 02.22 — Seat the shaft assembly into z_drive_retainer (the shallow half)
docs.text:
Step 22 of 44 · Chapter 02 — Z drives, Z idlers, Z rails, deck panel

Do:

  1. Set the retainer inserts down, cradles up.
  2. Lower the shaft assembly so each 625 drops into a cradle, the loop in the pocket.
  3. If one will not seat by hand, do not heat or hammer.

Parts:

  • z_drive_retainer_a or _b ×1, inserts fitted
  • the belted shaft assembly from Step 02.21

Check

All three bearings down in their cradles, the shaft parallel to the retainer's flat face, and the belt loop lying in the pocket.

What you're looking at

Manual p.35: the shaft assembly lowering into z_drive_retainer, the shallow tray half of the housing, 16 mm deep, with six brass inserts in its flat outer face. Its three half-round cradles take the 625 bearings; the deeper z_drive_main clamps them from the other side.

Source: Voron manual p.35

← PreviousStep 02.21 — Fit the 188 mm closed belt loop over the 80T pulley

Next →Step 02.23 — Check the shaft position against the section view

docs.title: Step 02.23 — Check the shaft position against the section view
Step 02.23 — Check the shaft position against the section view
docs.text:
Step 23 of 44 · Chapter 02 — Z drives, Z idlers, Z rails, deck panel

Do: Hold your part next to the isometric and section views. Confirm the 20T pulley is on the same side, the spacer stack sits between the same two bearings, and the shaft ends are flush the same way.

Parts: none.

Check

Your assembly and the drawing are indistinguishable. Fix it now: after the main goes on, six M3×40 have to come back out.

What you're looking at

Manual p.35's section view beside your part. The section is the only place the manual shows which side of the 20T pulley each spacer and bearing belongs on: after the main goes on, six long screws have to come back out to fix it.

Source: Voron manual p.35

← PreviousStep 02.22 — Seat the shaft assembly into z_drive_retainer (the shallow half)

Next →Step 02.24 — Close the drive with z_drive_main and six M3×40

docs.title: Step 02.24 — Close the drive with z_drive_main and six M3×40
Step 02.24 — Close the drive with z_drive_main and six M3×40
docs.text:
Step 24 of 44 · Chapter 02 — Z drives, Z idlers, Z rails, deck panel

Do:

  1. Lower the main over the shaft, counterbores up, halves meeting with no gap.
  2. Drive the six M3×40 SHCS through the counterbores into the retainer's inserts, criss-cross. Snug, then stop.
  3. Every head must sink into a counterbore.

Parts:

  • z_drive_main_a or _b ×1 (side inserts fitted, Step 02.04)
  • M3×40 SHCS ×6

Check

Six heads down in their counterbores, no gap along the joint line, and the shaft still spins freely by hand with the belt on.

What you're looking at

Manual p.36: z_drive_main, the deeper half, closing over the shaft. Its flat face has six counterbored holes, no inserts, and a rectangular window that clears only the 80T rim. The six M3×40 run through both halves and bite the inserts in the retainer's outer face.

Tip

If the shaft binds, a bearing is trapped crooked: back the screws off and reseat.

Source: Voron manual p.36 · Video: Part 1 @3:29:31

← PreviousStep 02.23 — Check the shaft position against the section view

Next →Step 02.25 — Fit the orange baseplate and its captive M5 nut

docs.title: Step 02.25 — Fit the orange baseplate and its captive M5 nut
Step 02.25 — Fit the orange baseplate and its captive M5 nut
docs.text:
Step 25 of 44 · Chapter 02 — Z drives, Z idlers, Z rails, deck panel

Do:

  1. Turn the baseplate plain-face up, drop the M5 hexnut into the pocket.
  2. Flip it straight onto the drive's foot face, pocket down, C-notch over an M5 well.
  3. Secure with three M3×8 SHCS from the counterbored face.

Parts:

  • [a]_z_drive_baseplate_a or _b ×1 (orange)
  • M5 hexnut ×1
  • M3×8 SHCS ×3

Check

Nut trapped behind the plate and unable to spin, plate flat on the drive with no rock, three M3×8 heads sunk in their counterbores.

What you're looking at

Manual p.37: the orange [a]_z_drive_baseplate, with an M5 hex nut dropped into a pocket on its plain face, the face that goes against the drive. That captive nut is the thread the rubber foot's M5×16 screws into.

Tip

Counterbored face up, C-notch opening to your left: the notch is far-left on _a, near-left on _b. Match the baseplate to the letter on its drive.

Source: Voron manual p.37

← PreviousStep 02.24 — Close the drive with z_drive_main and six M3×40

Next →Step 02.26 — Confirm the belt loop is captured

docs.title: Step 02.26 — Confirm the belt loop is captured
Step 02.26 — Confirm the belt loop is captured
docs.text:
Step 26 of 44 · Chapter 02 — Z drives, Z idlers, Z rails, deck panel

Do: Look into the drive through the retainer's window. The closed 188 mm loop must be inside the part, around the 80T pulley, with enough slack hanging out of that window to reach the motor pulley.

Parts: none.

Check

Belt visible inside the drive and free to move. Repeat Steps 02.22–02.26 for the other three drives, two a and two b.

What you're looking at

Manual p.37: the assembled drive with the belt loop visible inside it. The loop leaves the housing through the retainer's rectangular window, the face with the six insert heads, and must hang out far enough to hook over the motor's 16T.

Good stopping point · ~35 min since the last one

all four drives closed: shafts seated, retainers down on six M3×40 each, orange baseplates on with their captive M5 nuts, belt loops captive and free. Each drive is one ~9-minute unit, so if you stop earlier, stop with a drive fully closed and its baseplate on — never with a drive half-closed.

Source: Voron manual p.37

← PreviousStep 02.25 — Fit the orange baseplate and its captive M5 nut

Next →Step 02.27 — Fit the 16T pulley to a Z motor at 10.7 mm

docs.title: Step 02.27 — Fit the 16T pulley to a Z motor at 10.7 mm
Step 02.27 — Fit the 16T pulley to a Z motor at 10.7 mm
docs.text:
Step 27 of 44 · Chapter 02 — Z drives, Z idlers, Z rails, deck panel

Do:

  1. Check the tooth count: the only 16T pulleys in the printer.
  2. Slide it on so motor face to pulley underside is 10.7 mm.
  3. Rotate so a set screw meets the flat; tighten both with threadlocker.

Parts:

  • NEMA17 Z motor LDO-42STH48-2004AC ×1
  • GT2 16T pulley ×1
  • M4×4 set screws ×2

Check

10.7 mm on the caliper, the tooth band level with the 80T it will drive, no slip under hand force.

What you're looking at

Manual p.38: a Z stepper motor with its 16T pulley. The Z motors are the only place in this printer that uses 16T. The 20T pulleys elsewhere look identical, and fitting a 20T here silently changes the gear ratio the firmware assumes. See the glossary.

Tip

when all four are done, physically remove every remaining 16T pulley from the bench so one cannot end up on an A/B motor in Chapter 04. src

Tip

The pulley may sit better flipped, depending on the motor. What matters is where the teeth end up, not which way the boss faces.

Source: Voron manual p.38 · LDO Build Notes (Rev D) · Video: Part 2 @1:15:06

← PreviousStep 02.26 — Confirm the belt loop is captured

Next →Step 02.28 — Bolt the motor to z_motor_mount, watching the cable exit

docs.title: Step 02.28 — Bolt the motor to z_motor_mount, watching the cable exit
Step 02.28 — Bolt the motor to z_motor_mount, watching the cable exit
docs.text:
Step 28 of 44 · Chapter 02 — Z drives, Z idlers, Z rails, deck panel

Do:

  1. Set the motor's round boss in the plate's half-round notch, cable exit oriented as in the graphic.
  2. Fit three M3×8 SHCS through the plate's counterbored holes into the motor.
  3. Build all four: two a mounts, two b.

Parts:

  • z_motor_mount_a or _b ×1
  • M3×8 SHCS ×3

Check

All four cable exits point the same way relative to their mount, the 16T clears the mount, the foot's two M5 clearance holes unobstructed.

What you're looking at

Manual p.39: the motor bolted to z_motor_mount, the L-bracket that stands the motor off the frame. The mounts are mirrored _a / _b, and the two hands put the motor's cable exit on opposite sides. Three screw holes only: the fourth corner is open by design.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: the manual's own stepper wiring instructions do not apply to this kit. Wire the Z steppers per the LDO Rev D wiring guide (Z0 front-left→STEPPER-0, Z1 rear-left→STEPPER-1, Z2 rear-right→STEPPER-2, Z3 front-right→STEPPER-3). Label each motor cable now: in Chapter 10 the four are indistinguishable. src · wiring guide

Tip

Stood on its print face, thick foot arm on your right running toward you: the thin motor plate is the far edge on _a, the near edge on _b.

Good stopping point · ~25 min since the last one

four Z motors carry their 16T pulleys at 10.7 mm and are bolted to their a/b mounts with the cable exits matched. Get every remaining 16T pulley off the bench before you walk away, and leave the motor cables labelled.

Source: Voron manual p.39 · LDO Build Notes (Rev D) · LDO wiring guide § Connecting Steppers · Video: Part 2 @1:19:26

Step 02.29 — Identify Z0 and start there
docs.text:
Step 29 of 44 · Chapter 02 — Z drives, Z idlers, Z rails, deck panel

Do:

  1. Find the front-left corner from the FRONT tape; lay an _a drive and motor assembly beside it.
  2. Dry-fit first: retainer face toward the motor's extrusion, counterbore face outboard over the side rail, 16T in line with the 80T.

Parts:

  • one complete _a drive + one _a motor/mount assembly

Check

An _a drive and motor dry-fitted at front-left: retainer face toward the motor's extrusion, counterbore face outboard over the side rail, baseplate up.

What you're looking at

Manual p.40: the highlighted corner is Z0, front-left. The mirror hand of the printed parts decides which corner an assembly fits, so the drive and motor mount are matched to the corner before a single bolt goes in.

Tip

If the dry-fit only works with the _b parts, the map is reversed. Swap every _a for _b for the rest of the chapter and write that in the build log.

Source: Voron manual p.40 · Voron manual p.41 · Voron-2 CAD Voron_2.4r2_Assembly_STEP.zip @ de7e89d (corner map)

docs.title: Step 02.30 — Pre-load four M5 T-nuts at the Z0 corner
Step 02.30 — Pre-load four M5 T-nuts at the Z0 corner
docs.text:
Step 30 of 44 · Chapter 02 — Z drives, Z idlers, Z rails, deck panel

Do:

  1. Slide four M5 T-nuts into the two extrusions at this corner, two in each.
  2. Two M5×40 go into the side rail; two M5×10 lie along the front or rear rail, 25 mm apart. Z0/Z3 front, Z1/Z2 rear.

Parts:

  • M5 roll-in T-nut ×4 (or the four you pre-loaded at Step 02.11)

Check

Four T-nuts in, two per extrusion, all free to slide, none jammed or dropped inside the extrusion.

What you're looking at

Manual p.41: four M5 roll-in T-nuts loaded into the two bottom extrusions meeting at this corner. They are the threads for everything that bolts down here: two for the drive body's M5×40, two for the motor foot's M5×10. The drive-end one also pins the cam.

Source: Voron manual p.41 · LDO Build Notes (Rev D) · Voron-2 CAD Voron_2.4r2_Assembly_STEP.zip @ de7e89d (which rail takes which bolts)

docs.title: Step 02.31 — Bolt the drive body down with two M5×40
Step 02.31 — Bolt the drive body down with two M5×40
docs.text:
Step 31 of 44 · Chapter 02 — Z drives, Z idlers, Z rails, deck panel

Do:

  1. Set the drive baseplate up, retainer face toward the motor's extrusion, counterbore face outboard.
  2. Drop both M5×40 down the deep wells into the side-rail T-nuts, pull the body hard into the corner, tighten both fully now.

Parts:

  • M5×40 SHCS ×2
  • the completed _a drive

Check

Body hard against both extrusions, both M5×40 tight; the 188 mm loop hanging out of the retainer's window over the motor's extrusion.

What you're looking at

Manual p.41: the finished drive landing in the corner on two long M5×40 that run down the body's two 35 mm wells into the T-nuts. The drive is the fixed half: its two bolts go fully tight now.

Tip

The p.42–43 DON'T TIGHTEN applies to the two M5×10 in the motor foot. Those are the only bolts at this corner that stay loose.

Source: Voron manual p.41

docs.title: Step 02.32 — Slide the motor assembly in at an angle
Step 02.32 — Slide the motor assembly in at an angle
docs.text:
Step 32 of 44 · Chapter 02 — Z drives, Z idlers, Z rails, deck panel

Do:

  1. Hold the motor/mount at an angle, hook the loop over the 16T, slide the foot onto the extrusion beside the drive.
  2. Fit one M5×10 BHCS through the foot hole farthest from the drive and leave it loose.

Parts:

  • M5×10 BHCS ×1
  • the _a motor/mount assembly

Check

Loop squarely in both the 16T and 80T tooth bands, motor foot flat on the extrusion, motor-end screw loose, drive-end foot hole empty.

What you're looking at

Manual p.42: the motor and its mount sliding in beside the drive at an angle, with the hanging belt loop hooked over the 16T on the way in. That angled entry is the only path that gets the loop onto both pulleys.

Source: Voron manual p.42

docs.title: Step 02.33 — Fit the orange belt tensioner, still loose
Step 02.33 — Fit the orange belt tensioner, still loose
docs.text:
Step 33 of 44 · Chapter 02 — Z drives, Z idlers, Z rails, deck panel

Do:

  1. Slide the cam's lobe flat-face-down into the 4 mm pocket under the foot's drive end, hole over the foot's empty hole.
  2. Fit the second M5×10 BHCS through both and leave it loose: a pivot, not a fastener.

Parts:

  • [a]_belt_tensioner_a or _b ×1 (orange)
  • M5×10 BHCS ×1

Check

Tab free to swing about the screw; motor still free to slide along the extrusion; both M5×10 in the foot loose.

What you're looking at

Manual p.43: the orange [a]_belt_tensioner, a cam whose lobe lies in a pocket under the drive end of the motor foot. The lobe is eccentric: swinging the tab from upright to flat pushes the motor foot away and takes up the belt slack.

Tip

Flat face down, round lobe on your left: the upright tab is far-right on _a, near-right on _b. The wrong hand swings away from the motor.

Source: Voron manual p.43 · Video: Part 2 @1:18:50

← PreviousStep 02.32 — Slide the motor assembly in at an angle

docs.title: Step 02.34 — Flip the tensioner latch closed
Step 02.34 — Flip the tensioner latch closed
docs.text:
Step 34 of 44 · Chapter 02 — Z drives, Z idlers, Z rails, deck panel

Do: Swing the tab toward the motor, in the direction of the p.44 arrow, until it lies flat and seats in the notch. The lobe moves the motor foot ~2–3 mm away from the drive body, which must not move.

Parts: none.

Check

Tab flat in the notch and the loop taut: turning the motor shaft by hand spins the 80T with no slip or belt skip.

What you're looking at

Manual p.44: the cam being rotated closed. Closing it is what tensions the belt; the arrow on the page is the direction that pushes the motor foot away from the drive body. The tab ends flat in the notch in the foot's outer edge.

Source: Voron manual p.44 · Voron-2 CAD Voron_2.4r2_Assembly_STEP.zip @ de7e89d (cam throw)

← PreviousStep 02.33 — Fit the orange belt tensioner, still loose

docs.title: Step 02.35 — Tighten the M5 bolts
Step 02.35 — Tighten the M5 bolts
docs.text:
Step 35 of 44 · Chapter 02 — Z drives, Z idlers, Z rails, deck panel

Do: Only now, with the cam closed, tighten the two M5×10 in the motor foot; the drive-end one clamps the cam as well. Then confirm the two M5×40 in the drive body have not moved.

Parts:

  • none — the four M5 bolts already fitted

Check

All four bolts tight. Nothing has moved. The belt is still correctly seated in both pulleys.

What you're looking at

Manual p.45: the two M5×10 in the motor foot, the motor-end one and the drive-end one through the cam. They are tightened only now, with the cam closed, so the motor position the cam set is what gets locked in.

Source: Voron manual p.45 · Video: Part 2 @1:18:48

Step 02.36 — Fit the rubber foot
docs.text:
Step 36 of 44 · Chapter 02 — Z drives, Z idlers, Z rails, deck panel

Do: With the printer still upside down, set a rubber foot on the baseplate at this corner and fix it with one M5×16 BHCS through the foot into the M5 nut you dropped into the baseplate at Step 02.25.

Parts:

  • Rubber foot 38×19 mm ×1
  • M5×16 BHCS ×1

Check

Foot square to the corner and firmly attached.

What you're looking at

Manual p.45: one of the printer's four rubber feet, bolted to the corner while the machine is still upside down and the underside is reachable. Its M5×16 threads into the nut captive in the orange baseplate.

Source: Voron manual p.45 · Video: Part 1 @3:34:45

Step 02.37 — Check the drive did not shift when the tensioner closed
docs.text:
Step 37 of 44 · Chapter 02 — Z drives, Z idlers, Z rails, deck panel

Do: Sight down the section view on the page and compare. The drive body must still sit hard against the corner and square to both extrusions.

Parts: none.

Check

No skew, no gap at the corner, belt still fully on both pulleys. If the drive moved, undo the bolts, realign, and redo Steps 02.34–02.35.

What you're looking at

Manual p.46: a section through the finished corner. Closing the cam pushes the motor away from the drive body, and the reaction shoves the body. If it was not seated square when its M5×40 went tight it moves, and the section is how you tell.

Good stopping point · ~30 min since the last one

the Z0 corner is complete: drive body on its two M5×40, motor slid in, cam closed, both M5×10 tight, rubber foot on, and the p.46 section check passed. One corner is a self-contained unit and this is the natural stop.

Source: Voron manual p.46

Step 02.38 — Build and fit the other three Z drives
docs.text:
Step 38 of 44 · Chapter 02 — Z drives, Z idlers, Z rails, deck panel

Do:

  1. Repeat Steps 02.29–02.37 at Z2 rear-right with the other _a set, then at Z1 rear-left and Z3 front-right with the _b parts: diagonal corners share a hand.
  2. Label each motor's cable Z0/Z1/Z2/Z3 by its physical corner.

Parts:

  • the remaining three drives, motors, mounts, tensioners, feet and their hardware

Check

Four drives, feet, tensioned belts, closed cams and labelled cables. Deck captured by its eight clips, the frame back upright on its feet without rocking.

What you're looking at

Manual p.47: all four corners done. Two corners take the _a hand of every printed part, Z0 and Z2, and two take _b, Z1 and Z3. The cable labels go on now because in Ch 10 four identical black stepper cables arrive at the mainboard together.

Good stopping point · ~55 min since the last one

since the last pause, in three ~18-min corners — Z1, Z2 and Z3 built and fitted the same way. Stop after any corner whose four M5 bolts are tight, tensioner closed and foot fitted; never with a cam open and the motor free to slide. All four cables labelled Z0–Z3 by physical corner.

Source: Voron manual p.47 · LDO wiring guide § Connecting Steppers · Video: Part 2 @0:02:14

Step 02.39 — Assemble a Z idler cage
docs.text:
Step 39 of 44 · Chapter 02 — Z drives, Z idlers, Z rails, deck panel

Do: Drop the M3 hexnut into the bracket's pocket. Slide the orange tensioner in and run the M3×16 SHCS up through it into the nut. Leave it a couple of turns short of tight.

Parts:

  • z_tensioner_bracket_a or _b ×1
  • [a]_z_tensioner_9mm ×1 (orange)
  • M3×16 SHCS ×1
  • M3 hexnut ×1

Check

Nut captive, screw engaged, tensioner sliding smoothly in the bracket with no side play.

What you're looking at

Manual p.48: the Z idler, the assembly at the top corner that turns the long Z belt back down. z_tensioner_bracket is the printed cage that bolts to the frame; the orange [a]_z_tensioner_9mm slides inside it on the screw you tension the Z belt with in Ch 06.

Tip

In plan, print face down, the slider channel's open side toward you and the two oval slots left–right: tab on the left = _a, on the right = _b.

Source: Voron manual p.48 · Video: Part 2 @1:37:11

docs.title: Step 02.40 — Fit the 20T idler on its M5×30 axle
Step 02.40 — Fit the 20T idler on its M5×30 axle
docs.text:
Step 40 of 44 · Chapter 02 — Z drives, Z idlers, Z rails, deck panel

Do: Drive the M5×30 BHCS through the slider's fork with the 20T 9 mm idler between the arms. It cuts its own thread in the Ø5 holes, so keep it square. Build all four, two a brackets and two b.

Parts:

  • GT2 20T 9 mm idler ×1
  • M5×30 BHCS ×1

Check

Idler spins freely on the axle with no axial slop, and its tooth band sits centred in the fork. Four idlers built.

What you're looking at

Manual p.48: a 20T idler dropped into the fork of the orange tensioner on an M5×30 screw used as its axle. An idler is a pulley that redirects a belt without driving it. See the glossary. It has to spin freely and stay in plane.

Good stopping point · ~20 min since the last one

four idler cages assembled with their captive M3 nuts and 20T idlers on M5×30 axles, tensioner screws left deliberately short of tight. Nothing is mounted to the frame yet.

Source: Voron manual p.48

Step 02.41 — Pre-load two M5 T-nuts at a top corner

Two T-nuts in the side face, under the top rail, free to slide.

What you're looking at

Idler pulley and the drive's 20T below it lie in the same vertical plane, and the bracket sits hard against both faces of the corner.

What you're looking at

docs.title: Checkpoint 02
docs.text: Ch 02Checkpoint

docs.title: Checkpoint 02
docs.text:
Checkpoint · Chapter 02 — Z drives, Z idlers, Z rails, deck panel

What you should have now — The four Z drive units under the frame, the four idler cages above them, the Z rails and carriages on the verticals, and the deck panel. CAD rails are MGN9 300 mm; your 350 kit uses 400 mm rails, and the deck panel is the 350 one.
  • All four Z rails run their full travel with no notch, tight spot or grinding; every carriage is taped or stoppered.
  • Rail surfaces are clean and dry and grease is inside the carriages only — carried over from Ch 00 Steps 00.18–00.21 and re-confirmed at Step 02.05.
  • All four rails are centred on their extrusions, each facing the rail on its own side of the machine (front-left ↔ rear-left, front-right ↔ rear-right), and share the same 3 mm bottom gap and the same nine-hole pattern (holes 2–18, no end holes).
  • Deck panel notch is at the back; panel sits inside the frame opening on the bed extrusions, captured by eight clip ledges, no rock; four M5 T-nuts aligned under the four deck holes and left unbolted for Ch 09 Step 09.5.
  • _a parts at Z0 and Z2, _b at Z1 and Z3 (or the reverse if the Step 02.29 dry-fit said so — written in the build log), and each idler the same hand as the drive below it.
  • Measured deck-panel thickness is written down and the fitted deck supports (8 off) match it.
  • Every 20T drive pulley sits 33 mm along its shaft; every 16T motor pulley sits 10.7 mm off the motor face.
  • All 24 M4×4 set screws are tight, threadlocked, and at least one per pulley lands on the shaft flat.
  • Four M5 precision spacers per drive (16 total) — spacers, not shims.
  • Each Z drive shaft turns freely by hand through the belt, with no belt skip and no bearing rumble.
  • All four tensioner cams are closed and no drive shifted when its cam closed (p.46 check).
  • Four rubber feet fitted; the printer stands on all four without rocking on the reference surface.
  • Each Z idler faces the same way as the pulley in the drive below it and is pressed hard into its corner.
  • Four motor cables labelled Z0 / Z1 / Z2 / Z3 by physical corner.

← PreviousStep 02.44 — Close the chapter

Next →Ch 03 — before you start

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Bolting a rail on dry. Once a rail is on an extrusion you cannot use the flip-and-pack method, and a dry MGN9 wears out. Rails off again, or a compromised axis — check at Step 02.05 that Ch 00 really did all four (§5.2 W9).
  • Missing a heat-set insert before the drive is closed. Six M3×40 have to come out and the shaft assembly has to be lifted to reach it. Do the insert pass as a batch, count the pockets, and only then start assembling (§5.2 W3).
  • A 20T pulley on a Z motor. The 16T and 20T look nearly identical. The machine will home and move and be silently wrong on every Z dimension, because gear_ratio: 80:16 is baked into the config. Count teeth, then clear the 16T pulleys off the bench (p.38).
  • Skipping the deck supports "until the panels chapter". The deck cannot be lifted once the gantry and electronics are in — the frame has to come partly apart. LDO puts this at p.29–30 for a reason (§5.2 W4).
  • Tightening rail screws from one end. The rail bows and the carriage develops a tight spot that no amount of greasing fixes. Always centre-outward (p.24).
  • Set screws finger-tight or off the flat. They loosen under Z load, the belt slips, and the gantry drops out of level. Threadlocker on all of them, one on the flat, tightened with a proper hex driver (p.32, §5.2 W12).
  • Closing a drive with the halves upside down. Screws started from above into the retainer's visible brass inserts thread only into that insert, clamp nothing, and pull the insert out of its boss. The M3×40 heads sink into the main's counterbores; the retainer's inserts are at the bottom of the stack (Step 02.24).
  • The wrong hand at a corner. It bolts on fine and shows up in Ch 06 when the 20T is not under its idler. Diagonals share a hand (Step 02.02); dry-fit the first unit (Step 02.29).
  • M5×40 through the motor foot. The foot's holes are 9 mm deep M5×10 holes; a 40 mm screw bottoms in the slot and jacks the T-nut. The long screws go down the drive body's wells (Step 02.31); the motor foot takes the two M5×10, both left loose until the cam is closed (Steps 02.32–02.33).
  • Cam at the wrong end of the foot. The tensioner lives under the drive end of the motor foot, on the drive-end screw; at the motor end it has nothing to push against and the loop never comes taut (p.43, Step 02.33).
  • Bolting the deck down here. The four M5×10 go in with the DIN rails in Ch 09 Step 09.5. Fitting them now means undoing them again — and it double-counts the same four bolts in two chapters' hardware totals.

docs.title: Before you start Chapter 02
docs.text:
Before you start · Chapter 02 — Z drives, Z idlers, Z rails, deck panel

Builds the four Z drive units, the four Z idlers, the four Z linear rails and the deck panel. When this chapter closes, the frame has a floor, feet, and every part of the Z motion system except the belts and the Z joints — the gantry has somewhere to hang from.

What you're building in this chapter: the machinery that raises and lowers the gantry, one corner at a time. A Z drive is the gearbox in a bottom corner: a printed housing holding three bearings and a shaft, with a big 80-tooth pulley the motor drives through a short closed belt and a 20-tooth pulley the long Z belt runs over — 80:16 of reduction, which is what makes Z fine enough to print with. The housing is two printed halves: a shallow retainer tray the shaft and its bearings drop into, and the deeper main body that closes over them on six long screws and carries the two M5×40 that bolt the drive to the frame. An orange baseplate bolts across the drive's foot face and holds the nut the rubber foot screws into, and an orange cam tensioner pushes the motor along its extrusion to pull the short belt tight. Directly above each drive, at the top corner, a Z idler carries a free-spinning pulley that turns the long belt back down again; its orange slider is the adjuster you tension that belt with in Ch 06 (final tension is set in Ch 14). Between them run the four Z linear rails on the vertical extrusions, the tracks the gantry's corners actually ride on. Last comes the deck panel, the acrylic floor that divides the electronics bay underneath from the print chamber above — it goes in now because once the gantry and the wiring are in, it cannot be lifted out again. Four corners, all identical in function, built from mirrored _a and _b printed parts — diagonal corners share a hand (the map is at Step 02.02).

Time: 4.25–6.25 h hands-on, first build (survey §7.2, less the ~45 min of rail cleaning and greasing, which is done once for all seven rails in Ch 00 Steps 00.18–00.21).

Sessions: 11 × ~30 min — the Pause: lines below break the chapter into 11 segments; every minute figure is a first-build estimate.

Prerequisites:

  • Chapter 01 complete: frame assembled, squared, bed extrusions positioned 65 mm each side of the printer centreline (130 mm clear gap between their inner faces, 150 mm centre-to-centre) per Ch 01 Step 01.19, and the squareness re-checked after the final torque pass.
  • Print batch B00 (Calibration & jigs) — MGN9_rail_guide_x2, pulley_jig.
  • Print batch B01 (Z drive assemblies) — drive bodies, retainers, motor mounts, Z-tensioner brackets, deck supports.
  • Print batch B02 (Accent parts, orange) plates P1 and P3 — the five [a]_ parts below.
  • Steps 02.27–02.28 (16T pulleys, motors onto their mounts) need only B01-P2 and the Motor Kit — do them while B01-P1 is still printing if you like, and label the motor cables then.
  • Chapter 00 complete: all seven rails cleaned, flip-and-packed with grease, wiped and labelled (Steps 00.18–00.21). The four marked Z0–Z3 are used here.
  • Kit boxes open: Motion, Linear Rail Kit, Motor Kit, the M3/M5 fastener bags.

Tools

  • Hex drivers 1.5 / 2 / 2.5 / 3 / 4 mm — good quality, not ball-end for set screws (p.32).
  • Temperature-controlled soldering iron + the LDO brass M3 heat-set tip.
  • Digital caliper (deck-panel thickness gate; 33 mm and 10.7 mm pulley dimensions).
  • Printed jigs: MGN9_rail_guide_x2 ×2, pulley_jig ×1.
  • Masking tape (carriage retention, rail hole marking, the FRONT label) and a marker. The 3 mm hex key doubles as the rail-gap feeler (Step 02.06).

Consumables: Loctite 243 for any set screw that did not arrive with threadlocker pre-applied. (IPA, grease, soak tray, syringe and cloth were the Ch 00 rail-prep kit — nothing here needs them unless a rail was missed.)

Printed parts — all ASA. Black = main colour, Orange = accent ([a]_ prefix).

Parts arrive in the bins named below (see the bin map in print/README.md#bins); check the bin label's list before you start.

Looks like STL (Voron-2 STLs/, branch Voron2.4) Bin Qty Colour Z_Drive/z_drive_main_a_x2.stl 02-Z0 · 02-Z2 2 Black Z_Drive/z_drive_main_b_x2.stl 02-Z1 · 02-Z3 2 Black Z_Drive/z_drive_retainer_a_x2.stl 02-Z0 · 02-Z2 2 Black Z_Drive/z_drive_retainer_b_x2.stl 02-Z1 · 02-Z3 2 Black Z_Drive/z_motor_mount_a_x2.stl 02-Z0 · 02-Z2 2 Black Z_Drive/z_motor_mount_b_x2.stl 02-Z1 · 02-Z3 2 Black Z_Drive/[a]_z_drive_baseplate_a_x2.stl 02-Z0 · 02-Z2 2 Orange Z_Drive/[a]_z_drive_baseplate_b_x2.stl 02-Z1 · 02-Z3 2 Orange Z_Drive/[a]_belt_tensioner_a_x2.stl 02-Z0 · 02-Z2 2 Orange Z_Drive/[a]_belt_tensioner_b_x2.stl 02-Z1 · 02-Z3 2 Orange Z_Idlers/z_tensioner_bracket_a_x2.stl 02-Z0 · 02-Z2 2 Black Z_Idlers/z_tensioner_bracket_b_x2.stl 02-Z1 · 02-Z3 2 Black Z_Idlers/[a]_z_tensioner_9mm_x4.stl 02-Z0 · 02-Z1 · 02-Z2 · 02-Z3 4 Orange Panel_Mounting/deck_support_3mm_x8.stl 02-deck 8 Black — default (Rev D 350 BOM), see Step 02.12 no render — same clip, slotted for a 4 mm panel Panel_Mounting/deck_support_4mm_x8.stl — 8 Black — fallback if the panel measures 4 mm Tools/MGN9_rail_guide_x2.stl (jig, not consumed) 00-jigs 2 Black Tools/pulley_jig.stl (jig, not consumed) 00-jigs 1 Black LDO STLs/z_rail_stop_x4.stl (optional) 06-Z-joints 4 Black — batch B05, which prints after this chapter in the timeline

The _xN suffix is the quantity you need, not the number of copies in the file — each STL contains one part. _a and _b are mirrored: two drives use the a set, two use the b set.

Hardware — chapter totals.

Fastener / part Qty M3×8 SHCS 24 (drives) + 36 (Z rails — 9 per rail, Step 02.06) M3×16 SHCS 4 M3×40 SHCS 24 M3 hexnut 4 M3 roll-in T-nut, 2020 36 (one per Z-rail screw) M3×5×4 brass heat-set insert 36 (Step 02.04) + up to 7 on the practice coupon (Step 02.03) M5×10 BHCS 8 (drives) M5×16 BHCS 4 M5×30 BHCS 12 (idlers: 2 mounting + 1 axle each) M5×40 SHCS 8 M5 hexnut 4 M5 roll-in T-nut, 2020 28 (16 drives + 8 idlers + 4 deck) M5 precision spacer, 1 mm (kit substitute for "M5 Shim") 16 M4×4 set screw, pre-applied threadlocker 24 (2 each on 4× 20T, 4× 80T, 4× 16T) 625-2RS bearing 12 GT2 80T pulley, 5 mm ID 4 GT2 20T 9 mm pulley, 5 mm ID 4 GT2 16T pulley, 5 mm ID 6 mm W 4 GT2 20T 9 mm idler, 5 mm ID 4 5×60 mm shaft 4 Gates 2GT closed loop, 6 mm × 188 mm 4 NEMA17 Z motor, LDO-42STH48-2004AC(VRN) 4 MGN9H 400 mm rail, LDO-SLR9H-400Z0 4 Rubber foot, 38×19 mm 4 Deck panel, acrylic black 469×469 1

Quantities cross-checked against the LDO Rev D 350 BOM (350_BOM/Rev_D); the LDO kit ships 6× MGN9H-400 and 1× MGN12H-400 — four of the MGN9s are yours here, the other two are the gantry Y rails in Chapter 05.

Read first

  • The rails were cleaned and greased in Ch 00, not here. Flip-and-pack needs access to the back of the rail, which you lose the moment it is bolted to an extrusion — so if any of Z0–Z3 was missed, fix it before Step 02.06, not after (rail grease guide; survey §4.4 #5, §5.2 W9).
  • The Z motors are the only place in the whole printer that uses 16T pulleys. They look almost identical to the 20T. Get them off the bench when this chapter is done (p.38; survey §4.4 #7).
  • Every set screw gets threadlocker and must land on the flat/D-cut of the shaft. Loose set screws are the single most reported failure on this machine (p.32; §5.2 W12).
  • Two corners take _a parts, two take _b, and diagonal corners share a hand — _a at Z0 (front-left) and Z2 (rear-right), _b at Z1 (rear-left) and Z3 (front-right); map at Step 02.02, dry-fit at Step 02.29. A wrong-hand drive bolts on fine and is only found in Ch 06 when the Z belt goes on and the 20T is not under its idler.
  • Heat-set inserts go into the drive parts before the drive is assembled. A missed insert means taking a finished drive back apart (§4.4 #4, §5.2 W3).
  • The deck panel and its supports go in now, at p.28–30 — not later with the panels. Retro-fitting the deck means pulling the frame apart (LDO note p.29–30; §5.2 W4).
  • Nothing in this chapter touches a probe or an endstop. The Rev D+ nozzle probe and the Omron inductive probe belong to Chapters 08–09; leave both bagged.

docs.title: Step 03.1 — Unpack the plate and read the end state
Step 03.1 — Unpack the plate and read the end state
docs.text:
Step 1 of 20 · Chapter 03 — Build plate

Do: Take the plate out flat, never on edge; a dropped corner dents a 10 mm cast slab. Lay it on a clean towel. It ends up on the two bed extrusions above the deck panel, cables through the deck.

Parts:

  • build plate ×1, magnetic pad ×1, spring steel flex plate ×1

Check

Three cables leave the plate at the back-centre edge, with the M4×6 PE screw beside them. Washer type (verify on bench).

What you're looking at

Manual p.52: the finished bed and its three parts. The build plate is a 355 × 355 × 10 mm cast aluminium slab with the AC heater pad bonded underneath. The magnetic pad laminates on top. The flex plate is the removable spring-steel print surface.

Source: Voron manual p.52 · LDO 350 Rev D BOM · Video: Part 1 @0:44:56

← PreviousCh 03 — before you start

Next →Step 03.2 — Work out which side is which

docs.title: Step 03.10 — Trim the magnet at the four bolt holes
Step 03.10 — Trim the magnet at the four bolt holes
docs.text:
Step 10 of 20 · Chapter 03 — Build plate

Do:

  1. Press down to find the four counterbored holes as dimples.
  2. Cut the magnet away over each one, following the bore, in light repeated passes.
  3. Do not gouge the aluminium; a burr stops the bolt head sitting flush.

Parts:

  • Magnetic pad (applied), sharp craft knife

Check

All four bores fully open. Test each with an M3×20 SHCS and the hex key before you go anywhere near the frame.

What you're looking at

The laminated magnet with four dimples where the plate's counterbored corner holes sit underneath. The mounting bolts pass through those holes and a hex key has to reach their heads, so the magnet is cut away over each one.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: LDO's note at p.54 exists because the magnet gets applied here and the bolts do not go in until p.59. Trimming now costs two minutes; discovering it at p.59 costs the magnet (survey §5.2 W6). src

Good stopping point · ~30 min since the last one

the top face is cleaned, the magnet is rolled down bubble-free and all four bolt holes are cut clear through it and test-fitted with an M3×20 and a hex key. The lamination is finished, so nothing is mid-adhesive. Lay the plate flat, magnet up, and cover it.

Source: Voron manual p.54 · LDO Build Notes (Rev D)

← PreviousStep 03.9 — Apply the magnet sheet

Next →Step 03.11 — Verify the bed extrusion position

docs.title: Step 03.11 — Verify the bed extrusion position
Step 03.11 — Verify the bed extrusion position
docs.text:
Step 11 of 20 · Chapter 03 — Build plate

Do:

  1. With the printer upright, measure between the facing inner faces of the two bed extrusions: 130 mm clear.
  2. Centre that gap, 65 mm from the centreline to each inner face.
  3. Measure at both ends; both must match.

Parts:

  • none — measurement only

Check

130 mm clear gap between the facing inner faces, so 150 mm centre-to-centre, 65 mm from the centreline to each, the same at both ends.

What you're looking at

Manual p.58: the front elevation of the frame with the bed extrusions in it. Those two extrusions carry the plate's four mounting points, so you re-check Ch 01's placement here. The bare 25 on the verticals is unidentified and nothing depends on it.

Source: Voron manual p.58 · Voron manual p.20

← PreviousStep 03.10 — Trim the magnet at the four bolt holes

Next →Step 03.12 — Load the four M3 T-nuts

docs.title: Step 03.12 — Load the four M3 T-nuts
Step 03.12 — Load the four M3 T-nuts
docs.text:
Step 12 of 20 · Chapter 03 — Build plate

Do: Roll two T-nuts into the top slot of each bed extrusion, one toward each end, and position them roughly under where the plate's corner holes will land. Leave them loose enough to slide.

Parts:

  • M3 roll-in T-nut, 2020 ×4 (two per bed extrusion)

Check

Four T-nuts, all in the top slot, all rotated so their threads face up and they cannot fall out.

What you're looking at

Manual p.58: four M3 roll-in T-nuts in the top slots of the bed extrusions, two per extrusion. Each is the thread one corner bolt picks up.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: extrusion and roll-in T-nut tolerances on this kit are tight. Test-fit each nut and, if a slot is stiff, pick the extrusion face that accepts it best — do not force one and gall the slot. src

Source: Voron manual p.58 · LDO Build Notes (Rev D)

← PreviousStep 03.11 — Verify the bed extrusion position

Next →Step 03.13 — Fit the four thumb nuts as spacers

docs.title: Step 03.13 — Fit the four thumb nuts as spacers
Step 03.13 — Fit the four thumb nuts as spacers
docs.text:
Step 13 of 20 · Chapter 03 — Build plate

Do: Stand one M4 thumb nut over each T-nut, knurl up, bore concentric with the T-nut thread. Do not thread anything into the thumb nut; the M3 bolt passes straight through its bore.

Parts:

  • M4 knurled thumb nut ×4

Check

Four thumb nuts standing on the extrusions, none tipped, each aligned with the T-nut under it and all four the same height.

What you're looking at

Manual p.58: four knurled thumb nuts, used as spacers rather than nuts. They hold the plate a fixed height above the extrusion; the bolt passes through the thumb nut's bore into the T-nut below. Any substitute must be the same length and heat-resistant.

Source: Voron manual p.58

← PreviousStep 03.12 — Load the four M3 T-nuts

Next →Step 03.14 — Lower the plate on and feed the cables through the deck

docs.title: Step 03.14 — Lower the plate on and feed the cables through the deck
Step 03.14 — Lower the plate on and feed the cables through the deck
docs.text:
Step 14 of 20 · Chapter 03 — Build plate

Do:

  1. Two hands, plate flat, magnet up, cables at the back.
  2. Feed the two AC leads and the thermistor cable down through the deck opening.
  3. Lower the plate onto the four thumb nuts, cables clear of its edge.

Parts:

  • build plate assembly

Check

Plate rests on all four thumb nuts, none knocked over. All three cables hang free below the deck with slack, none trapped.

What you're looking at

Manual p.60: the plate coming down onto its four spacers, cables first. The three cables have to go through the deck opening before the plate lands; afterwards you cannot feed them through without lifting it again.

Source: Voron manual p.60 · Video: Part 2 @1:36:04

← PreviousStep 03.13 — Fit the four thumb nuts as spacers

Next →Step 03.15 — Start the four bolts

docs.title: Step 03.15 — Start the four bolts
Step 03.15 — Start the four bolts
docs.text:
Step 15 of 20 · Chapter 03 — Build plate

Do:

  1. Start an M3×20 SHCS by hand through each trimmed corner hole and thumb nut into the T-nut below.
  2. Nudge a T-nut if a bolt misses the thread.
  3. Run all four down only until they just take up.

Parts:

  • M3×20 SHCS ×4

Check

All four bolts engaged and turning freely, plate still sitting flat on the spacers, no bolt cross-threaded.

What you're looking at

Manual p.59: the four M3×20 bolts. They are longer than the official manual's M3×16 because this plate is 10 mm thick and sits on a spacer. Start them by hand so the T-nuts can still slide to meet each hole.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: M3×20 SHCS, not the manual's M3×16. This plate is 10 mm and the spacer stack is taller, so an M3×16 will not reach enough thread. src

Source: Voron manual p.59 · LDO Build Notes (Rev D)

docs.title: Step 03.16 — Set the 38 mm front offset and centre the plate
Step 03.16 — Set the 38 mm front offset and centre the plate
docs.text:
Step 16 of 20 · Chapter 03 — Build plate

Do:

  1. With the bolts loose, slide the plate until its front edge sits 38 mm behind the frame's front edge.
  2. Split the left and right gaps evenly, then re-check the 38 mm.
  3. Run a finger round the perimeter.

Parts:

  • steel rule / caliper

Check

38 mm at both front corners, left and right gaps equal, nothing touching a vertical extrusion or a Z rail. No tolerance is specified.

What you're looking at

Manual p.60: the plate's position in plan. The 38 mm setback puts the plate where the toolhead can reach it. Equal side gaps keep it clear of the vertical extrusions and Z rails, tight for a 355 mm plate in a 350 mm machine.

Source: Voron manual p.60

← PreviousStep 03.15 — Start the four bolts

Next →Step 03.17 — Tighten one bolt only

docs.title: Step 03.17 — Tighten one bolt only
Step 03.17 — Tighten one bolt only
docs.text:
Step 17 of 20 · Chapter 03 — Build plate

Do:

  1. Tighten one bolt fully, at a front corner clear of the cable exit.
  2. Leave the other three slightly loose. They locate the plate, not clamp it.
  3. Torque is not specified: snug by hand feel, no torque driver.

Parts:

  • the four M3×20 SHCS already fitted

Check

One bolt tight, the other three turnable with a fingertip on the hex key. A free corner gives slightly and returns.

What you're looking at

Manual p.59 and its DON'T TIGHTEN rule. One bolt locates the plate; the other three stay loose so the aluminium can grow as it heats. Clamped at all four corners and taken to 110 °C, a plate this size buckles for good.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: none — the manual's DON'T TIGHTEN rule stands unchanged (p.59). Aluminium at 110 °C grows against a steel-bolted frame; three loose bolts are what lets it grow.

Good stopping point · ~35 min since the last one

the plate is on its four thumb-nut spacers, set 38 mm behind the frame's front edge and centred, one bolt tight and three deliberately loose, cables fed through the deck. This is the natural stop: the plate is bolted and the assembly is stable. Do not tighten the other three bolts.

Source: Voron manual p.59

← PreviousStep 03.16 — Set the 38 mm front offset and centre the plate

Next →Step 03.18 — Verify the plate floats level

docs.title: Step 03.18 — Verify the plate floats level
Step 03.18 — Verify the plate floats level
docs.text:
Step 18 of 20 · Chapter 03 — Build plate

Do:

  1. Measure the gap between extrusion top and plate underside at each bolt.
  2. Sight along the plate at eye level, front and side.
  3. A short corner means an unrolled T-nut, a tipped thumb nut or a tight bolt.

Parts:

  • caliper

Check

All four gaps equal to the thumb-nut height and to each other. Press each corner in turn: no rock, no click.

What you're looking at

The four corners and a caliper. The plate rides on four bolts above the two bed extrusions; the gap under each bolt is what you measure, and all four should match. A short corner is a permanent tilt every bed mesh has to fight.

Tip

do not level the plate to the gantry mechanically. Quad gantry level does that in software in Ch 13; this step only proves the plate floats evenly.

Tip

The CAD bed is the 10 in (254 mm) MIC6 plate on 370 mm bed extrusions (250). Yours is the 350 plate on the 350 frame: four bolts, four gaps.

Source: Voron manual p.59 · Voron manual p.58 · CAD: Voron 2.4r2 STEP @ de7e89d

← PreviousStep 03.17 — Tighten one bolt only

Next →Step 03.19 — Dress the bed harness below deck

docs.title: Step 03.19 — Dress the bed harness below deck
Step 03.19 — Dress the bed harness below deck
docs.text:
Step 19 of 20 · Chapter 03 — Build plate

Do:

  1. Below the deck, separate the two AC leads from the thermistor cable.
  2. Lay them toward the electronics bay, generous slack at the plate end.
  3. Keep them off the deck opening's sharp edge and off the bed extrusions.

Parts:

  • none — no zip ties yet

Check

Slack loop at the plate; no cable under tension; no cable touching a cut edge; the thermal fuse's legs undisturbed. Nothing tied down.

What you're looking at

Manual p.60: the three bed cables below the deck, loose. Nothing is terminated in this chapter. The AC pair goes to the relay and the WAGO bus, the thermistor to a splicer PCB, all in Ch 10.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: do not zip-tie or terminate anything yet. The bed harness is a breakout design specifically so the plate can be removed from the top of the deck panel later; final routing, the WAGO terminals, the 2×2 XH splicer and the Omron SSR are all Ch 10. src

Source: Voron manual p.60 · LDO wiring guide § Wiring the Bed Heater

← PreviousStep 03.18 — Verify the plate floats level

docs.title: Step 03.2 — Work out which side is which
Step 03.2 — Work out which side is which
docs.text:
Step 2 of 20 · Chapter 03 — Build plate

Do:

  1. Find the four corner mounting holes. The counterbored face is the top.
  2. The face carrying the heater, thermal fuse and PE screw holes is the bottom.
  3. Mark the back edge, where the cables leave, with masking tape.

Parts:

  • build plate

Check

Drop an M3×20 SHCS into a corner hole from the top; the head sinks into the bore. From the other side it stands proud.

What you're looking at

Manual p.53: the plate's two faces. The top is the one whose four corner holes are counterbored, a pocket that lets the bolt head sit below the surface. The bottom carries the heater, the thermal fuse and the earth screw.

Source: Voron manual p.53

← PreviousStep 03.1 — Unpack the plate and read the end state

Next →Step 03.3 — Strip the protective film

docs.title: Step 03.20 — Fit the flex plate, then cover the bed
Step 03.20 — Fit the flex plate, then cover the bed
docs.text:
Step 20 of 20 · Chapter 03 — Build plate

Do:

  1. Drop the spring steel flex plate onto the magnet, coated side up, square to the edges. No fasteners.
  2. Take it straight back off and into its sleeve.
  3. Lay cardboard over the magnet for the next six chapters.

Parts:

  • Spring Steel Flex Plate 2.4-350 ×1

Check

Flex plate sits flat with no rocking and does not overhang the magnet on any side. Bed covered.

What you're looking at

Manual p.61: the flex plate, the removable spring-steel print surface that clicks onto the magnet. It goes on once to prove it sits flat, then straight back in its sleeve; the magnet is not something you can resurface.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: the flex plate is an LDO kit item; the official manual's PRINT BED section ends at p.60 and p.61 carries no build content. src

Good stopping point · ~20 min since the last one

the four-corner gap check is done, the bed harness is dressed loose below deck with nothing tied or terminated, and the flex plate has been test-fitted, removed and the bed covered with cardboard. Work through Checkpoint 03; the cover stays on for the next six chapters.

Source: Voron manual p.61 · LDO 350 Rev D BOM

← PreviousStep 03.19 — Dress the bed harness below deck

Next →Checkpoint 03

docs.title: Step 03.3 — Strip the protective film
Step 03.3 — Strip the protective film
docs.text:
Step 3 of 20 · Chapter 03 — Build plate

Do: Peel the blue/clear protective film off the top face and bin it. Work from one corner; do not use a metal tool on the ground surface.

Parts:

  • build plate

Check

No film left in the counterbores or under the edges. The ground surface is bare metal, matte, with visible Blanchard swirl.

What you're looking at

Manual p.54: the ground top face under its protective film. The face is Blanchard-ground, the swirl pattern you will see. The film has to come off before the magnet; adhesive will not bond through it.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: the manual never mentions the film — LDO adds this. Remove it now; the magnet will not bond through it. src

Source: Voron manual p.54 · LDO Build Notes (Rev D)

docs.title: Step 03.4 — Verify the heater pad (do not apply one)
Step 03.4 — Verify the heater pad (do not apply one)
docs.text:
Step 4 of 20 · Chapter 03 — Build plate

Do:

  1. Turn the plate bottom-up.
  2. Confirm the AC heatpad is flat and centred: no lifted corner, wrinkle or trapped air.
  3. Confirm every pad screw is present. Do not tighten them, add adhesive or re-press a lifted edge.

Parts: none.

Check

Pad flat and centred; every pad screw present and untouched, head type (verify on bench); nothing peeling at the cable exit. No bubble size specified.

What you're looking at

Manual p.55 shows the official manual applying a heater pad, a page you skip. The LDO photo beside it is your plate from below: the silicone AC pad bonded and screwed down, the thermal-fuse patch, the cable exit. Compare layout, not ratings.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: SKIP manual p.55 entirely — the heater pad is pre-applied on Rev C and later kits. This step is inspection only. If the pad is genuinely lifting, stop and raise it in #ldo_motors before you bolt the plate in. src · wiring guide § Wiring the Bed Heater

Source: Voron manual p.55 · LDO Build Notes (Rev D) · LDO wiring guide § Wiring the Bed Heater · image: LDO build_plate_bottom_view.jpg

Step 03.5 — Verify the thermal fuse (do not fit one)
docs.text:
Step 5 of 20 · Chapter 03 — Build plate

Do:

  1. Find the 125 °C thermal fuse on the bottom face by the cable exit.
  2. Confirm its body is pressed flat to the aluminium, its single screw and washer tight.
  3. It is wired in-line with one heater lead.

Parts:

  • none. The manual's M3×12 SHCS and M3 washer stay in the bag

Check

Fuse flat to the plate, screw tight, no strain on either leg of the fuse where it joins the heater wire.

What you're looking at

Manual p.56, the fuse installation you skip. The thermal fuse is a one-shot cut-out that opens permanently at 125 °C, wired in series with one heater lead, so a runaway heater loses supply. It works only pressed flat against the aluminium. See the glossary.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: SKIP manual p.56 entirely — the fuse is pre-installed. Inspect only. src

Source: Voron manual p.56 · LDO Build Notes (Rev D)

← PreviousStep 03.4 — Verify the heater pad (do not apply one)

Next →Step 03.6 — Verify the PE screw and identify the three cables

docs.title: Step 03.6 — Verify the PE screw and identify the three cables
Step 03.6 — Verify the PE screw and identify the three cables
docs.text:
Step 6 of 20 · Chapter 03 — Build plate

Do:

  1. Identify the three cables at the back edge: N, Bed L, and the BED TH ATC Semitec 104NT thermistor.
  2. Find the M4×6 BHCS beside them, the bed PE point.
  3. Leave it in place until Ch 10.

Parts:

  • none — the PE screw is already fitted

Check

Three labelled cables, no chafe or cut in the braid, no exposed conductor. PE screw present, snug.

What you're looking at

Manual p.57: the plate's cable exit. Three cables leave here: two thick braided AC leads, N and Bed L, and one thin two-pin BED TH thermistor cable. Beside them the protective-earth M4×6 BHCS bonds the plate to earth. Washer (verify on bench). See the glossary.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: the manual calls for an M3×6 BHCS you supply. Your plate ships with an M4×6 BHCS already attached — use that one. src

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: do not wire the PE, the heater leads or the thermistor here. The bed harness is a breakout design: the AC leads land on the bed WAGO mount and the SSR, and the thermistor on the 2×2 XH splicer PCB, all in Ch 10. src

Good stopping point · ~30 min since the last one

the plate is unpacked and identified top from bottom, the film is off, and the pre-applied heater, thermal fuse and PE screw are all inspected and left alone. The magnet is still in its backing. Do not start Step 03.9 until you can run 03.8–03.10 straight through: the magnet is a one-shot lamination.

Source: Voron manual p.57 · LDO Build Notes (Rev D) · LDO wiring guide § Wiring the Bed Heater

docs.title: Step 03.7 — Check the plate for flatness before the magnet goes on
Step 03.7 — Check the plate for flatness before the magnet goes on
docs.text:
Step 7 of 20 · Chapter 03 — Build plate

Do: Stand the straightedge on edge on the ground face and sight against a light: one diagonal and one centreline, two minutes. Do it now; once the magnet is on you cannot inspect this surface again.

Parts:

  • build plate, steel rule or straightedge

Check

No daylight under the straightedge. Flatness tolerance is not specified; raise it in #ldo_motors only if a sheet of paper slides under.

What you're looking at

The bare ground face and a straightedge. This is the last moment the aluminium is visible. Once the magnet is on, a dish or crown can only be inferred from a bed mesh, and neither mesh nor quad gantry level corrects it.

Tip

a cast, Blanchard-ground 5083 plate is deliberately thick and stress-relieved; a visible dish here does not get corrected by mesh or QGL later. src

Source: Voron manual p.53 · LDO 350 Rev D BOM

docs.title: Step 03.8 — Clean the top face
Step 03.8 — Clean the top face
docs.text:
Step 8 of 20 · Chapter 03 — Build plate

Do: Wipe the whole top face with IPA and let it flash off completely, so no solvent is trapped under the adhesive. Wear gloves from here on.

Parts:

  • build plate
  • IPA, lint-free cloth, gloves

Check

Surface dry, no lint, no residue in the counterbores.

What you're looking at

The top face, IPA and a lint-free cloth. Oil, dust or a fingerprint left on the surface becomes a permanent bump under an adhesive sheet you cannot lift again.

Source: Voron manual p.54

← PreviousStep 03.7 — Check the plate for flatness before the magnet goes on
