Next →Step 05.14 — Load the reserved M5 + M3 pair at each end

docs.title: Step 05.14 — Load the reserved M5 + M3 pair at each end
Step 05.14 — Load the reserved M5 + M3 pair at each end
docs.text:
Step 14 of 48 · Chapter 05 — Gantry: X and Y axes, XY joints, X carriage, titanium backers

Do: At each end of each C extrusion add one M5 T-nut and one M3 T-nut into the rail's own slot, in the bare 25 mm beyond each rail end: M5 outermost, M3 just inboard. Not the top slot.

Parts:

  • M5 T-nut ×4, M3 T-nut ×4

Check

Per end: 2× M5 in the top slot, 1× M5 and 1× M3 in the rail slot beyond the rail end.

What you're looking at

Another M5 and M3 nut at each end, in the rail's own slot, the underside of the Y axis. They serve the Ch 06 Z joints and the Ch 10 chain and endstop mounts; the idler and drive frames close these slots permanently.

Source: Voron manual p.90

← PreviousStep 05.13 — Second Y axis, then load the end M5 T-nuts

Next →Step 05.15 — Stop the carriages running off

docs.title: Step 05.15 — Stop the carriages running off
Step 05.15 — Stop the carriages running off
docs.text:
Step 15 of 48 · Chapter 05 — Gantry: X and Y axes, XY joints, X carriage, titanium backers

Do: Fit a rubber rail stopper, or a doubled tape flag, near each end of both Y rails so a carriage cannot run off. Keep the stoppers: LDO reuses them under the Z joints during the Ch 06 install. src

Parts:

  • rubber rail stoppers (LDO-supplied) or masking tape

Check

Each Y carriage is captive; the manual warns that "dropping the carriage likely irreparably damages it".

What you're looking at

A linear-rail carriage keeps its ball bearings only while it is on the rail: run it off the end and they scatter. The renders show the Y rails on the undersides of the C extrusions, each with one carriage and a stopper near each end.

Tip

The CAD Y rails are MGN9 300 mm; yours are 400 mm (Step 05.10). The stoppers go near the ends wherever those ends are.

Good stopping point · ~30 min since the last one

both Y rails down and tightened, end M5/M3 T-nuts loaded, both carriages captive. Do not fit a backer now: start one only when you can finish it.

Source: Voron manual p.88 · LDO Build Notes § Voron 2.4 build FAQ · CAD: Voron 2.4r2 STEP @ de7e89d

← PreviousStep 05.14 — Load the reserved M5 + M3 pair at each end

Next →Step 05.16 — Unpack and identify the titanium backers

docs.title: Step 05.16 — Unpack and identify the titanium backers
Step 05.16 — Unpack and identify the titanium backers
docs.text:
Step 16 of 48 · Chapter 05 — Gantry: X and Y axes, XY joints, X carriage, titanium backers

Do: Sort the three backers: the two matching long pieces are the Y backers, the odd shorter one is the X backer. Check they are drilled and countersunk, and count the holes in each.

Parts:

  • titanium backer set ×3 (2 long "Y", 1 shorter "X"), M3×8 FHCS ×~20, M3×6 FHCS ×~8, M3 roll-in T-nut ×~30

Check

2 Y + 1 X backer, hole counts written down, and you have at least that many M3 T-nuts. The set does not include T-nuts.

What you're looking at

The titanium backers are three flat drilled strips that bolt to the extrusion face opposite a linear rail. A steel rail on an aluminium extrusion bows as the chamber heats; the titanium strip opposite pulls the other way and cancels most of the bow.

Tip

Backer lengths in the picture follow the 250 CAD. Sort by matched pair versus odd one, not by drawn length. A slightly bowed backer straightens as you clamp it down.

Source: Ti extrusion-backers README (tanaes) · Fabreeko backer set · West3D backer set · CAD: Voron 2.4r2 STEP @ de7e89d

← PreviousStep 05.15 — Stop the carriages running off

Next →Step 05.17 — Fit the first Y backer

docs.title: Step 05.17 — Fit the first Y backer
Step 05.17 — Fit the first Y backer
docs.text:
Step 17 of 48 · Chapter 05 — Gantry: X and Y axes, XY joints, X carriage, titanium backers

Do: Turn the first C extrusion rail-down and work on the opposite face. Roll the M3 T-nuts in, lay the backer on, and start every screw before tightening any. Tighten M3×8 FHCS from the centre outwards, using Torx.

Parts:

  • Y backer ×1, M3×8 FHCS ×~10, M3 T-nut ×~10, T10 Torx driver

Check

Backer flat along its whole length, every screw seated in its countersink, and both ends clear of where the idler and drive frames land.

What you're looking at

You are working on the bare face of the first Y extrusion, which becomes the top of the Y axis. FHCS are countersunk screws whose heads sink flush into the backer's chamfered holes; a hex key cams out, so use the T10 Torx.

Never on the rail face

the whole point is to put steel on the face opposite the rail and cancel the bending couple. Doubling up on the rail side makes the bow worse. src

Source: Ti extrusion-backers README (tanaes) (image x_axis.jpeg)

← PreviousStep 05.16 — Unpack and identify the titanium backers

Next →Step 05.18 — Fit the second Y backer

docs.title: Step 05.18 — Fit the second Y backer
Step 05.18 — Fit the second Y backer
docs.text:
Step 18 of 48 · Chapter 05 — Gantry: X and Y axes, XY joints, X carriage, titanium backers

Do: Repeat on the second C extrusion, again on the face opposite its rail. Lay the two finished Y assemblies side by side and confirm they are mirrored: rails facing the same way, backers facing the same way.

Parts:

  • Y backer ×1, M3×8 FHCS ×~10, M3 T-nut ×~10

Check

Both backers on the rail-opposite face, both flat. Their cable-chain pilot holes end up on the same side of the machine.

What you're looking at

The second Y extrusion, same treatment on its rail-opposite face. The first render shows one Y extrusion from underneath, rail face and backer face both in frame. The second shows both Y beams in place: rails underneath on both, backers on top on both.

Tip

The CAD C extrusion is 350 mm with a 300 mm rail (250 machine); yours is the 350-kit C with a 400 mm rail.

Good stopping point · ~35 min since the last one

both titanium Y backers screwed down flat on the rail-opposite face. Check nothing is cammed out before you stop.

Source: Ti extrusion-backers README (tanaes) · CAD: Voron 2.4r2 STEP @ de7e89d

← PreviousStep 05.17 — Fit the first Y backer

Next →Step 05.19 — Fit the front idler to the first Y axis

docs.title: Step 05.19 — Fit the front idler to the first Y axis
Step 05.19 — Fit the front idler to the first Y axis
docs.text:
Step 19 of 48 · Chapter 05 — Gantry: X and Y axes, XY joints, X carriage, titanium backers

Do:

  1. Take the A idler: FRONT RIGHT, tall 21.6 mm lower frame, two M5 holes in the top.
  2. Slide it on the front end of the first C extrusion, then drive two M5×16 BHCS into its top T-nuts.

Parts:

  • front idler assembly ×1, M5×16 BHCS ×2

Check

Two M5 holes on top, both bolts biting into T-nuts, idler pulled up tight against the extrusion.

What you're looking at

The front idler block is the Ch 04 assembly that turns its belt around at the front corner: a printed frame around a stack of bearings, with a belt-clamp notch moulded into the outside. It slides onto the front end of a Y extrusion.

Source: Voron manual p.91 · Video: Part 4 @0:06:41

← PreviousStep 05.18 — Fit the second Y backer

Next →Step 05.20 — Check flush and notch orientation

docs.title: Step 05.2 — Name the six gantry parts
Step 05.2 — Name the six gantry parts
docs.text:
Step 2 of 48 · Chapter 05 — Gantry: X and Y axes, XY joints, X carriage, titanium backers

Do: Learn the names: B Drive rear left, A Drive rear right, XY Bridge, both XY Joints, X Linear Rail, B Idler front left, A Idler front right. Tape A and B onto the two drive units now.

Parts: none.

Check

You can point at the A drive, the B idler and the right XY joint without hesitating.

What you're looking at

The same rectangle, now labelled. A and B are the two CoreXY motors; neither one "is" an axis. The XY bridge holds the drives apart, the XY joints cap the ends of the X beam, and the front idlers turn each belt back.

Source: Voron manual p.83

← PreviousStep 05.1 — Clear the bench and confirm the sub-assemblies

Next →Step 05.3 — Pick the cable-chain bridge

docs.title: Step 05.20 — Check flush and notch orientation
Step 05.20 — Check flush and notch orientation
docs.text:
Step 20 of 48 · Chapter 05 — Gantry: X and Y axes, XY joints, X carriage, titanium backers

Do: Sight the joint from the end: the plastic must sit flush with the end face. A wrong-hand idler will not, so take it off rather than pulling it down with bolts. The notch points away from the idler assembly.

Parts: none.

Check

Plastic flush to the extrusion end, notch pointing outboard.

What you're looking at

The two front idlers are handed, different parts not mirrored copies: their lower frames differ by 10 mm to match the belt planes. Plastic flush to the end face means the right hand; the notch outboard means the right way up.

Source: Voron manual p.92 · Video: Part 4 @0:08:32

← PreviousStep 05.19 — Fit the front idler to the first Y axis

Next →Step 05.21 — Fit the second front idler

docs.title: Step 05.21 — Fit the second front idler
Step 05.21 — Fit the second front idler
docs.text:
Step 21 of 48 · Chapter 05 — Gantry: X and Y axes, XY joints, X carriage, titanium backers

Do: Same on the second Y assembly with the B idler: FRONT LEFT, the short 11.6 mm lower frame, which becomes the left-hand Y axis. Push flush, two M5×16 BHCS into the top-slot T-nuts, snug.

Parts:

  • front idler assembly ×1, M5×16 BHCS ×2

Check

Both Y assemblies now have an idler at the front, both flush, both notches pointing away from the idler body.

What you're looking at

The other front corner, with the opposite-hand idler. After this the two Y assemblies are complete as sides of the machine: rail, backer and idler on each.

Source: Voron manual p.93

← PreviousStep 05.20 — Check flush and notch orientation

Next →Step 05.22 — Offer both Y axes to the drive units

docs.title: Step 05.22 — Offer both Y axes to the drive units
Step 05.22 — Offer both Y axes to the drive units
docs.text:
Step 22 of 48 · Chapter 05 — Gantry: X and Y axes, XY joints, X carriage, titanium backers

Do: Bring each C extrusion into its drive frame: the A idler axis into the A drive, the B-idler axis into the B drive. Push each until the printed frame is flush with the extrusion end, on a flat bench.

Parts:

  • the two Y assemblies, the bridge + drives assembly

Check

A U-shaped gantry: A idler with A drive on one beam, B with B, both rails and both backers facing the same way.

What you're looking at

Now the two sides meet the rear beam. The A drive takes the right-hand side and the B drive the left, so the Ch 04 belt planes reach the corners those belts run to. The result is a U, open at the front.

Source: Voron manual p.94 · Video: Part 4 @0:34:56

← PreviousStep 05.21 — Fit the second front idler

Next →Step 05.23 — Bolt the Y axes to the drives

docs.title: Step 05.23 — Bolt the Y axes to the drives
Step 05.23 — Bolt the Y axes to the drives
docs.text:
Step 23 of 48 · Chapter 05 — Gantry: X and Y axes, XY joints, X carriage, titanium backers

Do: Two M5×16 BHCS per side, down through the drive frame's top flange into the M5 T-nuts at the rear of each C extrusion, snug only. Plastic flush with the extrusion end, notch pointing away from the drive assembly.

Parts:

  • M5×16 BHCS ×4

Check

Four bolts in, both rear joints flush, both notches outboard.

What you're looking at

Two M5×16 per side, down through each drive frame's flange into the rear-end T-nuts, closing the two rear corners. The checks repeat the idler checks: a block not pushed fully home leaves that corner short, and a short corner cannot be squared.

Source: Voron manual p.95

← PreviousStep 05.22 — Offer both Y axes to the drive units

Next →Step 05.24 — Sanity-check the gantry frame, then leave it alone

docs.title: Step 05.24 — Sanity-check the gantry frame, then leave it alone
Step 05.24 — Sanity-check the gantry frame, then leave it alone
docs.text:
Step 24 of 48 · Chapter 05 — Gantry: X and Y axes, XY joints, X carriage, titanium backers

Do: Lay the U-frame flat and measure from the inside face of one Y extrusion to the other, at the bridge and again at the idlers. A difference means a corner block is not pushed home.

Parts: none.

Check

Front and rear spacing equal on the rule. Do not square or lock the gantry now; Ch 06 does it in the frame.

What you're looking at

Four corners, all snug, none torqued. Measuring inside face to inside face at both ends tells you the two Y axes are parallel. The frame can still rack, deforming into a parallelogram, and that freedom is deliberate: Ch 06 squares it in the frame.

Good stopping point · ~40 min since the last one

front idlers and both Y axes bolted to the drives, gantry frame sanity-checked and deliberately left slightly loose. Do not tighten anything further; do not start an XY joint (each joint is a bearing stack you must finish in one go).

Source: Voron manual p.95

← PreviousStep 05.23 — Bolt the Y axes to the drives

Next →Step 05.25 — Seat the M5 nuts in both XY joints

docs.title: Step 05.25 — Seat the M5 nuts in both XY joints
Step 05.25 — Seat the M5 nuts in both XY joints
docs.text:
Step 25 of 48 · Chapter 05 — Gantry: X and Y axes, XY joints, X carriage, titanium backers

Do: Drop three M5 nuts into the hex pockets of each XY joint body, flats aligned to the pocket. Push each fully home with a spare M5 bolt; a proud nut stops the joint closing and cracks the pocket.

Parts:

  • xy_joint_left_lower_MGN12 ×1, xy_joint_right_lower_MGN12 ×1, M5 nut ×6

Check

Three nuts per joint, all flush in their pockets, none rotated out of the hex.

What you're looking at

The XY joints are the two printed blocks that ride on the Y carriages. Each is a thick lower body, ~34 mm, plus a thin upper plate, ~16 mm. The right lower body has a moulded wire channel; the left is plain.

Source: Voron manual p.96 · Video: Part 5 @1:18:07 (differs: substitutes Trident-repo parts still in beta at the time)

← PreviousStep 05.24 — Sanity-check the gantry frame, then leave it alone

Next →Step 05.26 — Start the right XY joint bearing stack

docs.title: Step 05.26 — Start the right XY joint bearing stack
Step 05.26 — Start the right XY joint bearing stack
docs.text:
Step 26 of 48 · Chapter 05 — Gantry: X and Y axes, XY joints, X carriage, titanium backers

Do:

  1. Keep the right-hand joint's moulded cable path clear and pointing as the page shows.
  2. Push an M5×40 SHCS up through the upper plate.
  3. Thread on bottom to top: spacer, F695 flange down, F695 flange up, spacer.

Parts:

  • xy_joint_right_upper_MGN12 ×1, M5×40 SHCS ×1, F695 bearing ×2, M5 precision spacer ×2

Check

Four items on the bolt, reading spacer, flange, plain, plain, flange, spacer from the side; bearings spin freely, cable channel clear.

What you're looking at

The two upper plates, left and right, carry the same tell as the lower bodies: the right-hand plate has the endstop wire channel. The stack you build on the M5×40 is the belt corner: two F695 flanged bearings, flange-out, between two brass precision spacers.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: the manual's "M5 Shim" is the brass M5 precision spacer in this kit, here and everywhere else unless a page is explicitly noted otherwise. src

Source: Voron manual p.97 · LDO Build Notes § Voron 2.4 build FAQ · Video: Part 3 @1:27:47 (differs: pre-release kit had no titanium rail backers)

← PreviousStep 05.25 — Seat the M5 nuts in both XY joints

Next →Step 05.27 — Close the right XY joint

docs.title: Step 05.27 — Close the right XY joint
Step 05.27 — Close the right XY joint
docs.text:
Step 27 of 48 · Chapter 05 — Gantry: X and Y axes, XY joints, X carriage, titanium backers

Do: Bring the joint body down over the bearing stack so the M5×40's thread enters the nut pocket you loaded at Step 05.25. The two halves must meet with no gap and no bearing pinched between them.

Parts:

  • xy_joint_right_lower_MGN12 ×1 (with its three M5 nuts)

Check

Halves closed flat, bolt engaged in its nut, bearing stack still turning by finger.

What you're looking at

The lower body comes down over the bearing stack and the M5×40's thread picks up one of its seated M5 nuts. The two halves must close plastic-to-plastic with no gap; a bearing pinched between them drags on the belt until Ch 07 finds it.

Source: Voron manual p.97 · Video: Part 3 @1:28:26 (differs: pre-release kit had no titanium rail backers)

← PreviousStep 05.26 — Start the right XY joint bearing stack

Next →Step 05.28 — Bolt the right XY joint together

docs.title: Step 05.28 — Bolt the right XY joint together
Step 05.28 — Bolt the right XY joint together
docs.text:
Step 28 of 48 · Chapter 05 — Gantry: X and Y axes, XY joints, X carriage, titanium backers

Do: Add the two remaining M5×40 SHCS from the top into the other two M5 nuts, then tighten all three evenly and firm: they thread into steel nuts and clamp the joint into one rigid part.

Parts:

  • M5×40 SHCS ×2

Check

No light between the halves anywhere. The bearing stack still spins.

What you're looking at

The other two M5×40 bolts. Three bolts into three captive nuts turn the two printed halves into a single rigid block, which it has to be: belt tension in Ch 07 pulls hard on this corner and tries to prise it open.

Source: Voron manual p.98 · Video: Part 3 @1:21:27 (differs: pre-release kit had no titanium rail backers)

← PreviousStep 05.27 — Close the right XY joint

Next →Step 05.29 — Fit the right joint's 20-tooth idler

docs.title: Step 05.29 — Fit the right joint's 20-tooth idler
Step 05.29 — Fit the right joint's 20-tooth idler
docs.text:
Step 29 of 48 · Chapter 05 — Gantry: X and Y axes, XY joints, X carriage, titanium backers

Do: Drop the 20T idler into its pocket and run an M5×40 SHCS down through it. This bolt threads directly into plastic and only positions the idler.

Parts:

  • GT2 20-tooth idler ×1, M5×40 SHCS ×1

Check

Idler spins under a fingernail flick with no drag and no wobble.

What you're looking at

The 20 T idler is a small toothed pulley running on its own bearing; the toothed side of the belt wraps it. Its M5×40 threads straight into plastic and only holds the idler in place, so it stops the instant the head seats.

Caution

Do not over-tighten. Stop the moment the head seats and the idler still spins freely; a crushed pocket here shows up as belt noise and premature wear in Ch 07.

Good stopping point · ~25 min since the last one

right XY joint fully built, bolted and its 20T idler fitted and spinning. Leave the left joint's parts bagged; do not part-build it.

Source: Voron manual p.98 · Video: Part 3 @1:25:58 (differs: pre-release kit had no titanium rail backers)

← PreviousStep 05.28 — Bolt the right XY joint together

Next →Step 05.30 — Build the left XY joint

docs.title: Step 05.3 — Pick the cable-chain bridge
Step 05.3 — Pick the cable-chain bridge
docs.text:
Step 3 of 48 · Chapter 05 — Gantry: X and Y axes, XY joints, X carriage, titanium backers

Do: You printed only the 2-hole bridge, on plate B02-P3. Confirm it is the 2-hole one: two holes on the raised pad. Set it beside the raised alternate.

Parts:

  • [a]_xy_joint_cable_bridge_2hole.stl ×1 (orange)

Check

One 2-hole bridge on the bench, one raised alternate beside it; no 3-hole part exists in this build.

What you're looking at

The cable bridge is the orange arch on top of the right XY joint, lifting the toolhead's drag chain clear of the belts. The two versions differ in the end-link hole pattern: three for generic chains, two for the IGUS chains this kit ships.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: "Our cable chain ends use the 2 hole configuration. When printing parts that interface with cable chains, always use the 2hole version instead of 3hole (e.g. xy_joint_cable_bridge_2hole instead of xy_joint_cable_bridge_3hole)." src

Tip

keep XY_cable_chain_bridge-Igus-3mm_backer.stl beside it — same 2-hole pattern, raised ~3 mm for a backer. The backers' chain-end holes are pilot only: drill 2.5 mm, tap M3. src

Source: Voron manual p.84 · LDO printed-parts guide (Rev D) · Ti extrusion-backers README (tanaes) · Video: Part 3 @1:43:24

← PreviousStep 05.2 — Name the six gantry parts

Next →Step 05.4 — Test-fit T-nuts and stage the fasteners

docs.title: Step 05.30 — Build the left XY joint
Step 05.30 — Build the left XY joint
docs.text:
Step 30 of 48 · Chapter 05 — Gantry: X and Y axes, XY joints, X carriage, titanium backers

Do: Mirror of Steps 05.26–05.27: M5×40 up through the upper plate, then spacer, F695 flange down, F695 flange up, spacer. Close the joint body over it into its M5 nut. The left parts have no cable channel.

Parts:

  • xy_joint_left_upper_MGN12 ×1, xy_joint_left_lower_MGN12 ×1, M5×40 SHCS ×1, F695 bearing ×2, M5 precision spacer ×2

Check

Left and right joints sit as mirror images on the bench, not as two of the same hand.

What you're looking at

The left joint, built exactly as the right was. The tell is the wire channel: only the right-hand pair has one. If the parts in your hand have a channel, put them down; they are the right joint's.

Source: Voron manual p.99

← PreviousStep 05.29 — Fit the right joint's 20-tooth idler

Next →Step 05.31 — Bolt the left joint and fit its idler

docs.title: Step 05.31 — Bolt the left joint and fit its idler
Step 05.31 — Bolt the left joint and fit its idler
docs.text:
Step 31 of 48 · Chapter 05 — Gantry: X and Y axes, XY joints, X carriage, titanium backers

Do: Two M5×40 SHCS from the top into the remaining M5 nuts, tightened evenly and firm into steel. Then the 20T idler and its own M5×40 into plastic: snug only, must spin.

Parts:

  • M5×40 SHCS ×3, GT2 20-tooth idler ×1

Check

Both joints complete: 4× M5×40 each, 2× F695 each, two spacers each, one 20T idler each, all bearing stacks and both idlers free.

What you're looking at

Both joints finished and identical in content: 4× M5×40, 2× F695 between two precision spacers, and one 20 T idler each. Everything meant to spin must still spin freely; drag here becomes belt noise once the belts go on.

Good stopping point · ~20 min since the last one

both XY joints built, bolted and idler-fitted, sitting loose on the bench. Do not slide them onto the X extrusion yet.

Source: Voron manual p.100 · Video: Part 3 @1:31:05 (differs: pre-release kit had no titanium rail backers)

← PreviousStep 05.30 — Build the left XY joint

Next →Step 05.32 — Load M3 T-nuts for the X rail

docs.title: Step 05.32 — Load M3 T-nuts for the X rail
Step 05.32 — Load M3 T-nuts for the X rail
docs.text:
Step 32 of 48 · Chapter 05 — Gantry: X and Y axes, XY joints, X carriage, titanium backers

Do: The 400 mm MGN12H LDO-SLR12H-400Z1 has ~16 holes at 25 mm pitch and uses every other one, so about 8 T-nuts. Mark them. Slide the T-nuts into the D extrusion's rail slot, leaving about 15 mm clear at each end.

Parts:

  • D extrusion ×1, M3 T-nut ×~8

Check

~8 nuts in, one per marked hole, flat, with clear slot at both ends.

What you're looking at

The D extrusion is the X beam, the one the toolhead runs along. It carries an MGN12 rail, wider than the Y rails because it holds the toolhead off one carriage. Same T-nut rule: load them before the XY joints cap the ends.

Source: Voron manual p.101

← PreviousStep 05.31 — Bolt the left joint and fit its idler

Next →Step 05.33 — Centre and fit the MGN12 rail

docs.title: Step 05.33 — Centre and fit the MGN12 rail
Step 05.33 — Centre and fit the MGN12 rail
docs.text:
Step 33 of 48 · Chapter 05 — Gantry: X and Y axes, XY joints, X carriage, titanium backers

Do: Tape the carriage mid-rail; peel its Ch 00 bands off with the rail flat. Sit the rail on the D extrusion, centred by an MGN12 guide at each end. Start at the second hole from each end, then tighten centre-outwards.

Parts:

  • MGN12H 400 mm rail ×1, MGN12_rail_guide_x2 jig ×2, M3×8 SHCS ×~8 (one per marked hole)

Check

15 mm of bare extrusion beyond each rail end, equal; the carriage runs the rail with no tight spot and no gap underneath.

What you're looking at

Same centre-and-tighten procedure as the Y rails, with the larger MGN12 guides. This is the rail that decides print quality across X: it must sit centred along its whole length and pull down flat with no gap underneath.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: second hole in from each end here too, not the end hole. src

Source: Voron manual p.101 · LDO Build Notes § Voron 2.4 build FAQ · LDO rail-grease guide · Video: Part 3 @1:34:46

← PreviousStep 05.32 — Load M3 T-nuts for the X rail

Next →Step 05.34 — Fit the X backer to the rear face

docs.title: Step 05.34 — Fit the X backer to the rear face
Step 05.34 — Fit the X backer to the rear face
docs.text:
Step 34 of 48 · Chapter 05 — Gantry: X and Y axes, XY joints, X carriage, titanium backers

Do: Turn the D extrusion so the MGN12 rail faces you. The backer goes on the rear face, opposite the rail, not on top. Roll the T-nuts in, start every screw, then tighten centre-outwards. Use M3×6 FHCS for X.

Parts:

  • X backer ×1, M3×6 FHCS ×~8, M3 T-nut ×~8

Check

Backer on the face opposite the MGN12, flat, all screws M3×6 and seated; the top face of the D extrusion still clear.

What you're looking at

The X backer goes on the rear face, the one opposite the rail, same as on the Y axes: steel on one face, titanium on the other, the bows cancelling. The top face stays bare for the XY joints and cable bridge.

Caution

"For X axes, in most cases you'll want to install them on the rear of the X extrusion, opposite the MGN12 rail… If you have a single MGN12 but decide to put a backer on top, you will be actively contributing to the problem of bimetallic expansion!" src

Source: Ti extrusion-backers README (tanaes) (image fusion_x_chainmount.png)

← PreviousStep 05.33 — Centre and fit the MGN12 rail

Next →Step 05.35 — Check backer clearance for the cable chain

docs.title: Step 05.35 — Check backer clearance for the cable chain
Step 05.35 — Check backer clearance for the cable chain
docs.text:
Step 35 of 48 · Chapter 05 — Gantry: X and Y axes, XY joints, X carriage, titanium backers

Do: Offer the chain's end link up to the X and Y backers and see whether the holes line up and the stock printed bridge sits flat. Do not fit the chain; you are only deciding which bridge to keep.

Parts:

  • cable-chain end link (dry fit only)

Check

You know whether you will use [a]_xy_joint_cable_bridge_2hole or the raised XY_cable_chain_bridge-Igus-3mm_backer. "Igus" = the 2-hole pattern LDO ships. src

What you're looking at

A dry fit. The backers carry pilot holes for the cable chain's end link, and a 3 mm titanium strip may now hold the printed bridge's flat foot off the extrusion. The renders show the chain's fixed end and its run to the bridge.

Tip

The CAD is the 250 machine's; a 350 chain run is longer. Only the face the end link lands on transfers. The raised bridge is a mod part.

Good stopping point · ~35 min since the last one

MGN12 rail centred and screwed down on the X extrusion, titanium X backer on the rear face, cable-chain clearance checked. Carriage taped captive.

Source: Ti extrusion-backers README (tanaes) · LDO cable-chain guide · CAD: Voron 2.4r2 STEP @ de7e89d

← PreviousStep 05.34 — Fit the X backer to the rear face

Next →Step 05.36 — Load the D extrusion's M5 T-nuts

docs.title: Step 05.36 — Load the D extrusion's M5 T-nuts
Step 05.36 — Load the D extrusion's M5 T-nuts
docs.text:
Step 36 of 48 · Chapter 05 — Gantry: X and Y axes, XY joints, X carriage, titanium backers

Do: In the top slot, at 90° to the rail face, put two M5 T-nuts at each end, four in total. In the bottom slot put one at each end, two in total. Nothing in the rail or backer slots.

Parts:

  • M5 T-nut ×6

Check

4 + 2 = six M5 T-nuts. The two singles line up with the through-holes the M5×30 bolts will use from underneath.

What you're looking at

Six M5 T-nuts in two slots of the X beam: four in the top face the XY joints bolt onto, two in the bottom face for the bolts that come up from underneath. They clamp each joint from both sides so it cannot rock.

Source: Voron manual p.102

← PreviousStep 05.35 — Check backer clearance for the cable chain

Next →Step 05.37 — Slide both XY joints onto the X extrusion

docs.title: Step 05.37 — Slide both XY joints onto the X extrusion
Step 05.37 — Slide both XY joints onto the X extrusion
docs.text:
Step 37 of 48 · Chapter 05 — Gantry: X and Y axes, XY joints, X carriage, titanium backers

Do: Push a joint onto each end of the D extrusion: left joint to the left end, right joint, the one with the endstop cable channel, to the right. Seat each until the extrusion bottoms out in the joint's pocket.

Parts:

  • left XY joint ×1, right XY joint ×1

Check

Both joints fully home; the two 20T idlers and the two bearing stacks all face the same way along the extrusion.

What you're looking at

Each joint's pocket slides over an end of the X beam. This is the first time the X axis exists as one object: beam, rail, backer and both belt corners.

Source: Voron manual p.103

← PreviousStep 05.36 — Load the D extrusion's M5 T-nuts

Next →Step 05.38 — Bolt the joints from above, with the cable bridge

docs.title: Step 05.38 — Bolt the joints from above, with the cable bridge
Step 05.38 — Bolt the joints from above, with the cable bridge
docs.text:
Step 38 of 48 · Chapter 05 — Gantry: X and Y axes, XY joints, X carriage, titanium backers

Do:

  1. Left joint: two M5×10 BHCS down into the top-slot T-nuts.
  2. Right joint: lay the cable bridge's foot over the same two holes and bolt through both with the longer M5×16 BHCS.
  3. "LEAVE SLIGHTLY LOOSE": lightly tighten.

Parts:

  • M5×10 BHCS ×2, [a]_xy_joint_cable_bridge_2hole ×1, M5×16 BHCS ×2

Check

Bridge foot flat with its arm standing up on the right-hand side; four bolts started and lightly tightened, none torqued.

What you're looking at

Bolts through the top of each joint into the beam's top-slot T-nuts. On the right, the cable bridge's foot is sandwiched under the heads, so that side needs the longer M5×16. They stay slightly loose: Ch 06 squares the gantry by nudging these joints.

Source: Voron manual p.104

← PreviousStep 05.37 — Slide both XY joints onto the X extrusion

Next →Step 05.39 — Bolt the joints from below

docs.title: Step 05.39 — Bolt the joints from below
Step 05.39 — Bolt the joints from below
docs.text:
Step 39 of 48 · Chapter 05 — Gantry: X and Y axes, XY joints, X carriage, titanium backers

Do: Turn the X assembly over and run an M5×30 BHCS with a washer under its head up into each of the single M5 T-nuts from Step 05.36. Light tightening again: the joint stays slightly loose until Ch 06.

Parts:

  • M5×30 BHCS ×2, black M5 washer ×2

Check

Two M5×30 in with black washers under the heads, both lightly tightened.

What you're looking at

Two more bolts, this time up into the joints from underneath the beam, each with a black washer to spread the load across the plastic. Pulled from both faces the joint cannot rock, but stays lightly tightened until squaring.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO (p.104): "Use the black M5 Washer instead of the M5 Shim cause it looks nicer." This page is the documented exception to the precision-spacer substitution. src

Source: Voron manual p.104 · LDO Build Notes § Voron 2.4 build FAQ

← PreviousStep 05.38 — Bolt the joints from above, with the cable bridge

Next →Step 05.40 — Check the X axis assembly

docs.title: Step 05.4 — Test-fit T-nuts and stage the fasteners
Step 05.4 — Test-fit T-nuts and stage the fasteners
docs.text:
Step 4 of 48 · Chapter 05 — Gantry: X and Y axes, XY joints, X carriage, titanium backers

Do:

  1. Roll one M5 and one M3 T-nut through each face of all four extrusions.
  2. Mark any face that binds with tape.
  3. Count the fasteners out into labelled trays per the hardware table above.

Parts:

  • M5 roll-in T-nut ×26, M3 roll-in T-nut ×≈32 (+ ~30 for the backers)

Check

Every T-nut you will use rolls in without force; a forced nut galls the channel.

What you're looking at

A roll-in T-nut drops into an extrusion slot and rotates a quarter turn to lock, and almost every bolt in this chapter pulls against one. The renders show the four extrusions, E, both C beams and D, with every T-nut already in its slot.

Tip

The CAD extrusions are the 250 lengths (E 240, C 350, D 330 mm); yours are the 350 set. Which faces carry nuts, and how many, is what transfers.

Good stopping point · ~25 min since the last one

bench cleared, sub-assemblies laid out left/right, T-nuts test-rolled and counted into trays. Nothing is assembled; leave the trays covered so nothing gets swept off.

Source: LDO Build Notes § Voron 2.4 build FAQ · Voron manual p.85 · Video: Part 4 @0:36:43 · CAD: Voron 2.4r2 STEP @ de7e89d

← PreviousStep 05.3 — Pick the cable-chain bridge

Next →Step 05.5 — Load the E extrusion (XY bridge)

docs.title: Step 05.40 — Check the X axis assembly
Step 05.40 — Check the X axis assembly
docs.text:
Step 40 of 48 · Chapter 05 — Gantry: X and Y axes, XY joints, X carriage, titanium backers

Do:

  1. Left joint: F695 stack upper, 20T idler lower. Right joint: 20T upper, F695 lower.
  2. Sight along the extrusion: left 20T level with right F695, left F695 level with right 20T. Spin all four.

Parts: none.

Check

Left 20T level with right F695, left F695 level with right 20T; nothing binds; the MGN12 carriage still slides freely and is still taped.

What you're looking at

The finished X axis, checked against the drawing. You are sighting for each belt's two corners at the same height: a corner a millimetre out of plane feeds the belt into the drive pulley at an angle and chews its edge.

Good stopping point · ~35 min since the last one

both XY joints bolted to the X extrusion top and bottom, cable bridge on, assembly checked against p.105. Still motors-down, the way it runs. The flip is the next step — do not attempt it alone.

Source: Voron manual p.105

← PreviousStep 05.39 — Bolt the joints from below

Next →Step 05.41 — Turn the gantry upside down

docs.title: Step 05.41 — Turn the gantry upside down
Step 05.41 — Turn the gantry upside down
docs.text:
Step 41 of 48 · Chapter 05 — Gantry: X and Y axes, XY joints, X carriage, titanium backers

Do: Turn the gantry over so the A/B motors point up and both Y rails face you. The gantry is now upside down and stays that way through Step 05.48. Get help: it is large and the drives are heavy.

Parts: none.

Check

Motors up, both Y rails and carriages up, nothing dropped on a bearing stack. Left and right are now swapped from where you stand.

What you're looking at

So far the gantry has been built the way it runs: motors hanging below the bridge, Y rails underneath. Now it goes upside down, motors up and both Y rails facing up, so the X axis can be lowered onto the carriages.

Source: Voron manual p.106

← PreviousStep 05.40 — Check the X axis assembly

Next →Step 05.42 — Insert the X axis at an angle

docs.title: Step 05.42 — Insert the X axis at an angle
Step 05.42 — Insert the X axis at an angle
docs.text:
Step 42 of 48 · Chapter 05 — Gantry: X and Y axes, XY joints, X carriage, titanium backers

Do: Tilt the X axis in, one joint onto its Y carriage then the other. The right joint, with the cable bridge, goes on the A drive axis, on your left with the gantry inverted.

Parts:

  • the X axis assembly

Check

Both joints square on their carriages, bolt holes lined up, nothing fouling the Y extrusion; the MGN12 rail faces the idler end.

What you're looking at

The X axis drops onto the two Y carriages, the sliding blocks on the Y rails. Tilting it lets you land one joint at a time; lowering it flat means fighting both carriages at once, and a carriage shoved off its rail is ruined.

Source: Voron manual p.106

← PreviousStep 05.41 — Turn the gantry upside down

Next →Step 05.43 — Bolt the XY joints to the Y carriages

docs.title: Step 05.43 — Bolt the XY joints to the Y carriages
Step 05.43 — Bolt the XY joints to the Y carriages
docs.text:
Step 43 of 48 · Chapter 05 — Gantry: X and Y axes, XY joints, X carriage, titanium backers

Do: The left joint takes all four M3×16 SHCS. The right joint takes two only: "2X BOLT ONLY: the remaining bolts will be installed during the end-stop installation." Take all six to snug.

Parts:

  • M3×16 SHCS ×6

Check

4 bolts on one joint, 2 on the other, and 2 M3×16 left over as spares; Step 05.46 bags the pod's 2× M3×30.

What you're looking at

M3×16 down through each XY joint into the threaded holes in the Y carriage below it. The right joint gets only two: the XY endstop pod fitted at wiring shares its other two holes. The pod's own bolts are M3×30.

Source: Voron manual p.106

← PreviousStep 05.42 — Insert the X axis at an angle

Next →Step 05.44 — Run the X axis end to end

docs.title: Step 05.44 — Run the X axis end to end
Step 05.44 — Run the X axis end to end
docs.text:
Step 44 of 48 · Chapter 05 — Gantry: X and Y axes, XY joints, X carriage, titanium backers

Do: Push the X axis slowly end to end several times, a hand on each XY joint. A tight spot means a rail is not centred; rising stiffness means racking. Do not loosen rails to fix it.

Parts: none.

Check

Full travel both directions, no notch, no rising resistance, both Y carriages moving together. Racking is normal and is corrected in Ch 06.

What you're looking at

The first real function test of the gantry as a mechanism. Even, light resistance the whole way means both rails are centred and both carriages sit square. Resistance growing towards one end is racking, a Ch 06 problem, not a rail problem.

Good stopping point · ~30 min since the last one

gantry upside down (motors up), X axis in and bolted to both Y carriages, running end to end without binding. It stays upside down into Ch 06. Belts still bagged, XY joint bolts still only lightly tightened — leave both alone.

Source: Voron manual p.106

← PreviousStep 05.43 — Bolt the XY joints to the Y carriages

Next →Step 05.45 — Stage the X-carriage frame halves

docs.title: Step 05.45 — Stage the X-carriage frame halves
Step 05.45 — Stage the X-carriage frame halves
docs.text:
Step 45 of 48 · Chapter 05 — Gantry: X and Y axes, XY joints, X carriage, titanium backers

Do: Offer the two carriage halves to the MGN12 carriage and confirm the bolt pattern matches before you commit any heat-set inserts. Then bag them, labelled, with the probe retainer.

Parts:

  • x_frame_V2TR_MGN12_left ×1, x_frame_V2TR_MGN12_right ×1, probe_retainer_bracket ×1

Check

Bolt pattern matches the MGN12 carriage; both halves and the probe retainer bagged and labelled for Ch 07.

What you're looking at

The X carriage is the two-part frame that clamps onto the MGN12 carriage and becomes the mounting plate for the whole toolhead. These are the Clockwork-2 halves, handed so they nest only one way; older X-carriage parts look the same and will not fit.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO (p.129–130): "If you are building Clockwork 2 double-check that you have the correct X-Carriage and follow the instructions in the Stealthburner manual." src The carriage goes on with the belts in Ch 07; the toolhead itself is Ch 08.

Source: Voron manual p.129 · LDO Build Notes § Voron 2.4 build FAQ · Video: Part 5 @1:05:47 (differs: substitutes Trident-repo parts still in beta at the time · MGN12 X was a mod then; it is stock on this kit) · CAD: Voron 2.4r2 STEP @ de7e89d

← PreviousStep 05.44 — Run the X axis end to end

Next →Step 05.46 — Bag what belongs to later chapters

docs.title: Step 05.46 — Bag what belongs to later chapters
Step 05.46 — Bag what belongs to later chapters
docs.text:
Step 46 of 48 · Chapter 05 — Gantry: X and Y axes, XY joints, X carriage, titanium backers

Do:

  1. Bag the endstop pod with 2× M3×30 SHCS and the two spare M3×16 from Step 05.43, labelled.
  2. Bag the [a]_cable_cover and the unused bridge variant separately.

Parts:

  • [a]_endstop_pod_D2F_switch ×1, M3×30 SHCS ×2 (p.164 — verify against the bag), the 2 spare M3×16 kept back earlier, [a]_cable_cover, the unused cable bridge variant

Check

Two labelled bags; nothing loose on the bench that Ch 06 or Ch 07 will need.

What you're looking at

The XY endstop pod is the orange box carrying the X and Y limit switches on the right XY joint. The renders show both either/or choices pulled apart: the D2F pod and 2-hole bridge are kept, the hall-effect pod and 3-hole bridge are not.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: "Our kit includes the XY microswitch PCB, print [a]_endstop_pod_D2F_switch instead of [a]_endstop_pod_hall_effect." src

Source: LDO printed-parts guide (Rev D) · CAD: Voron 2.4r2 STEP @ de7e89d

← PreviousStep 05.45 — Stage the X-carriage frame halves

Next →Step 05.47 — Stop here: no belts, no squaring

docs.title: Step 05.47 — Stop here: no belts, no squaring
Step 05.47 — Stop here: no belts, no squaring
docs.text:
Step 47 of 48 · Chapter 05 — Gantry: X and Y axes, XY joints, X carriage, titanium backers

Do: Do not cut, route or tension the A/B belts, do not tighten the XY joints "properly", and do not square the gantry. Ch 06 squares it in the frame, with A/B tension released and the lower Z joints dropped.

Parts: none.

Check

A/B belts still in their bag. XY joint bolts still only lightly tightened.

What you're looking at

The gantry is complete as a mechanism and deliberately unfinished as a machine. Belts and squaring are held back because the official squaring procedure begins by releasing A/B belt tension; tension it now and Ch 06 simply undoes it.

Source: Voron manual p.107 · Voron docs § V2 Gantry Squaring

← PreviousStep 05.46 — Bag what belongs to later chapters

Next →Step 05.48 — Log the measurements

docs.title: Step 05.48 — Log the measurements
Step 05.48 — Log the measurements
docs.text:
Step 48 of 48 · Chapter 05 — Gantry: X and Y axes, XY joints, X carriage, titanium backers

(no image — see text)

Do: Record the rail overhangs you measured, Y and X at both ends, the two Y-to-Y spacings, which face each backer is on, and anything you left deliberately loose.

Parts:

  • pen
  • the table below

Check

Numbers written down, not "looked fine". You will want the Y-to-Y spacings when the gantry is squared in Ch 06.

What you're looking at

The paperwork you will want in Ch 06. The rail overhangs are the evidence that each rail is centred; the two Y-to-Y spacings are the baseline you measure against once the gantry has been squared in the frame.

Measurement Target Yours Notes Y rail overhang, extrusion 1 — end A / end B 25 / 25 mm Y rail overhang, extrusion 2 — end A / end B 25 / 25 mm X rail overhang — end A / end B 15 / 15 mm Inside Y-to-Y spacing at the bridge — Inside Y-to-Y spacing at the idlers = at bridge Backer face — Y1 / Y2 / X top / top / rear M3×30 SHCS bagged for the endstop pod (p.164) 2

Source: Voron manual p.107 · survey §7.5

← PreviousStep 05.47 — Stop here: no belts, no squaring

Next →Checkpoint 05

docs.title: Step 05.5 — Load the E extrusion (XY bridge)
Step 05.5 — Load the E extrusion (XY bridge)
docs.text:
Step 5 of 48 · Chapter 05 — Gantry: X and Y axes, XY joints, X carriage, titanium backers

Do: Slide eight M5 T-nuts into the E extrusion: per end, two in the top slot and two in the bottom slot. None in the side slots. Push them 10–15 mm from the ends, under the drive frame's bolt holes.

Parts:

  • E extrusion ×1, M5 T-nut ×8

Check

4 nuts at each end: 2 top, 2 bottom, threaded holes facing outward, none jammed.

What you're looking at

The E extrusion is the XY bridge: the beam across the back of the gantry that holds the two drive blocks a fixed distance apart and so sets the gantry's width. The eight M5 T-nuts are what those blocks bolt down onto.

Source: Voron manual p.85

← PreviousStep 05.4 — Test-fit T-nuts and stage the fasteners

Next →Step 05.6 — Slide the A drive onto the E extrusion

docs.title: Step 05.6 — Slide the A drive onto the E extrusion
Step 05.6 — Slide the A drive onto the E extrusion
docs.text:
Step 6 of 48 · Chapter 05 — Gantry: X and Y axes, XY joints, X carriage, titanium backers

Do: Push the A drive unit onto one end of the E extrusion, motor pointing down. It stays this way up until the flip at Step 05.41. Seat it until the printed part is flush with the extrusion end.

Parts:

  • A drive assembly ×1, E extrusion ×1

Check

Plastic flush to the aluminium end face, and the four M5 T-nuts visible through the drive frame's bolt holes.

What you're looking at

The A drive is the right-hand assembly from Ch 04: a stepper motor with its 20 T pulley, wrapped in a printed frame that carries the belt bearing posts. It slides over the end of the bridge extrusion like a sleeve.

Source: Voron manual p.85

← PreviousStep 05.5 — Load the E extrusion (XY bridge)

Next →Step 05.7 — Bolt the A drive to the bridge

docs.title: Step 05.7 — Bolt the A drive to the bridge
Step 05.7 — Bolt the A drive to the bridge
docs.text:
Step 7 of 48 · Chapter 05 — Gantry: X and Y axes, XY joints, X carriage, titanium backers

Do: Drive four M5×10 BHCS, two into the upper slot and two into the lower, to snug, not torqued. If a bolt spins without pulling, its T-nut has not rolled: back it out and reseat the nut.

Parts:

  • M5×10 BHCS ×4

Check

All four bolts bite. The drive frame does not rock on the extrusion.

What you're looking at

Four M5×10 BHCS pass through the drive frame's flange into the T-nuts underneath. This is what turns the drive block and the bridge into one rigid rear corner; a bolt that spins freely means its T-nut never rolled and the corner is holding on three.

Source: Voron manual p.86

← PreviousStep 05.6 — Slide the A drive onto the E extrusion

Next →Step 05.8 — Slide the B drive onto the other end

docs.title: Step 05.8 — Slide the B drive onto the other end
Step 05.8 — Slide the B drive onto the other end
docs.text:
Step 8 of 48 · Chapter 05 — Gantry: X and Y axes, XY joints, X carriage, titanium backers

Do: Push the B drive onto the free end of the E extrusion, motor down, flush to the end face. The motor cable exits must point towards each other. If they point apart, the drives are swapped end for end.

Parts:

  • B drive assembly ×1

Check

Both motor cable exits face inboard, both printed parts flush.

What you're looking at

The B drive is the left-hand counterpart, not an identical copy: its motor pulley sits at 6.5 mm where the A drive's sits at 16.5 mm, which puts the two belts in separate planes so they can cross without touching.

Source: Voron manual p.86

← PreviousStep 05.7 — Bolt the A drive to the bridge

Next →Step 05.9 — Bolt the B drive and check the bridge

docs.title: Step 05.9 — Bolt the B drive and check the bridge
Step 05.9 — Bolt the B drive and check the bridge
docs.text:
Step 9 of 48 · Chapter 05 — Gantry: X and Y axes, XY joints, X carriage, titanium backers

Do: Fit the last four M5×10 BHCS, snug. Then sight down the plan view: the two drive frames must be parallel and the two pulley stacks must line up across the bridge, exactly as the lower graphic shows.

Parts:

  • M5×10 BHCS ×4

Check

Drives parallel, no twist along the bridge, all eight M5×10 in and snug. Nothing here is torqued yet.

What you're looking at

With both drives bolted on, bridge plus drives is a single rear beam: the fixed back edge of the gantry, and the reference everything else is built to. The plan view is the alignment check.

Good stopping point · ~30 min since the last one

XY bridge bolted to both drive units, all eight M5×10 snug, none torqued. Lay the assembly flat, motors down. Do not start a Y rail: a rail must be centred and screwed down in one sitting.

Source: Voron manual p.87

← PreviousStep 05.8 — Slide the B drive onto the other end

Next →Step 05.10 — Load M3 T-nuts for the first Y rail

docs.title: Checkpoint 05
docs.text: Ch 05Checkpoint

docs.title: Checkpoint 05
docs.text:
Checkpoint · Chapter 05 — Gantry: X and Y axes, XY joints, X carriage, titanium backers

What you should have now — The whole gantry as one unit, off the machine: both Y extrusions, the X extrusion, both XY joints with the cable bridge, and the X carriage, with Chapter 04's drive units and idlers closing its four corners. Shown the right way up for comparison with Chapter 06 - Checkpoint 05 leaves it upside down on the bench, and Step 06.11 is where it is turned over and hung on the Z joints. CAD gantry is the 250: 350 mm Y extrusions and a 330 mm X extrusion. Yours are longer. The titanium backers are not in the CAD.
  • E extrusion joined to both drive units with 8× M5×10 BHCS; drives parallel, no twist
  • Both MGN9 rails centred and tightened, first screw in the second hole from each end, overhang equal at both ends
  • MGN12 rail centred and tightened, second hole in, overhang equal at both ends
  • Every carriage retained by a stopper or tape; none dropped
  • At each of the four C-extrusion ends: 2× M5 in the top (backer) slot, 1× M5 + 1× M3 in the rail slot beyond the rail end
  • Titanium backers on the face opposite the rail — top of both Y extrusions, rear of the X extrusion — flat, all screws seated, none cammed out
  • Both front idlers and both rear drive joints flush with the extrusion ends, notches pointing away from the assembly
  • Both XY joints: 3 M5 nuts, 4 M5×40 SHCS, 2 F695 flange-out between 2 precision spacers, 1 free-spinning 20T idler; the three joint bolts firm, the idler bolt snug
  • Cable bridge fitted to the right XY joint with M5×16 BHCS; left joint on M5×10
  • M5×30 BHCS with black M5 washers underneath, both lightly tightened
  • XY joints bolted to the Y carriages: 4 bolts one side, 2 the other; 2× M3×30 SHCS bagged with the endstop pod (p.164), the 2 unused M3×16 kept as spares
  • X axis runs the full Y travel with no tight spot
  • A/B belts still unopened; nothing squared, nothing torqued down
  • Gantry is upside down (motors up, rails up) with the right joint (bridge, endstop channel) on the A-drive side; it is turned back at Ch 06 Step 06.11

← PreviousStep 05.48 — Log the measurements

Next →Ch 06 — before you start

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Fitting the backers after the gantry is built. Their T-nut slots are capped by the idler and drive frames, and the backer face is buried once the gantry is in the frame. It is a ~3 h teardown to fix (survey §5.2 W2).
  • Putting the X backer on top of the X extrusion. With a single MGN12 on the front face, a top backer adds to the bimetallic bow instead of cancelling it, and it blocks the top slot the XY joints and cable bridge bolt into.
  • Using the rails' end holes. The manual only forbids it on 300 mm builds; LDO forbids it on all of them, because the end holes sit exactly where the M5/M3 T-nuts of p.89–90 and p.102 have to live. Caught late, the rail comes off and goes back on.
  • Forgetting the reserved T-nuts at p.90. Nothing in this chapter uses them, so they are easy to skip — and Ch 06's Z joints and Ch 10's chain hardware then have nowhere to bolt to. Count per slot — 2× M5 in the top slot, 1× M5 + 1× M3 in the rail slot — before the idlers go on.
  • One spacer in an XY joint stack, or a flange facing inward. The pair drops 1 mm and its inner races are never clamped, or there is no belt channel at all; found in Ch 07 as belt rub, and both joints come apart again (3× M5×40 + idler each). Fix: spacer, flange down, flange up, spacer — read it from the side before closing the joint (p.97, p.99).
  • Torquing the XY joints and "squaring" on the bench. The joints are meant to stay slightly loose and the gantry is squared in the frame with the belts slack. Tightening now, or tensioning belts now, costs a full de-tension in Ch 07 (survey §5.2 W1).
  • Over-tightening the 20T idler bolts. They thread straight into plastic and only locate the idler. Crushed pockets show up later as belt noise you will blame on tension.

docs.title: Next
docs.text:
Ch 06 — Z axis: gantry install, Z belts and gantry squaring (manual p.108–123, plus the official 16-step squaring procedure); gated on batch B05 (Z joints + Z chain, 1 plate, 6.4 h) — start it now if it is not already printed. Keep the rubber rail stoppers: LDO uses them under the Z joints to rest the gantry during install.

Source: survey §7.5 · Voron manual p.107

Good stopping point · ~25 min since the last one

gantry complete and still upside down (motors up), measurements written down, Ch 06/07 parts bagged and labelled. Do not tension belts and do not square the gantry: both are Ch 06/07 and both would be undone.

docs.title: Before you start Chapter 05
docs.text: Ch 05Before you start

docs.title: Before you start Chapter 05
docs.text:
Before you start · Chapter 05 — Gantry: X and Y axes, XY joints, X carriage, titanium backers

Builds the complete gantry on the bench — XY bridge, both Y axes with their MGN9 rails, both XY joints, the X extrusion with its MGN12 rail, and the titanium extrusion backers — and ends with the X axis riding on the Y carriages. Unlocks Ch 06 (gantry install, Z belts, squaring).

What you're building in this chapter. The gantry is the entire moving upper half of the printer — a rectangle of aluminium extrusion that later hangs on four belts and slides up and down, with the toolhead riding inside it. Its back edge is the XY bridge, the cross-beam that carries the A and B motors you built in Ch 04. Two side extrusions, the Y axes, run forward from that bridge; each has a linear rail along one face and a front idler block at its front end that turns its belt back. Spanning the two sides is the X beam, capped at each end by an XY joint — the printed blocks that ride on the Y carriages and turn each belt around from its Y run to its X run. Bolted to the face opposite every rail are the titanium backers, flat strips that stop a steel rail bowing its aluminium extrusion as the chamber heats. Nothing in this chapter gets belts or squaring: both belong to Ch 06/07, and both would undo work done here.

Time: 5.0–7.0 h hands-on, first build, two people (survey §5.1 P05 / §7.2).

Sessions: 12 × ~30 min (first-build estimate; each Pause: line carries its own segment minutes).

Prerequisites:

  • Ch 04 — A drive, B drive and both front idler assemblies built and checked (manual p.62–81). This chapter consumes them whole.
  • Ch 00 — all seven rails cleaned and packed with grease before they go on an extrusion (LDO rail grease guide); jigs Tools/MGN9_rail_guide_x2.stl and Tools/MGN12_rail_guide_x2.stl printed (batch B00). The rails still wear their Ch 00 end bands (Step 00.17) — they come off at Steps 05.11 / 05.33.
  • Print batches: B04 (XY joints + X carriage, plate B04-P1, 8.6 h, black) and B02-P3 (the orange accent plate — cable bridge and endstop pod) (print plan §B04). B04 needs Gate B (Step B00.7).
  • Titanium backer set (Fabreeko/LDO, 350 size) unpacked and counted.
  • Ch 01's bagged C ×2, D ×1, E ×1 extrusions.

Tools

  • Hex drivers 2 / 2.5 / 3 / 4 mm; a ball-end 2.5 mm helps at the XY joints
  • T10 Torx driver — strongly preferred for the backer M3 FHCS; hex cams out of a countersink easily (backers README)
  • Printed rail-centring jigs MGN9_rail_guide_x2, MGN12_rail_guide_x2
  • Steel rule 300 mm and a caliper — to equalise the rail overhang at both ends
  • Masking tape (carriage retention) and the kit's rubber rail stoppers
  • 2.5 mm flat screwdriver (cable-chain latches, if you dry-fit the chain end)

Read first

  • The titanium backers go on during this chapter, not after it. Fitting them once the gantry is assembled or installed means a teardown (survey §5.2 W2). They mount on the face opposite the rail — top of the Y extrusions, rear of the X extrusion. "If you have a single MGN12 but decide to put a backer on top, you will be actively contributing to the problem of bimetallic expansion!" src
  • Do not tension the A/B belts and do not square the gantry here. Both are Ch 06/07, and the official squaring procedure begins by releasing A/B tension — tension it now and you undo it (survey §4.4 #2, §5.2 W1). Several joints in this chapter are deliberately left "slightly loose".
  • Every T-nut this chapter needs must go in before the drive and idler frames cap the extrusion ends. LDO: "Due to the tight tolerances of the extrusions and roll-in t-nuts it is advisable to either test fit before assembly … or to pre-load the t-nuts into the extrusions." src
  • Rails ship dry. If Ch 00's clean-and-pack pass has not been done, stop and do it — the flip-and-pack method needs access to the back of the rail (survey §4.4 #5).
  • Carriages slide off rails and are ruined by a drop (manual p.88, p.101). Tape or stopper every carriage the moment its rail is on an extrusion.
  • Orientation. Through p.105 the gantry is built the way it runs — motors hanging down below the bridge, Y rails underneath (p.85, p.116). p.106 turns it upside down (motors up, rails up) so the X axis can be lowered onto the Y carriages; it stays that way to the end of this chapter and is turned back in Ch 06 (Step 06.11). Every step that turns it over says so.

docs.title: Step 06.1 — Confirm the starting state
docs.text: Ch 06 › Part A — Chapter 06: Z axis (mechanical)1 / 42

docs.title: Step 06.1 — Confirm the starting state
docs.text:
Step 1 of 42 · Chapter 06 — Z axis (and Chapter 06b — Gantry squaring)

Do: Confirm: four Z drives bolted in; four Z idlers with tensioners at the upright tops; four MGN9 Z rails on the second holes from each end, carriages on and greased; the gantry on the bench with its titanium backers on.

Parts: none.

Check

Every Z carriage slides its full rail by hand, smooth, with no notchiness or gritty spots. Fix a rail that fights you now.

What you're looking at

Manual p.108–123. Nothing in this part needs power.

The frame before the gantry goes in: a Z drive at each bottom corner, a Z idler at the top of each upright, and a Z rail with a carriage on each upright. Those four carriages carry the whole gantry.

Source: Voron manual p.108

← PreviousCh 06 — before you start

Next →Step 06.2 — Learn the four names

docs.title: Step 06.10 — Park the four lower joints at a matched height
docs.text: Ch 06 › Part A — Chapter 06: Z axis (mechanical)10 / 42

docs.title: Step 06.10 — Park the four lower joints at a matched height
docs.text:
Step 10 of 42 · Chapter 06 — Z axis (and Chapter 06b — Gantry squaring)

Do:

  1. Move each Z carriage to mid-rail; screw a rubber stopper into the free rail hole directly under it.
  2. Use the same hole from the same end at all four corners.
  3. Fit a z_rail_stop_x4 at each rail top.

Parts:

  • four rubber rail stoppers off the Z rails
  • z_rail_stop_x4 ×4 (optional, from batch B05)

Check

Deck-to-joint-top height at all four corners is within ~1 mm, and each carriage stops on its rubber stopper when pushed down.

What you're looking at

A rubber rail stopper screws into a free rail hole and blocks the carriage. Screwed in directly under each lower joint it becomes a shelf, so all four joints park at the same height. The printed z_rail_stop_x4 does the same job at the rail top.

Good stopping point · ~25 min since the last one

four lower Z joints on the Z carriages and parked at a matched height. Do not attempt the gantry lift until your second person is there: the next segment is one unbroken two-person move.

Source: Voron manual p.115 · LDO Build Notes § Voron 2.4 build FAQ

← PreviousStep 06.9 — Fit the four lower Z joints to the Z carriages

Next →Step 06.11 — Turn the gantry over and stage the lift

docs.title: Step 06.11 — Turn the gantry over and stage the lift
docs.text: Ch 06 › Part A — Chapter 06: Z axis (mechanical)11 / 42

docs.title: Step 06.11 — Turn the gantry over and stage the lift
docs.text:
Step 11 of 42 · Chapter 06 — Z axis (and Chapter 06b — Gantry squaring)

Do:

  1. Turn the gantry the right way up: A/B motors down, Y rails underneath, X rail to the front.
  2. Mark Front and Back in tape on gantry and frame.
  3. Agree aloud who lifts which end.

Parts:

  • the gantry

Check

Front and back marked and matching on both parts, belt tails taped clear, both people can reach their side without leaning over the bed.

What you're looking at

The gantry back the way it runs: A/B motors hanging down below the rear extrusion, Y rails on the underside, X rail facing the front, the four Z bearing blocks at the corners with their belt tails hanging. The frame is not front-to-back symmetric.

Source: Voron manual p.113 · Voron manual p.106 · Voron manual p.116 · Video: Part 4 @1:01:50

← PreviousStep 06.10 — Park the four lower joints at a matched height

Next →Step 06.12 — Two-person lift: tilt the gantry into the frame

docs.title: Step 06.12 — Two-person lift: tilt the gantry into the frame
docs.text: Ch 06 › Part A — Chapter 06: Z axis (mechanical)12 / 42

docs.title: Step 06.12 — Two-person lift: tilt the gantry into the frame
docs.text:
Step 12 of 42 · Chapter 06 — Z axis (and Chapter 06b — Gantry squaring)

Do:

  1. Cover the bed with a towel.
  2. Two people, one per Y extrusion, hands on extrusions only.
  3. Lift from above and tilt side-to-side: one Y extrusion enters the frame first, then bring the high side down.

Parts:

  • the gantry

Check

The gantry is inside the frame, level, front to the front, each Z bearing block over its lower joint, and no belt pinched.

What you're looking at

The lift itself. The gantry will not pass the four uprights flat, so it goes in tilted and levels out inside the frame. Hands on the Y extrusions only: the X carriage, the drive units and the belts are not handles.

Source: Voron manual p.114

← PreviousStep 06.11 — Turn the gantry over and stage the lift

Next →Step 06.13 — Set the gantry down onto the lower joints

docs.title: Step 06.13 — Set the gantry down onto the lower joints
docs.text: Ch 06 › Part A — Chapter 06: Z axis (mechanical)13 / 42

docs.title: Step 06.13 — Set the gantry down onto the lower joints
docs.text:
Step 13 of 42 · Chapter 06 — Z axis (and Chapter 06b — Gantry squaring)

Do:

  1. Lower the gantry until each Z block seats on its lower joint, nudging the carriages until the bores line up.
  2. Let go one at a time.
  3. No rail stoppers? Zip-tie each corner to its upright first.

Parts:

  • the gantry
  • long zip ties ×4 only if you skipped step 06.10

Check

The gantry rests on all four joints with nobody holding it. It does not rock, and no corner is visibly lower than the others.

What you're looking at

Each Z bearing block comes down onto the domed top of its lower joint. The last millimetre should be gravity, not force: if a block will not seat, slide that carriage along its rail rather than levering the gantry.

Source: Voron manual p.114 · Video: Part 4 @1:10:15

← PreviousStep 06.12 — Two-person lift: tilt the gantry into the frame

docs.title: Step 06.14 — Bolt the first Z joint together
docs.text: Ch 06 › Part A — Chapter 06: Z axis (mechanical)14 / 42

docs.title: Step 06.14 — Bolt the first Z joint together
docs.text:
Step 14 of 42 · Chapter 06 — Z axis (and Chapter 06b — Gantry squaring)

Do: From underneath, run one M5×40 SHCS up through the lower joint's bore into the M5 nut captive in the Z bearing block. Tighten lightly only: the joint must still articulate. Final torque is Ch 14, hot, at Step 06b.16.

Parts:

  • M5×40 SHCS ×1

Check

The bolt threads in freely by hand for most of its length, and the joint still rocks slightly when you push the gantry corner.

What you're looking at

One M5×40 runs up through the lower joint's bore into the M5 nut, turning the two blocks into one Z joint. It stays light on purpose: the joint must swivel while the gantry is squared, and gets full torque once, hot, in Ch 14.

Source: Voron manual p.115

← PreviousStep 06.13 — Set the gantry down onto the lower joints

docs.title: Step 06.15 — Repeat at the other three joints
docs.text: Ch 06 › Part A — Chapter 06: Z axis (mechanical)15 / 42

docs.title: Step 06.15 — Repeat at the other three joints
docs.text:
Step 15 of 42 · Chapter 06 — Z axis (and Chapter 06b — Gantry squaring)

Do: Add the other three joints the same way. Same light tightening on all four.

Parts:

  • M5×40 SHCS ×3

Check

Four M5×40 in, all light. Lift gently under one Y extrusion: the gantry moves as one piece, all four carriages together.

What you're looking at

The other three corners, same single bolt, same lightness. With four in, the gantry is properly attached to all four Z carriages and moves as one piece up and down the uprights.

Good stopping point · ~45 min since the last one

gantry lifted into the frame and bolted to all four Z joints, articulating freely. This segment could not be broken (two-person lift). Z belts are still unrouted; leave the idlers alone.

Source: Voron manual p.116 · Video: Part 4 @1:20:06

← PreviousStep 06.14 — Bolt the first Z joint together

Next →Step 06.16 — Extend all four Z idlers

docs.title: Step 06.16 — Extend all four Z idlers
docs.text: Ch 06 › Part A — Chapter 06: Z axis (mechanical)16 / 42

docs.title: Step 06.16 — Extend all four Z idlers
docs.text:
Step 16 of 42 · Chapter 06 — Z axis (and Chapter 06b — Gantry squaring)

Do:

  1. The tensioner is the M3×16 under the orange slider, 2.5 mm key from below.
  2. Loosen it anticlockwise from below, out to the maximum before it comes undone.
  3. Tighten back 4 turns. Repeat on all four idlers.

Parts:

  • none (the four [a]_z_tensioner_9mm_x4 fitted in Ch 02)

Check

All four idlers extended and backed off by the same 4 turns, counted out loud, with none of the four bolts fallen out.

What you're looking at

The Z idler is the toothed pulley on a sliding bracket at the top of each upright. Its bolt is the tensioner: it moves the pulley, changing how much belt the loop needs. The same four turns back parks all four identically.

Source: Voron manual p.117

← PreviousStep 06.15 — Repeat at the other three joints

Next →Step 06.17 — Loosen the four top belt clamps

docs.title: Step 06.17 — Loosen the four top belt clamps
docs.text: Ch 06 › Part A — Chapter 06: Z axis (mechanical)17 / 42

docs.title: Step 06.17 — Loosen the four top belt clamps
docs.text:
Step 17 of 42 · Chapter 06 — Z axis (and Chapter 06b — Gantry squaring)

Do: At each corner, back off the M3×30 and M5×30 just far enough to slide the second belt end in under the top clip. Do not undo them completely: they also hold the lower clamp. One corner at a time.

Parts: none.

Check

A strip of belt slips between top clip and block at all four corners, and no lower belt tail pulls out.

What you're looking at

The upper clip is where the belt's second end gets clamped, so its two screws must open enough to admit a belt. The same two screws hold the lower clip and the end already in it, so loosen one corner at a time.

Source: Voron manual p.117

← PreviousStep 06.16 — Extend all four Z idlers

Next →Step 06.18 — Route the first belt down and around the Z drive

docs.title: Step 06.18 — Route the first belt down and around the Z drive
docs.text: Ch 06 › Part A — Chapter 06: Z axis (mechanical)18 / 42

docs.title: Step 06.18 — Route the first belt down and around the Z drive
docs.text:
Step 18 of 42 · Chapter 06 — Z axis (and Chapter 06b — Gantry squaring)

Do: Take the belt tail down past the lower Z joint on the rail side, around the Z drive pulley, and back up the run further from the rail. Teeth face inward, onto the pulley. Needle-nose pliers help.

Parts:

  • the belt tail at one corner

Check

The belt seats fully round the drive pulley, and teeth face each other between the two runs; teeth showing outside means a twist.

What you're looking at

The belt tail runs down the rail side of the upright and wraps the toothed pulley in the Z drive, the pulley that lifts this corner. Teeth face inward so they engage; a belt running smooth-side-on over a toothed pulley skips teeth.

Source: Voron manual p.118 · Video: Part 4 @1:30:31

← PreviousStep 06.17 — Loosen the four top belt clamps

Next →Step 06.19 — Take the belt up and over the Z idler

docs.title: Step 06.19 — Take the belt up and over the Z idler
docs.text: Ch 06 › Part A — Chapter 06: Z axis (mechanical)19 / 42

docs.title: Step 06.19 — Take the belt up and over the Z idler
docs.text:
Step 19 of 42 · Chapter 06 — Z axis (and Chapter 06b — Gantry squaring)

Do: Run the belt up the far run to the top of the upright, over the Z idler pulley, and back down the rail side toward the Z joint. Teeth stay on the inside of the loop.

Parts:

  • the same belt

Check

The belt sits centred in the idler's groove between its flanges, and both runs are vertical and clear of the extrusion.

What you're looking at

The same belt continues up the run further from the rail, over the Z idler, and back down on the rail side toward the joint, closing the loop. The idler's flanges are all that keep the belt on it.

Source: Voron manual p.119

← PreviousStep 06.18 — Route the first belt down and around the Z drive

Next →Step 06.20 — Clamp the second end and pull it tight

docs.title: Step 06.2 — Learn the four names
docs.text: Ch 06 › Part A — Chapter 06: Z axis (mechanical)2 / 42

docs.title: Step 06.2 — Learn the four names
docs.text:
Step 2 of 42 · Chapter 06 — Z axis (and Chapter 06b — Gantry squaring)

Do: Learn the stack at one corner: the Z drive at the bottom, the Z joint above it, the Z belt between them, and the Z idler at the top. Both ends of each belt terminate at its Z joint.

Parts: none.

Check

You can point at all four features on the real machine at the front-left corner before you build the other three.

What you're looking at

One corner, top to bottom: the Z idler at the top of the upright, the Z joint that clamps the belt and carries the gantry corner, the Z belt, and the Z drive at the bottom. Four of these lift and level the gantry.

Source: Voron manual p.109 · Video: Part 4 @0:55:46

← PreviousStep 06.1 — Confirm the starting state

Next →Step 06.3 — Seat an M5 nut in each Z bearing block

docs.title: Step 06.20 — Clamp the second end and pull it tight
docs.text: Ch 06 › Part A — Chapter 06: Z axis (mechanical)20 / 42

docs.title: Step 06.20 — Clamp the second end and pull it tight
docs.text:
Step 20 of 42 · Chapter 06 — Z axis (and Chapter 06b — Gantry squaring)

Do: Feed the returning belt end between the block and the loosened top clip, teeth against the block's serrations. Pull the tail hard and hold it while you tighten the M3 and then the M5, firm rather than crushed.

Parts:

  • M3×30 SHCS and M5×30 BHCS at this corner (already in place)

Check

The long run plucks with real tension, not a floppy note; the tail does not slip and the lower belt end is still clamped.

What you're looking at

The returning end feeds in under the upper clip against the block's serrations, as the first end did under the lower clip. Pulling hard on the tail while you tighten takes the slack out of the loop; the tensioner only fine-tunes what is left.

Source: Voron manual p.120 · Video: Part 5 @0:47:55

← PreviousStep 06.19 — Take the belt up and over the Z idler

Next →Step 06.21 — Trim, fold and tie the excess

docs.title: Step 06.21 — Trim, fold and tie the excess
docs.text: Ch 06 › Part A — Chapter 06: Z axis (mechanical)21 / 42

docs.title: Step 06.21 — Trim, fold and tie the excess
docs.text:
Step 21 of 42 · Chapter 06 — Z axis (and Chapter 06b — Gantry squaring)

Do: Fold the tail back on itself and zip-tie it to the running belt. Leave enough tail to re-clamp once if the tension comes out wrong, so do not cut it flush yet. Trim the zip-tie tail flush.

Parts:

  • zip tie, 3×150 mm ×1

Check

The folded tail cannot flap into a pulley or panel, and nothing rubs as you move the gantry by hand.

What you're looking at

The leftover belt past the clamp. Folded back and zip-tied it cannot flap into a pulley or a panel; left long rather than cut flush, it gives you one free re-clamp if the tension comes out wrong.

Good stopping point · ~40 min since the last one

all four Z idlers extended, top clamps loosened, and the first Z belt routed, clamped at both ends, trimmed and tied. Never stop with a belt half-routed: finish the corner you are on.

Source: Voron manual p.120

← PreviousStep 06.20 — Clamp the second end and pull it tight

Next →Step 06.22 — Do the other three Z belts

docs.title: Step 06.22 — Do the other three Z belts
docs.text: Ch 06 › Part A — Chapter 06: Z axis (mechanical)22 / 42

docs.title: Step 06.22 — Do the other three Z belts
docs.text:
Step 22 of 42 · Chapter 06 — Z axis (and Chapter 06b — Gantry squaring)

Do: Repeat steps 06.18–06.21 at each of the remaining three corners. Do them in the same order every time, drive then idler then clamp, so you notice if one comes out different.

Parts:

  • the remaining three belts, 3× zip tie

Check

Four belts on, four tails tied. Every belt is fully seated on its drive pulley and its idler.

What you're looking at

The other three corners, the same four operations each. Doing them in the same order every time is how you notice a corner that came out different, rather than discovering it as a QGL that will not converge.

Good stopping point · ~30 min since the last one

all four Z belts routed, clamped, trimmed and tied. Belts are hand-even but not tensioned; do not touch the A/B front-idler tension screws (Ch 07's).

Source: Voron manual p.121

← PreviousStep 06.21 — Trim, fold and tie the excess

Next →Step 06.23 — Even the four belts by hand

docs.title: Step 06.23 — Even the four belts by hand
docs.text: Ch 06 › Part A — Chapter 06: Z axis (mechanical)23 / 42

docs.title: Step 06.23 — Even the four belts by hand
docs.text:
Step 23 of 42 · Chapter 06 — Z axis (and Chapter 06b — Gantry squaring)

Do:

  1. Pluck each Z belt on the short run between the top belt clip and the Z idler.
  2. Bring the four notes together with each corner's Z idler tensioner bolt: 2.5 mm key from below, clockwise for tighter.

Parts: none.

Check

All four belts sound within a semitone of each other, and lifting one gantry corner moves all four carriages together.

What you're looking at

The Z idler tensioner: the small bolt standing proud below the idler. Plucking a belt is a rough tension reading, and the four Z belts must be close to equal or QGL will not repeat. The measured 140 Hz target waits for Part B.

Tip

The CAD idler height is the 250 machine's. There is one of these at each of the four corners either way.

Source: Voron manual p.121 · Voron docs § Secondary printer tuning — A/B and Z belts · CAD: Voron 2.4r2 STEP @ de7e89d
