docs.title: Step 07.5 — Set both front-idler tensioners
docs.text:
Step 5 of 39 · Chapter 07 — A/B belts and tensioning

Do:

  1. Back each M3×40 out until the tension arm is at its slackest end of travel.
  2. Wind it back in exactly 4 turns. Count the turns and give both idlers the same number.

Parts:

  • the two M3×40 SHCS + M3 washers already in the front idlers (Ch 04, p.67 and p.71)

Check

Both tensioner screws stand proud of the front idler bodies by the same amount, with travel left in both directions.

What you're looking at

The front-idler tensioners are the two orange parts at the front; each carries an M3×40 whose job is belt tension. Winding it in pulls the idler forward and tightens that belt, backing it out releases it. A handed pair: 45×25 mm and 25×45 mm.

Good stopping point · ~25 min since the last one

both belt paths traced against p.126–127 and both front-idler tensioners backed out to the loose starting position. Nothing is cut. Do not start cutting belt unless you can also thread it.

docs.title: Step 07.6 — Fit the heat-set inserts and M3 nuts
docs.text:
Step 6 of 39 · Chapter 07 — A/B belts and tensioning

Do:

  1. If the inserts went in during the Ch 00 pass, verify them. Otherwise set all four flush with the plastic, square to the face.
  2. Press the two M3 nuts into their pockets in the right carriage half.

Parts:

  • M3 heat-set insert ×4 (1 per X carriage half, 2 in the probe retainer bracket)
  • M3 nut ×2 (both in the right X carriage half)

Check

Inserts flush and square; nuts fully seated with no gap behind them; an M3 screw starts by hand in every insert.

What you're looking at

A heat-set insert is a knurled brass sleeve melted into the plastic so a steel screw has metal threads to bite into. Four go in here: one per X carriage half, two in the probe retainer bracket. The halves are a handed pair.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: "If you are building Clockwork 2 double-check that you have the correct X-Carriage and follow the instructions in the Stealthburner manual." For this kit that is the pair x_frame_V2TR_MGN12_left / x_frame_V2TR_MGN12_right — the R2 / Clockwork-2 halves, not the Afterburner ones. Confirm the filenames against what you actually printed before the belts go in. src (p.129–130)

docs.title: Step 07.7 — Set the two carriage stop screws to 3 mm
docs.text:
Step 7 of 39 · Chapter 07 — A/B belts and tensioning

Do: Thread one M3×12 into the heat-set insert in each carriage half, from the face shown, until 3 mm stands proud of the plastic. Measure with the caliper depth blade or a rule.

Parts:

  • M3×12 SHCS ×2

Check

Both screws at 3 mm ±0.5 mm, and the same on both halves.

What you're looking at

These two M3×12 are stop screws rather than fasteners. The 3 mm of thread standing proud of each half sets how the two halves meet over the belt, so the two must match each other as well as the number.

Source: Voron manual p.130

docs.title: Step 07.8 — Cut both belts to the same length
docs.text: Ch 07 › Cut and clamp8 / 39

docs.title: Step 07.8 — Cut both belts to the same length
docs.text:
Step 8 of 39 · Chapter 07 — A/B belts and tensioning

(no image — see text)

Do:

  1. Measure 2000 mm from the free end and fold the belt back there.
  2. Lay the doubled belt flat and cut through both layers at the fold, square across.
  3. Cut the reel side level with the free end.

Parts:

  • Gates 2GT 6 mm open belt, 2 lengths

Check

Both belts side by side against a square edge: the far ends flush. About 100 mm of tail reaches each clamp (verify on bench).

What you're looking at

No picture, and the most consequential measurement in the chapter. Both belt paths are the same length by design, so two belts of identical length arrive at identical tension. A few millimetres of difference is a permanent imbalance the tensioners cannot remove.

Tip

Mark one belt A with a dot on the smooth back near each end: it goes into the upper slot. Once both are threaded they are impossible to tell apart.

Tip

Nervous? Cut one belt generously at 2100 mm, route it as A, trim its tail, then cut the second to match. The 6.21 m reel leaves ~2 m spare.

Good stopping point · ~30 min since the last one

heat-set inserts and M3 nuts in the carriage halves, stop screws set to 3 mm, both belts cut to matched length and marked A and B. Coil the two belts and bag them; the next segment is the one that cannot be broken.

Source: Voron manual p.125 · LDO 350 Rev D BOM · LDO Build Notes § Voron 2.4 build FAQ · onetwo3D Voron 2.4 350 BOM

docs.title: Step 07.9 — Clamp the first end of both belts in the left carriage half

Step 9 of 39 · Chapter 07 — A/B belts and tensioning

Do:

  1. Feed belt A into the upper slot of the left carriage part, B into the lower, teeth away from the extrusion on both.
  2. Install it against the rail carriage and run the two M3×8 SHCS in, snug only.

Parts:

  • M3×8 SHCS ×2
  • both belts

Both ends captured and immovable under a firm tug, the A mark in the upper slot, teeth facing the same way, neither belt twisted.

What you're looking at

The X carriage clamps a belt by squeezing it between its two printed halves. Both belts' first ends go into the left half, one upper, one lower. The upper slot is A, whose pulley and idler sit 10 mm higher than B's.

docs.title: Checkpoint 07
docs.text: Ch 07Checkpoint

docs.title: Checkpoint 07
docs.text:
Checkpoint · Chapter 07 — A/B belts and tensioning

What you should have now — The A and B belt loops threaded through both idler stacks and closed at the X carriage, plus the inductive probe and the A/B drive cable cover. The CAD belt loops are the 250 lengths and the only thing on this picture that is size-dependent. Cut yours to Chapter 07 Step 07.8, never to this render.
  • Both belts routed to match p.126 (A) and p.127 (B); each belt stays in one plane, neither crosses the other.
  • No half-twist anywhere; belt teeth face away from the extrusion at the X carriage; each belt's toothed face stays on the same side all the way round.
  • Teeth meshed on both toothed motor pulleys — each pulley indexes when the belt is nudged, no slip — and on the two XY-joint toothed idlers (A at the right joint, B at the left); smooth back on every plain stack.
  • Belt not riding on any printed part at any of the ten contacts (six locations), checked at both ends of X travel and both ends of Y travel (p.142).
  • Equal length of belt protruding from the X carriage on both belts, after moving the gantry and returning (p.141).
  • Carriage bolts and all four M3×8 belt clamps fully tightened; nothing slips under a hard pull.
  • Both belts read within a few Hz of each other at ~110 Hz over a 150 mm span, re-checked after moving the gantry — provisional; Ch 14 Step 14.4 sets the final value.
  • Gantry moves through the full XY envelope by hand with even resistance, no ticking, no notchiness.
  • Probe insulated (front + sides only), fitted, wires cut to ~150 mm, tip 6 mm below the plastic, cable in its channel.
  • No hall-effect magnet fitted (p.145 skipped).

← PreviousStep 07.39 — Fit the A/B drive cable cover

Next →Ch 08 — before you start

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Tensioning to final now. Ch 06b releases A/B tension completely as its first move, and it cannot run until the printer is alive (Ch 13); the final value is Ch 14 Step 14.4 — cold, door open, just before the 14.6 soak. Set ~110 Hz, confirm A ≈ B, move on. Chasing the last 5 Hz here is time you will spend again.
  • Cutting the second belt after the first is installed. Any length error becomes a permanent tension imbalance you will try to fix with the tensioners, which cannot fix it. Cut both together against a square edge (Step 07.8).
  • Wrapping the wrong element of a rear drive unit. Each drive unit holds the motor pulley for its own belt and an idler stack for the other belt. Putting the A belt on the B motor pulley looks plausible and locks the two axes together. The p.126 top-left and p.127 top-right insets show which is which.
  • A half-twist in a long run. It shows up as a belt that runs fine at one end of travel and rubs at the other. Sight down each straight run and confirm the teeth face the same way at both ends.
  • "Fixing" the teeth-on turn at an XY joint with a half-twist. Each belt meets one toothed idler at the XY joints — A at the right joint (Step 07.16), B at the left (Step 07.17) — and wraps it teeth-on by design. A twist put in to get the smooth back there walks the belt off a flange at the far end of travel.
  • Reading a harmonic on the phone. Spectrum apps show peaks at 2× and 3× the fundamental; 220 Hz reads as "too tight" and sends you loosening a correctly tensioned belt. Take the lowest peak, and take three plucks.
  • Forcing a belt round a bearing stack. You will damage the flange or unseat a bearing. At a front idler, pull the M3×40 SHCS, thread the belt, refit and redo Step 07.5 (Step 07.15, p.134). A drive unit or XY joint has no such screw — find what is fouling instead.

inductive probe insulated, fitted, set to height and its cable routed; endstop magnet correctly skipped; A/B cable cover on. Gantry is a working XY system. Do not tension further and do not square the gantry.

docs.title: Before you start Chapter 07
docs.text: Ch 07Before you start

docs.title: Before you start Chapter 07
docs.text:
Before you start · Chapter 07 — A/B belts and tensioning

Cut, route and clamp the two CoreXY belts, set a provisional tension, and finish the X carriage with the inductive probe. This makes the gantry a working XY motion system — everything after it (toolhead, wiring, bring-up) assumes the belts are on.

What you're building in this chapter. Two belt loops and the printed carriage that clamps them. In CoreXY neither motor owns an axis: the rear-right motor drives the A belt, the rear-left drives the B belt, and the toolhead moves in X when both turn the same way and in Y when they turn opposite ways. Each belt is one long loop that starts and ends at the X carriage, and on a Voron the two loops sit at different heights and never cross — each stays in its own horizontal plane the whole way round. Where a belt has to be driven it wraps a toothed motor pulley teeth-first; everywhere it is merely turned, it runs smooth-side-on over a plain bearing stack — except at the XY joints, where each belt meets one toothed 20T idler and one plain F695 pair: A rides the left joint's upper plain stack and the right joint's upper toothed idler; B rides the left joint's lower toothed idler and the right joint's lower plain stack (p.105, p.135, p.136, p.138). Whether a face is teeth-on is fixed by which joint and which height — never twist a belt to change it. The A belt is the upper of the two planes, B the lower. Both belts start in the left carriage half and leave it heading left, so A's first turn is on the left joint's plain stack and B's first turn is on the left joint's toothed idler. Both loops are the same length by design, so two belts cut identical arrive at identical tension — and no amount of tensioner adjustment can undo a length error, which is why they are cut together and their protruding tails measured against each other at the carriage. The chapter finishes by fitting the inductive probe that later levels the gantry and maps the bed.

Time: 2.5–4.0 h hands-on, first build (survey §5.1 P07 / §7.2 Ch 07).

Sessions: 5 × ~30 min (first-build estimate; each Pause: line carries its own segment minutes — note that segment 3, threading both belts, cannot be broken and needs ~80 min in one sitting — there is a soft stop after Step 07.16 if you must).

Prerequisites:

  • Ch 04 (A/B drives and front idlers assembled, motor pulley set screws threadlocked), Ch 05 (gantry, XY joints, X carriage on the rail, Ti backers), Ch 06 Part A (gantry installed on the Z joints, Z belts clamped).
  • Print batches B02 (accent: [a]_tensioner_left/right, [a]_cable_cover), B03 (front idlers), B04 (XY joints + X carriage + probe_retainer_bracket).
  • The gantry must move freely by hand over its full travel with no belts on. Fix binding now, not after belting.

Tools

  • Ball-end hex 2.0 mm and 2.5 mm
  • Needle-nose pliers and tweezers (belt threading; the manual calls these out on p.132)
  • Flush cutters or sharp scissors for belt; steel rule or tape ≥ 2.2 m; 150 mm steel rule for the tension span; marker
  • Phone with a spectrum app: Spectroid (Android), Sound Spectrum Analysis (iOS), or Gates Carbon Drive (both — use the "motorcycle" option) (Voron tuning docs)
  • Temperature-controlled soldering iron + M3 brass tip, only if the heat-set inserts on p.129 were not done in the Ch 00 insert pass

Printed parts

Parts arrive in the bins named below (see the bin map in print/README.md#bins); check the bin label's list before you start.

Looks like STL Bin Qty Colour Gantry/X_Axis/X_Carriage/x_frame_V2TR_MGN12_left 07-X 1 Black Gantry/X_Axis/X_Carriage/x_frame_V2TR_MGN12_right 07-X 1 Black Gantry/X_Axis/X_Carriage/probe_retainer_bracket 07-X 1 Black Gantry/Front_Idlers/[a]_tensioner_left 04-B 1 Orange — fitted in Ch 04, adjusted here Gantry/Front_Idlers/[a]_tensioner_right 04-A 1 Orange — fitted in Ch 04, adjusted here Gantry/AB_Drive_Units/[a]_cable_cover 07-X 1 Orange

Hardware (chapter totals)

Fastener / part Qty Where Gates 2GT open belt, 6 mm wide 2 lengths, cut equal A and B belts (p.125, p.131 — see Step 07.8) M3×8 SHCS 4 belt clamps, 2 per X carriage half (p.131, p.140) M3×12 SHCS 2 1 per X carriage half, set to 3 mm protrusion (p.130) M3×30 SHCS 4 2 carriage bolts (p.140) + 2 probe retainer bracket (p.143) M3 nut 2 right X carriage half, capture the M3×30 carriage bolts (p.129) M3 heat-set insert 4 1 per X carriage half + 2 in probe_retainer_bracket (p.129) M3×40 SHCS + M3 washer 2 + 2 front-idler tensioners — already fitted in Ch 04 (p.67, p.71); adjusted on p.128, temporarily removable on p.134 Inductive probe, Omron TL-Q5MC 1 X carriage (p.143) Fibreglass tape (LDO-supplied) as needed probe insulation, front + sides only (LDO note p.143)

Read first

  • The tension you set here is provisional. Gantry squaring (Ch 06b) begins by fully releasing A/B belt tension, and it needs a running printer (G28, QUAD_GANTRY_LEVEL, SET_STEPPER_ENABLE), so it happens inside Ch 13. Set enough tension to home and QGL. A/B tension is set three times on purpose: Ch 07 (provisional — enough to home and QGL), Ch 06b Step 06b.15 (provisional again, after squaring, cold and open) and Ch 14 Step 14.4 (final — panels on, cold, door open, immediately before the closed-chamber soak and hot Z-joint tighten of 14.6). Z belts: 06b.3 (so QGL converges for squaring), set for the last time at 14.5, same cold session. Ch 14 owns the final number; tensioning to final now just gets undone — that is survey §5.2 W1, a ~1.5 h rework.
  • Equal length is the whole trick. Both belt paths are the same length by design, so if the two belts are cut identical, equal tension follows (p.125). Cut them together, not one after the other.
  • There is no sourced deflection number. The official manual gives no tension figure at all — only the equal-length rule. The one sourced number in this build's document set is 110 Hz over a 150 mm span (Voron secondary tuning). voronldo.com's 80–100 Hz is discarded (survey §4.3). Do not substitute a "push it 2 mm with your finger" test — nothing here calibrates it.
  • Nothing in this chapter is torqued. Belt clamps and carriage bolts go on lightly, the belts get pulled tight by hand, then the carriage bolts are fully tightened (p.140–141). The manual specifies no torque values; don't invent one.
  • Three LDO deviations land in this page range: the X-carriage variant check (p.129–130), probe insulation (p.143), and p.145 skipped entirely.
  • The inductive probe is built once, here. Insulation, fitting, the 6 mm height and the cable route are Steps 07.34–07.37 (manual p.143–144). Ch 08 does not touch the probe again — it only confirms the decision and bags the Klicky set. The probe_retainer_bracket and the fibreglass tape are counted in this chapter's totals, not Ch 08's.

docs.title: Step 08.1 — Sort the printed parts and confirm the hotend code
docs.text: Ch 08 › A — Part preparation and heat-set inserts1 / 65

docs.title: Step 08.1 — Sort the printed parts and confirm the hotend code
docs.text:
Step 1 of 65 · Chapter 08 — Toolhead: Stealthburner, Clockwork 2, Revo HF, Nitehawk-SB V2

Do:

  1. Lay the parts out in build order; bag the Klicky set aside.
  2. Read the code on both printhead halves: it must say E-RV, E3D Revo Voron.
  3. Confirm the rear half is the _rear_cw2 variant, circled corner solid.

Parts:

  • all B02 and B06 toolhead prints
  • the two revo_voron printhead halves

Check

E-RV on both halves, and the circled corner of the rear half is closed. A different printhead folder means reprinting.

What you're looking at

Stealthburner is the toolhead: a shroud carrying two fans and three LEDs around a removable tool cartridge that holds the hotend. The two printhead halves are that cartridge; their moulded code says which hotend they fit. CW1 variants have the circled corner cut open.

Tip

the revo_voron folder is the settled choice for this kit; the SB printhead README maps "E3D Revo Voron → E-RV". src

Source: SB manual p.37

docs.title: Step 08.10 — Close the guidler arm
docs.text: Ch 08 › B — Clockwork 2 extruder10 / 65

docs.title: Step 08.10 — Close the guidler arm
docs.text:
Step 10 of 65 · Chapter 08 — Toolhead: Stealthburner, Clockwork 2, Revo HF, Nitehawk-SB V2

Do: Join the two guidler halves with one M3×16 SHCS, p.16. Slide the greased idler assembly from 08.9 into the arm from the side, in the orientation p.17 circles: toothed face toward the filament path. Snug only.

Parts:

  • [a]_guidler_a ×1, [a]_guidler_b ×1, M3×16 SHCS ×1, the idler assembly from 08.9

Check

The idler spins freely in the closed arm. The two halves meet with no gap.

What you're looking at

The guidler is the swinging arm that carries the idler: two orange halves joined by a single M3×16 on p.16, with the idler assembly sliding into the joined arm on its own shaft on p.17.

Source: SB manual p.16

← PreviousStep 08.9 — Build the BMG idler assembly and grease it

Next →Step 08.11 — Fit the latch shuttle and the BMG thumbscrew assembly

docs.title: Step 08.11 — Fit the latch shuttle and the BMG thumbscrew assembly
docs.text: Ch 08 › B — Clockwork 2 extruder11 / 65

docs.title: Step 08.11 — Fit the latch shuttle and the BMG thumbscrew assembly
docs.text:
Step 11 of 65 · Chapter 08 — Toolhead: Stealthburner, Clockwork 2, Revo HF, Nitehawk-SB V2

Do: Seat the latch shuttle on top of the guidler's boss, hook facing the latch side, p.18 right. Slide the spring then the washer onto the thumbscrew, pass it through the boss and thread it into the shuttle's insert.

Parts:

  • [a]_latch_shuttle ×1 (insert from 08.5), Thumb Screw Kit — thumbscrew ×1, spring ×1, washer ×1

Check

The shuttle is captive and draws against the spring by hand. The spring measures roughly 12 mm long, 6 mm OD, 1 mm wire.

What you're looking at

The thumbscrew, spring and washer are the extruder's grip adjustment; the latch shuttle is what they thread into. Winding the thumbscrew in compresses the spring and pushes the guidler arm, and so the idler, harder onto the filament.

Tip

a substitute spring of the wrong size changes the tension curve and prints badly; source the Bondtech part before continuing.

Source: SB manual p.18

← PreviousStep 08.10 — Close the guidler arm

Next →Step 08.12 — Seat the first MR85 in the motor plate

docs.title: Step 08.12 — Seat the first MR85 in the motor plate
docs.text: Ch 08 › B — Clockwork 2 extruder12 / 65

docs.title: Step 08.12 — Seat the first MR85 in the motor plate
docs.text:
Step 12 of 65 · Chapter 08 — Toolhead: Stealthburner, Clockwork 2, Revo HF, Nitehawk-SB V2

Do: Press the MR85 fully into its plastic pocket, even pressure on the outer ring only. Never push on the inner ring. If it needs real force the part is over-extruded: check the print rather than hammering it.

Parts:

  • motor_plate.stl, MR85 bearing ×1 (of 2)

Check

The bearing face is flush with the pocket floor and spins freely.

What you're looking at

An MR85 is a small ball bearing, 5 mm bore and 8 mm outside; two of them carry the extruder's drive shaft, one in each printed half. Pressing on the inner ring drives load through the balls and dents the races.

Source: SB manual p.19

← PreviousStep 08.11 — Fit the latch shuttle and the BMG thumbscrew assembly

Next →Step 08.13 — Check the drive shaft slides through both bearings

docs.title: Step 08.13 — Check the drive shaft slides through both bearings
docs.text: Ch 08 › B — Clockwork 2 extruder13 / 65

docs.title: Step 08.13 — Check the drive shaft slides through both bearings
docs.text:
Step 13 of 65 · Chapter 08 — Toolhead: Stealthburner, Clockwork 2, Revo HF, Nitehawk-SB V2

Do: The bearings must slip on and off the shaft by hand so the gear can self-centre. Pressing a bearing onto the shaft destroys it. If either is tight, lightly sand the shaft: a few passes, then re-test.

Parts:

  • Bondtech drive shaft, both MR85 bearings, fine sandpaper (supplied)

Check

Each bearing slides on and off with fingertip force and no rocking.

What you're looking at

The drive shaft carries the filament drive gear and the 50 T gear the motor's pinion turns. The bearings must be a slide fit on it, not a press fit, so the gear train can find its own centre.

Source: SB manual p.19

← PreviousStep 08.12 — Seat the first MR85 in the motor plate

Next →Step 08.14 — Seat the second MR85 in the main body and lock it

docs.title: Step 08.14 — Seat the second MR85 in the main body and lock it
docs.text: Ch 08 › B — Clockwork 2 extruder14 / 65

docs.title: Step 08.14 — Seat the second MR85 in the main body and lock it
docs.text:
Step 14 of 65 · Chapter 08 — Toolhead: Stealthburner, Clockwork 2, Revo HF, Nitehawk-SB V2

Do: Press the second MR85 into the main-body pocket, outer ring only. Then put a small drop of medium-strength threadlocker on the M3×6 FHCS and drive it into the retaining position shown.

Parts:

  • main_body.stl, MR85 bearing ×1, M3×6 FHCS ×1, threadlocker

Check

Bearing flush and free; the flat head sits level in its countersink.

What you're looking at

The second MR85, this time in the main body, plus one countersunk screw to retain it. Threadlocker rather than more torque: the screw goes into printed plastic, and vibration, not slackness, is what would otherwise back it out.

Source: SB manual p.20

← PreviousStep 08.13 — Check the drive shaft slides through both bearings

Next →Step 08.15 — Set the drive gear at its initial position and threadlock it

docs.title: Step 08.15 — Set the drive gear at its initial position and threadlock it
docs.text: Ch 08 › B — Clockwork 2 extruder15 / 65

docs.title: Step 08.15 — Set the drive gear at its initial position and threadlock it
docs.text:
Step 15 of 65 · Chapter 08 — Toolhead: Stealthburner, Clockwork 2, Revo HF, Nitehawk-SB V2

Do:

  1. Read SB p.21–24 first.
  2. Slide the drive gear on, set screw on the shaft's machined notch, to the 15.6 mm p.21 dimension.
  3. Apply threadlocker and tighten the set screw carefully; its head strips easily.

Parts:

  • Bondtech filament drive gear, 50T gear, drive shaft, caliper, threadlocker

Check

Caliper reads 15.6 mm at the dimensioned face, and the set screw is on the notch, not the round. Step 08.18 corrects it.

What you're looking at

The filament drive gear is the toothed wheel that pushes the filament; 15.6 mm is where its teeth line up with the filament path. Its set screw must land on the flat machined into the shaft, not the round, or it creeps.

Source: SB manual p.21

← PreviousStep 08.14 — Seat the second MR85 in the main body and lock it

Next →Step 08.16 — Drop the drive assembly into the main body

docs.title: Step 08.16 — Drop the drive assembly into the main body
docs.text: Ch 08 › B — Clockwork 2 extruder16 / 65

docs.title: Step 08.16 — Drop the drive assembly into the main body
docs.text:
Step 16 of 65 · Chapter 08 — Toolhead: Stealthburner, Clockwork 2, Revo HF, Nitehawk-SB V2

Do: Lower the shaft-and-gears assembly into the main body so the shaft enters the MR85 you fitted in 08.14 and the 50T gear sits in its chamber.

Parts:

  • drive assembly from 08.15, main_body.stl

Check

The shaft turns by hand with only bearing drag. No gear rubs the plastic.

What you're looking at

Shaft, drive gear and 50 T gear go into the main body as one assembly, the shaft picking up the bearing from 08.14. Everything turns on bearing drag alone; a gear touching plastic wears a groove and adds permanent load.

Source: SB manual p.22

← PreviousStep 08.15 — Set the drive gear at its initial position and threadlock it

Next →Step 08.17 — Close the extruder with the motor plate

docs.title: Step 08.17 — Close the extruder with the motor plate
docs.text: Ch 08 › B — Clockwork 2 extruder17 / 65

docs.title: Step 08.17 — Close the extruder with the motor plate
docs.text:
Step 17 of 65 · Chapter 08 — Toolhead: Stealthburner, Clockwork 2, Revo HF, Nitehawk-SB V2

Do: Bring the motor plate onto the main body so the shaft picks up its second MR85, then fit two M3×25 SHCS. Tighten until the parts meet, then stop. Tightened past that, the plastic bends and cracks.

Parts:

  • motor_plate.stl (from 08.12), M3×25 SHCS ×2

Check

No visible gap at the parting line and no stress whitening at either bolt boss. The shaft still turns freely.

What you're looking at

The motor plate closes the extruder and picks up the shaft's second bearing. The manual's warning is exact: these two M3×25 pull two printed parts together, and past the point where they actually meet you are bending plastic rather than tightening a joint.

Source: SB manual p.23

← PreviousStep 08.16 — Drop the drive assembly into the main body

Next →Step 08.18 — Verify drive-gear alignment with real filament

docs.title: Step 08.18 — Verify drive-gear alignment with real filament
docs.text: Ch 08 › B — Clockwork 2 extruder18 / 65

docs.title: Step 08.18 — Verify drive-gear alignment with real filament
docs.text:
Step 18 of 65 · Chapter 08 — Toolhead: Stealthburner, Clockwork 2, Revo HF, Nitehawk-SB V2

Do:

  1. Push filament down the path: it must land on the gear's toothed section, not the shoulder.
  2. If off, loosen the set screw, nudge the gear, re-check, re-tighten.
  3. Sand the shaft end face if it stands proud.

Parts:

  • a 100 mm offcut of 1.75 mm filament

Check

Filament centres on the gear teeth; the shaft end sits at or below the plastic surface when fully seated.

What you're looking at

A live check with real filament, because the 15.6 mm figure is only a starting point. The filament must land on the drive gear's toothed band, not on the smooth shoulder either side; a gear a millimetre out grips only intermittently.

Good stopping point · ~30 min since the last one

the drive train is closed between the main body and the motor plate, and threadlocker is curing on the drive-gear set screw and on the M3×6 FHCS. Do not re-open the set screw or work the drive gear against a tight spot while the threadlocker sets; the motor is not on yet, so nothing is under load.

Source: SB manual p.24

← PreviousStep 08.17 — Close the extruder with the motor plate

Next →Step 08.19 — Hang the tension arm — and leave it loose

docs.title: Step 08.19 — Hang the tension arm — and leave it loose
docs.text: Ch 08 › B — Clockwork 2 extruder19 / 65

docs.title: Step 08.19 — Hang the tension arm — and leave it loose
docs.text:
Step 19 of 65 · Chapter 08 — Toolhead: Stealthburner, Clockwork 2, Revo HF, Nitehawk-SB V2

Do: Locate the guidler/tension arm on its pivot and pass one M3×25 SHCS through. Do not tighten it. This bolt is a hinge pin; torquing it locks the arm and kills filament tensioning.

Parts:

  • guidler assembly from 08.10, M3×25 SHCS ×1

Check

The arm swings through its full travel under finger pressure and falls back under spring load.

What you're looking at

The tension arm's M3×25 is a hinge pin, not a fastener. Tightened, the arm cannot swing and the extruder cannot tension filament at all; left loose, the arm swings and the spring does the work it was fitted for.

Source: SB manual p.25

← PreviousStep 08.18 — Verify drive-gear alignment with real filament

Next →Step 08.20 — Fit the latch

docs.title: Step 08.2 — Snap the built-in supports out of the Stealthburner body
docs.text: Ch 08 › A — Part preparation and heat-set inserts2 / 65

docs.title: Step 08.2 — Snap the built-in supports out of the Stealthburner body
docs.text:
Step 2 of 65 · Chapter 08 — Toolhead: Stealthburner, Clockwork 2, Revo HF, Nitehawk-SB V2

Do: Snap the three built-in supports SB p.45 highlights out of the orange main body, using flush cutters: pry and break, do not carve. Leave the fan-cavity supports alone; SB p.52 says those break when the fans go in.

Parts:

  • [a]_stealthburner_main_body ×1

Check

The LED pockets, diffuser channels and the two mounting bores are clear. The fan cavities still have their thin support webs in place.

What you're looking at

The orange body is the Stealthburner shroud itself, carrying the LEDs, air ducts and both fans. It prints with sacrificial support inside. The webs across the fan cavities are the exception: they snap as a fan is pushed in and that snap retains it.

Source: SB manual p.45

← PreviousStep 08.1 — Sort the printed parts and confirm the hotend code

Next →Step 08.3 — Inserts: Clockwork 2 main body

docs.title: Step 08.20 — Fit the latch
docs.text: Ch 08 › B — Clockwork 2 extruder20 / 65

docs.title: Step 08.20 — Fit the latch
docs.text:
Step 20 of 65 · Chapter 08 — Toolhead: Stealthburner, Clockwork 2, Revo HF, Nitehawk-SB V2

Do: Drop the latch over its post and secure with one M3×25 SHCS. Snug: the latch must still pivot.

Parts:

  • [a]_latch ×1 (insert fitted in 08.5), M3×25 SHCS ×1

Check

The latch swings over and hooks the shuttle, holding the guidler closed, and releases cleanly when lifted.

What you're looking at

The latch is the orange lever that hooks over the latch shuttle from 08.11 to hold the guidler arm closed against spring pressure, so filament can be loaded one-handed. It also has to pivot, so it too is snug rather than tight.

Source: SB manual p.26 · Video: Part 5 @1:48:10 (differs: builds Afterburner + Clockwork 1; this kit is Stealthburner + Clockwork 2 + Revo HF)

← PreviousStep 08.19 — Hang the tension arm — and leave it loose

Next →Step 08.21 — Set the tension and the anti-squish stop

docs.title: Step 08.21 — Set the tension and the anti-squish stop
docs.text: Ch 08 › B — Clockwork 2 extruder21 / 65

docs.title: Step 08.21 — Set the tension and the anti-squish stop
docs.text:
Step 21 of 65 · Chapter 08 — Toolhead: Stealthburner, Clockwork 2, Revo HF, Nitehawk-SB V2

Do: Clockwise on the thumbscrew increases grip. Set it just tight enough that the filament cannot be pulled back through by hand. Then set the CW2 anti-squish stop, the minimum drive-gear-to-idler distance, so the gears mesh without binding.

Parts:

  • the assembled extruder, 1.75 mm filament offcut

Check

With filament loaded, the arm closes without the gears grinding against each other, and the filament shows shallow tooth marks rather than a flattened track.

What you're looking at

Two independent adjustments meet here. The thumbscrew sets how hard the idler presses; the CW2 anti-squish stop sets the minimum gap, so the gears can never be driven into each other. Shallow tooth marks are correct, a flattened track is not.

Source: SB manual p.27

← PreviousStep 08.20 — Fit the latch

Next →Step 08.22 — Fit the pancake stepper, first bolt

docs.title: Step 08.22 — Fit the pancake stepper, first bolt
docs.text: Ch 08 › B — Clockwork 2 extruder22 / 65

docs.title: Step 08.22 — Fit the pancake stepper, first bolt
docs.text:
Step 22 of 65 · Chapter 08 — Toolhead: Stealthburner, Clockwork 2, Revo HF, Nitehawk-SB V2

Do: Present the stepper to the motor plate, pinion entering the 50T gear chamber, cable exiting where the CW2 body routes it. Start the M3×30 SHCS in the upper mounting position and leave it loose.

Parts:

  • LDO-36STH20-1004AHG(VRN) NEMA14 pancake stepper ×1, M3×30 SHCS ×1

Check

The motor sits flat against the plate with the pinion engaged, not bottomed.

What you're looking at

The pancake stepper is a slim NEMA14 motor; its pinion drives the 50 T gear, and that reduction is what gives the extruder its pushing force. Both its bolts stay loose to start with, because the motor's position in its slots is the gear-mesh adjustment.

Source: SB manual p.28

← PreviousStep 08.21 — Set the tension and the anti-squish stop

Next →Step 08.23 — Fit the second motor bolt through the front access hole

docs.title: Step 08.23 — Fit the second motor bolt through the front access hole
docs.text: Ch 08 › B — Clockwork 2 extruder23 / 65

docs.title: Step 08.23 — Fit the second motor bolt through the front access hole
docs.text:
Step 23 of 65 · Chapter 08 — Toolhead: Stealthburner, Clockwork 2, Revo HF, Nitehawk-SB V2

Do: Put the washer on the M3×8 SHCS and drive it into the second motor position. It is reached from the front of the extruder through the access hole. Leave this one loose too.

Parts:

  • M3×8 SHCS ×1, M3 washer ×1

Check

Both motor bolts started, both still finger-loose, and the motor can be nudged in its slots.

What you're looking at

The second motor bolt is reached from the front of the extruder through an access hole. This is the bolt that gets forgotten, and a motor held by one bolt slowly rotates in its slots under load until the mesh is gone.

Source: SB manual p.29

← PreviousStep 08.22 — Fit the pancake stepper, first bolt

Next →Step 08.24 — Set the gear mesh, then tighten both motor bolts

docs.title: Step 08.24 — Set the gear mesh, then tighten both motor bolts
docs.text: Ch 08 › B — Clockwork 2 extruder24 / 65

docs.title: Step 08.24 — Set the gear mesh, then tighten both motor bolts
docs.text:
Step 24 of 65 · Chapter 08 — Toolhead: Stealthburner, Clockwork 2, Revo HF, Nitehawk-SB V2

Do: Slide the motor until the pinion and the 50T teeth fully overlap with a very small gap between the tooth faces. Turn the drive shaft by hand as you adjust. Then tighten the M3×30 first, the M3×8 second.

Parts:

  • the extruder assembly

Check

Rotating the drive gear by hand gives a barely perceptible backlash and no tight spot anywhere through a full turn. Both bolts tight.

What you're looking at

Gear mesh is how deeply the pinion and the 50 T teeth overlap. Too shallow and the teeth skip under load; preloaded and the drivetrain binds and whines. You want full tooth overlap with a faint backlash, then the motor locked there.

Source: SB manual p.30 · Video: Part 5 @1:41:54 (differs: builds Afterburner + Clockwork 1; this kit is Stealthburner + Clockwork 2 + Revo HF)

← PreviousStep 08.23 — Fit the second motor bolt through the front access hole

Next →Step 08.25 — Fit the LDO tilted chain anchor

docs.title: Step 08.25 — Fit the LDO tilted chain anchor
docs.text: Ch 08 › B — Clockwork 2 extruder25 / 65

docs.title: Step 08.25 — Fit the LDO tilted chain anchor
docs.text:
Step 25 of 65 · Chapter 08 — Toolhead: Stealthburner, Clockwork 2, Revo HF, Nitehawk-SB V2

Do: Sit the anchor onto the rear of the CW2 so its chain face points back along the X extrusion, and fix it with one M3×20 SHCS.

Parts:

  • CW2 Chain Anchor Tilted (supplied printed, inserts from 08.6), M3×20 SHCS ×1

Check

The anchor is solid on the body and its two chain holes face rearwards and slightly up.

What you're looking at

The chain anchor is the terminus of the toolhead's cable run: the umbilical is tied to it, so every pull from the moving drag chain lands on this printed block rather than on the toolboard's connectors.

Source: SB manual p.31

← PreviousStep 08.24 — Set the gear mesh, then tighten both motor bolts

Next →Step 08.26 — Fit the cable-bridge bolt

docs.title: Step 08.26 — Fit the cable-bridge bolt
docs.text: Ch 08 › B — Clockwork 2 extruder26 / 65

docs.title: Step 08.26 — Fit the cable-bridge bolt
docs.text:
Step 26 of 65 · Chapter 08 — Toolhead: Stealthburner, Clockwork 2, Revo HF, Nitehawk-SB V2

Do: Drive the M3×8 SHCS into the cable-bridge position on the side of the extruder: the second fixing that ties the anchor and the cable path to the body.

Parts:

  • M3×8 SHCS ×1

Check

The anchor no longer twists when you push it sideways.

What you're looking at

The cable-bridge bolt is the anchor's second fixing. On one bolt the anchor can twist; on two the cable path is rigid, which is what a drag chain tugging at it needs.

Good stopping point · ~25 min since the last one

Clockwork 2 is a complete, self-supporting sub-assembly: mesh set, both motor bolts tight, chain anchor and cable bridge fitted. The tension arm's M3×25 is deliberately loose and is a hinge pin — do not torque it to tidy the assembly up before you walk away.

Source: SB manual p.32

← PreviousStep 08.25 — Fit the LDO tilted chain anchor

docs.title: Step 08.27 — Assemble the Revo HF hotend
docs.text: Ch 08 › C — Tool cartridge and E3D Revo HF27 / 65

docs.title: Step 08.27 — Assemble the Revo HF hotend
docs.text:
Step 27 of 65 · Chapter 08 — Toolhead: Stealthburner, Clockwork 2, Revo HF, Nitehawk-SB V2

Do:

  1. Fit the spring into the groove on the heatsink's bottom and push the HeaterCore on.
  2. Screw the nozzle in finger-tight only, no tools.
  3. Aim the cables by rotating the HeaterCore anti-clockwise only; clockwise disengages the spring.

Parts:

  • Revo Voron heatsink ×1, retaining spring ×1, Revo HeaterCore ×1, Revo nozzle ×1

Check

Nozzle fully home and hand-tight. HeaterCore captive under spring load. Cables pointing to the rear.

What you're looking at

The Revo HF is E3D's quick-change hotend in three pieces: the heatsink, the finned top the filament enters; the HeaterCore, heater and thermistor in one module; and a nozzle that screws in by hand. A retaining spring holds the HeaterCore captive.

Source: SB manual p.39 · E3D Revo Voron support

← PreviousStep 08.26 — Fit the cable-bridge bolt

Next →Step 08.28 — Seat the hotend in the rear printhead half

docs.title: Step 08.28 — Seat the hotend in the rear printhead half
docs.text: Ch 08 › C — Tool cartridge and E3D Revo HF28 / 65

docs.title: Step 08.28 — Seat the hotend in the rear printhead half
docs.text:
Step 28 of 65 · Chapter 08 — Toolhead: Stealthburner, Clockwork 2, Revo HF, Nitehawk-SB V2

Do: Drop the Revo Voron heatsink into the rear printhead half so the heatsink's groove locates on the printed rib, with the HeaterCore's wires pointing up the side p.40 draws them on. Do not bend anything yet.

Parts:

  • stealthburner_printhead_revo_voron_rear_cw2 (inserts from 08.7), Revo assembly

Check

The heatsink cannot rotate in the pocket, and the nozzle protrudes centrally.

What you're looking at

The rear printhead half is the pocket the hotend lives in. The heatsink's groove locates on a moulded rib that stops the hotend rotating when you hand-tighten the nozzle. SB p.40 draws the hotend in this half: it goes in before the wires are routed.

Source: SB manual p.39 · SB manual p.40

← PreviousStep 08.27 — Assemble the Revo HF hotend

Next →Step 08.29 — Route the wires and bend the strain relief so the nozzle can seat fully

docs.title: Step 08.29 — Route the wires and bend the strain relief so the nozzle can seat fully
docs.text: Ch 08 › C — Tool cartridge and E3D Revo HF29 / 65

docs.title: Step 08.29 — Route the wires and bend the strain relief so the nozzle can seat fully
docs.text:
Step 29 of 65 · Chapter 08 — Toolhead: Stealthburner, Clockwork 2, Revo HF, Nitehawk-SB V2

Do:

  1. Route the hotend wires up the side of the rear half as SB p.40 shows.
  2. Bend the HeaterCore's stainless strain relief clear of the printed part, holding the HeaterCore firmly so no load goes on the nozzle.

Parts:

  • Revo assembly in the rear half (from 08.28)

Check

The relief clears its wall, the nozzle still turns the last part-turn home by hand, and the wires exit rearwards clear of the nozzle.

What you're looking at

The strain relief is the stainless sleeve where the HeaterCore's wires leave the module. With it in the way the nozzle cannot go the last part-turn home, and a nozzle not fully seated leaks molten plastic into the printhead on the first hot print.

Source: SB manual p.40

← PreviousStep 08.28 — Seat the hotend in the rear printhead half

Next →Step 08.30 — Close the tool cartridge

docs.title: Step 08.3 — Inserts: Clockwork 2 main body
docs.text: Ch 08 › A — Part preparation and heat-set inserts3 / 65

docs.title: Step 08.3 — Inserts: Clockwork 2 main body
docs.text:
Step 3 of 65 · Chapter 08 — Toolhead: Stealthburner, Clockwork 2, Revo HF, Nitehawk-SB V2

Do:

  1. Fit the brass M3 tip and bring the iron to your ASA setting.
  2. Press in the three inserts SB p.11 highlights: foot, both side faces.
  3. Add the p.13 fourth, for the toolhead PCB. Press each one square.

Parts:

  • main_body.stl, heat-set inserts M3×5×4 ×4

Check

All four sit below the surface, none is cocked, and an M3 screw starts by hand in each. Count: 4 (verify on bench — the manual highlights locations, not counts).

What you're looking at

Clockwork 2 is the extruder, the geared drive that grips filament and pushes it down. main_body is its larger half: drive gear, one bearing, filament path. A heat-set insert is a knurled brass sleeve melted into plastic so a screw threads into metal.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: the p.13 "OPTION: TOOLHEAD PCB" inserts are not optional here. The Nitehawk-SB V2 bolts to the CW2 sides with two M3×8 into these inserts. src

Tip

set the iron from the ASA figure on your Ch 00 Step 00.14 coupon, tongue bottoming flush. The p.13 insert sits beside a tall wall: approach from directly above.

Source: SB manual p.11 · SB manual p.12 · SB manual p.13

← PreviousStep 08.2 — Snap the built-in supports out of the Stealthburner body

Next →Step 08.4 — Inserts: Clockwork 2 motor plate

docs.title: Step 08.30 — Close the tool cartridge
docs.text: Ch 08 › C — Tool cartridge and E3D Revo HF30 / 65

docs.title: Step 08.30 — Close the tool cartridge
docs.text:
Step 30 of 65 · Chapter 08 — Toolhead: Stealthburner, Clockwork 2, Revo HF, Nitehawk-SB V2

Do: Bring the front half onto the rear half around the hotend and fix with two M3×16 SHCS.

Parts:

  • stealthburner_printhead_revo_voron_front ×1, M3×16 SHCS ×2

Check

The two halves close with no gap and the hotend has zero play in any direction.

What you're looking at

Front half on, two bolts, and the tool cartridge now exists as an object: hotend, both printhead halves and, next, the PTFE, as one unit that later slides up into the toolhead. Any movement here is movement of the nozzle.

Source: SB manual p.41

← PreviousStep 08.29 — Route the wires and bend the strain relief so the nozzle can seat fully

Next →Step 08.31 — Fit the four tool-cartridge mounting bolts

docs.title: Step 08.31 — Fit the four tool-cartridge mounting bolts
docs.text: Ch 08 › C — Tool cartridge and E3D Revo HF31 / 65

docs.title: Step 08.31 — Fit the four tool-cartridge mounting bolts
docs.text:
Step 31 of 65 · Chapter 08 — Toolhead: Stealthburner, Clockwork 2, Revo HF, Nitehawk-SB V2

Do: Drive four M3×8 SHCS into the top face of the tool cartridge. Do not overtighten and do not leave them proud.

Parts:

  • M3×8 SHCS ×4

Check

Four bolts, all seated to the same depth.

What you're looking at

These four M3×8 are studs, not fasteners. Their heads engage keyholes in the Clockwork 2 when the cartridge slides up into place at Step 08.61, so all four must stand at exactly the same height or the cartridge hangs crooked.

Source: SB manual p.42

← PreviousStep 08.30 — Close the tool cartridge

Next →Step 08.32 — Cut and fit the PTFE to 11 mm stickout

docs.title: Step 08.32 — Cut and fit the PTFE to 11 mm stickout
docs.text: Ch 08 › C — Tool cartridge and E3D Revo HF32 / 65

docs.title: Step 08.32 — Cut and fit the PTFE to 11 mm stickout
docs.text:
Step 32 of 65 · Chapter 08 — Toolhead: Stealthburner, Clockwork 2, Revo HF, Nitehawk-SB V2

Do: Push the PTFE down into the tool cartridge until it bottoms on the heatsink, then cut it so exactly 11 mm stands above the printed part. Cut square: a diagonal cut leaves a filament-catching step.

Parts:

  • PTFE 4 mm OD / 2 mm ID (10 cm piece), caliper, flush cutters

Check

Caliper across the stickout reads 11 mm. Push 1.75 mm filament through: it enters the hotend with no catch.

What you're looking at

The PTFE tube is the low-friction liner that guides filament from the extruder's outlet down into the hotend. 11 mm of stickout is the Clockwork 2 figure: the length that closes the gap between the two, so the filament cannot buckle under extrusion pressure.

Good stopping point · ~20 min since the last one

the tool cartridge is closed around the Revo, the four M3×8 studs are in, and the PTFE is cut to 11 mm. Bag it nozzle-up. Do not put a tool on the nozzle and do not stand the cartridge on its nozzle; both undo the hand-tight seat you just set.

Source: SB manual p.43 · Video: Part 5 @2:06:01 (differs: builds Afterburner + Clockwork 1; this kit is Stealthburner + Clockwork 2 + Revo HF)

← PreviousStep 08.31 — Fit the four tool-cartridge mounting bolts

Next →Step 08.33 — Terminate the hotend leads for the Nitehawk V2

docs.title: Step 08.33 — Terminate the hotend leads for the Nitehawk V2
docs.text: Ch 08 › C — Tool cartridge and E3D Revo HF33 / 65

docs.title: Step 08.33 — Terminate the hotend leads for the Nitehawk V2
docs.text:
Step 33 of 65 · Chapter 08 — Toolhead: Stealthburner, Clockwork 2, Revo HF, Nitehawk-SB V2

Do:

  1. Open the Toolhead PCB Cables bag. If LDO's cables mate the Revo's Molex Micro-Fit 3.0 2-pin, use them as-is.
  2. Otherwise cut the Revo pigtails and fit E0508 ferrules for HE0, a JST-PH2.0 2-pin housing for TH0. (verify on bench — depends on what LDO packed for the Revo option)

Parts:

  • Revo heater and thermistor leads, E0508 ferrules ×2, JST-PH2.0 2-pin housing + crimps (only if re-terminating)

Check

Heater leads end in two crimped E0508 ferrules with no stray strands. Thermistor lead ends in a 2-pin PH2.0 housing that drops into TH0 without force.

What you're looking at

The Nitehawk-SB V2 is the toolboard: a PCB on the toolhead collecting heater, thermistor, fans, LEDs, probe and motor onto one USB-plus-24 V umbilical. HE0 is the heater screw terminal, TH0 the 2-pin JST-PH2.0 socket. A ferrule stops stranded wire splaying in a screw terminal.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: the Rev D wiring guide says "the connector type to use is JST-XH2.5 two pin" for the thermistor. On the V2 board TH0, PROBE and the XY endstop are JST-PH2.0. An XH2.5 housing will not fit, and the PH2.0 body is easy to force into the wrong header — check the silkscreen before every insertion. src

Source: Nitehawk-SB V2 pinout

← PreviousStep 08.32 — Cut and fit the PTFE to 11 mm stickout

Next →Step 08.34 — Prepare the 5015 part-cooling blower

docs.title: Step 08.34 — Prepare the 5015 part-cooling blower
docs.text: Ch 08 › C — Tool cartridge and E3D Revo HF34 / 65

docs.title: Step 08.34 — Prepare the 5015 part-cooling blower
docs.text:
Step 34 of 65 · Chapter 08 — Toolhead: Stealthburner, Clockwork 2, Revo HF, Nitehawk-SB V2

Do: Remove the front cover of the 5015. Clip the stock mounting ears off flush and file the remains until the housing sides are flat. A trimming jig STL ships in the Stealthburner release archive, not in the repo's STLs/ tree.

Parts:

  • 50×50×15 centrifugal fan (24 V) ×1, flush cutters, small flat file

Check

No ear stands proud of the housing wall. The fan drops into the SB main body pocket without spreading the printed walls.

What you're looking at

The 5015 is the part-cooling blower: a centrifugal fan that throws air sideways out of a nozzle rather than straight through, which lets it feed the printhead's narrow ducts. Its moulded mounting ears belong to a different machine; Stealthburner grips the bare housing.

Source: SB manual p.55 · Video: Part 6 @0:20:10

← PreviousStep 08.33 — Terminate the hotend leads for the Nitehawk V2

Next →Step 08.35 — Build the logo LED into its carrier

docs.title: Step 08.35 — Build the logo LED into its carrier
docs.text: Ch 08 › D — Stealthburner body: LEDs and fans35 / 65

docs.title: Step 08.35 — Build the logo LED into its carrier
docs.text:
Step 35 of 65 · Chapter 08 — Toolhead: Stealthburner, Clockwork 2, Revo HF, Nitehawk-SB V2

Do:

  1. Seat the logo LED in the carrier, wires exiting upwards.
  2. Stack from the outside in: opaque mask, then diffuser with its prongs forward and flat base behind, then the LED carrier. SB p.47 right draws the result.

Parts:

  • [o]_stealthburner_LED_carrier ×1, [o]_stealthburner_LED_diffuser_mask ×1, [c]_stealthburner_LED_diffuser ×1 (supplied, clear PETG), logo LED (chain index 1)

Check

Three translucent bars sit flush in the black face, the diffuser's flat base behind the mask and not in front. Nothing rattles.

What you're looking at

The logo LED and its three-part sandwich, from the outside in: the opaque mask with three windows is the face you see; the clear PETG diffuser behind it pokes three prongs forward through those windows; the carrier holds the LED behind both.

Source: SB manual p.47

← PreviousStep 08.34 — Prepare the 5015 part-cooling blower

Next →Step 08.36 — Wire the three-LED chain

docs.title: Step 08.36 — Wire the three-LED chain
docs.text: Ch 08 › D — Stealthburner body: LEDs and fans36 / 65

docs.title: Step 08.36 — Wire the three-LED chain
docs.text:
Step 36 of 65 · Chapter 08 — Toolhead: Stealthburner, Clockwork 2, Revo HF, Nitehawk-SB V2

Do:

  1. Check the toolhead cable bag: many Rev D kits ship this chain pre-soldered.
  2. Otherwise solder OUT to IN along the chain, logo 1, right 2, left 3, every LED's wires exiting the same way.

Parts:

  • logo LED (index 1), toolhead LED right (index 2), toolhead LED left (index 3)
  • 3-core 0.16 mm² (AWG26–30) — 120 mm controller→logo, 100 mm between each LED

Check

Continuity from the connector's DIN through each LED's DIN/DOUT pair in chain order; 5 V and GND common; no 5 V–GND short.

What you're looking at

These are addressable LEDs wired as a chain: data goes in to the first and out to the next, so each LED's position is its address. Logo is index 1, right toolhead LED 2, left 3, the order chain_count: 3 and every LED macro assume.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: the config declares chain_count: 3 and color_order: GRBW. A colour-order mismatch shows up as wrong colours, never as a failure — if the LEDs light in the wrong colours in Ch 13, change color_order, do not rewire. src

Good stopping point · ~25 min since the last one

the hotend leads are terminated, the 5015 ears are trimmed and filed, and the three-LED chain is soldered and continuity-checked. Nothing is in the Stealthburner body yet. Iron off and cool. Do not coil the chain tightly: the 100 and 120 mm pigtails are cut to fit the printed channels and kinking them loses that length.

Source: SB manual p.46

← PreviousStep 08.35 — Build the logo LED into its carrier

Next →Step 08.37 — Seat the two toolhead LEDs

docs.title: Step 08.37 — Seat the two toolhead LEDs
docs.text: Ch 08 › D — Stealthburner body: LEDs and fans37 / 65

docs.title: Step 08.37 — Seat the two toolhead LEDs
docs.text:
Step 37 of 65 · Chapter 08 — Toolhead: Stealthburner, Clockwork 2, Revo HF, Nitehawk-SB V2

Do: Push each toolhead LED into its pocket in the top corners of the main body, from the outside inwards, wires trailing outboard. p.48 is drawn from behind: its RIGHT pocket is index 2, its LEFT pocket index 3.

Parts:

  • toolhead LED left (index 3), toolhead LED right (index 2), [a]_stealthburner_main_body

Check

Both LEDs bottom in their pockets and face down into the print area.

What you're looking at

The two toolhead LEDs sit in the top corners of the body and light the print area from above. SB p.48 names them from behind: index 2 is the toolhead's own right, the pocket on your left when you face the printer.

Source: SB manual p.48

← PreviousStep 08.36 — Wire the three-LED chain

Next →Step 08.38 — Insert the LED diffusers and push them forward

docs.title: Step 08.38 — Insert the LED diffusers and push them forward
docs.text: Ch 08 › D — Stealthburner body: LEDs and fans38 / 65

docs.title: Step 08.38 — Insert the LED diffusers and push them forward
docs.text:
Step 38 of 65 · Chapter 08 — Toolhead: Stealthburner, Clockwork 2, Revo HF, Nitehawk-SB V2

Do: Drop the mask-and-diffuser into the top slot and push it towards the front until it fills the front window, p.49. Drop the carrier with the LED in behind it, p.50. (verify on bench which of p.49/p.50 is the mask+diffuser and which the carrier)

Parts:

  • the logo LED assembly from 08.35 (mask + diffuser, and the LED carrier)

Check

Diffuser faces sit flush with the front of the body; no gap behind them.

What you're looking at

The diffusers are the translucent panels you stacked at 08.35: the mask-and-diffuser sandwich and the LED carrier, which the SB manual feeds into the body in two pieces. Pushed fully forward they sit flush with the front; left back, they leave a shadow line.

Source: SB manual p.49 · SB manual p.50 · Video: More Extras! @1:06:03 (differs: builds Afterburner + Clockwork 1; this kit is Stealthburner + Clockwork 2 + Revo HF)

← PreviousStep 08.37 — Seat the two toolhead LEDs

Next →Step 08.39 — Route the LED wires out of the body

docs.title: Step 08.39 — Route the LED wires out of the body
docs.text: Ch 08 › D — Stealthburner body: LEDs and fans39 / 65

docs.title: Step 08.39 — Route the LED wires out of the body
docs.text:
Step 39 of 65 · Chapter 08 — Toolhead: Stealthburner, Clockwork 2, Revo HF, Nitehawk-SB V2

Do: Lay the LED wires into the moulded channels so the whole harness exits on the right side of the body. Keep them out of the fan cavities.

Parts:

  • the LED chain in the body

Check

With the body face-down, no wire crosses either fan opening and the harness leaves as a single bundle on the right.

What you're looking at

Every wire in the body is routed to leave on one side, so the whole harness can be taken to the fan adapter as a single bundle. A wire crossing a fan opening is a wire an impeller will eventually find.

Source: SB manual p.51

← PreviousStep 08.38 — Insert the LED diffusers and push them forward

Next →Step 08.40 — Clip in the hotend fan, correct way round

docs.title: Step 08.4 — Inserts: Clockwork 2 motor plate
docs.text: Ch 08 › A — Part preparation and heat-set inserts4 / 65

docs.title: Step 08.4 — Inserts: Clockwork 2 motor plate
docs.text:
Step 4 of 65 · Chapter 08 — Toolhead: Stealthburner, Clockwork 2, Revo HF, Nitehawk-SB V2

Do: SB p.12 highlights three locations. The top and bottom inserts must both sit below the surface; mind the cutout beside the bottom one and keep it straight. SB p.13 adds the fourth, for the toolhead PCB.

Parts:

  • motor_plate.stl, heat-set inserts M3×5×4 ×4

Check

Lay a steel rule across each insert: no insert stands proud. Count: 4 (verify on bench).

What you're looking at

The motor plate is the other half: the thin 8.2 mm plate with the large central bore that closes the extruder and carries the pancake stepper. Its inserts have to finish below the surface, because one standing proud stops the motor sitting flat.

Source: SB manual p.12 · SB manual p.13

← PreviousStep 08.3 — Inserts: Clockwork 2 main body

Next →Step 08.5 — Inserts: latch, latch shuttle and guidler arm (flush, not below)

docs.title: Step 08.40 — Clip in the hotend fan, correct way round
docs.text: Ch 08 › D — Stealthburner body: LEDs and fans40 / 65

docs.title: Step 08.40 — Clip in the hotend fan, correct way round
docs.text:
Step 40 of 65 · Chapter 08 — Toolhead: Stealthburner, Clockwork 2, Revo HF, Nitehawk-SB V2

Do: Rotate the fan so its wires exit at the top and its airflow pushes inwards, into the heatsink. Confirm against the moulded arrow on the frame. Clip it in at a slight angle; it snaps the body's support webs.

Parts:

  • 40×40×10 axial fan, 24 V ×1

Check

Wires at top, airflow arrow pointing into the body. Spin the impeller with a finger: free, no rub.

What you're looking at

The 4010 axial fan is the hotend fan: it blows through the heatsink's fins to keep the cold side of the hotend cold. Direction is absolute: the moulded arrow must point into the heatsink. As it seats, the fan snaps the body's support webs.

Source: SB manual p.53

← PreviousStep 08.39 — Route the LED wires out of the body

Next →Step 08.41 — Route the hotend fan wires

docs.title: Step 08.41 — Route the hotend fan wires
docs.text: Ch 08 › D — Stealthburner body: LEDs and fans41 / 65

docs.title: Step 08.41 — Route the hotend fan wires
docs.text:
Step 41 of 65 · Chapter 08 — Toolhead: Stealthburner, Clockwork 2, Revo HF, Nitehawk-SB V2

Do: Lay the fan wires into their channel so they exit on the right side, alongside the LED harness.

Parts:

  • hotend fan wires

Check

All wire exits are on one side; nothing is pinched under the fan frame.

What you're looking at

The fan wires join the LED harness in the same right-hand channel: one bundle, one exit, and nothing trapped under the fan frame.

Source: SB manual p.54

← PreviousStep 08.40 — Clip in the hotend fan, correct way round

Next →Step 08.42 — Fit the part-cooling blower

docs.title: Step 08.42 — Fit the part-cooling blower
docs.text: Ch 08 › D — Stealthburner body: LEDs and fans42 / 65

docs.title: Step 08.42 — Fit the part-cooling blower
docs.text:
Step 42 of 65 · Chapter 08 — Toolhead: Stealthburner, Clockwork 2, Revo HF, Nitehawk-SB V2

Do: Drop the trimmed blower into the upper cavity, above the hotend fan, outlet feeding the ducts, and fix it with two M3×6 FHCS. Blower wires exit right. Part cooling is the top fan, the hotend fan the bottom.

Parts:

  • trimmed 5015 from 08.34, M3×6 FHCS ×2

Check

The blower is square in the upper cavity with the 4010 below it, the impeller spins freely, and the outlet aims down through the duct.

What you're looking at

The trimmed 5015 goes in the upper cavity, above the hotend fan. Which fan is which matters: the config drives them on different pins, and Ch 13's fan verification tests whether top and bottom got swapped.

Good stopping point · ~20 min since the last one

the Stealthburner body is fully populated: three LEDs seated, diffusers pushed forward, both fans in, every wire exiting on the right. Rest it face-down on a soft cloth. Do not put weight on the diffuser faces or spin the impellers with anything but a finger.

Source: SB manual p.56

← PreviousStep 08.41 — Route the hotend fan wires

Next →Step 08.43 — Bolt the Nitehawk-SB V2 to the Clockwork 2

docs.title: Step 08.43 — Bolt the Nitehawk-SB V2 to the Clockwork 2
docs.text: Ch 08 › E — Nitehawk-SB V2 and the fan adapter43 / 65

docs.title: Step 08.43 — Bolt the Nitehawk-SB V2 to the Clockwork 2
docs.text:
Step 43 of 65 · Chapter 08 — Toolhead: Stealthburner, Clockwork 2, Revo HF, Nitehawk-SB V2

Do:

  1. Sit the PCB spacer against the CW2 side, the toolboard on top, two M3×8 SHCS.
  2. Trap the supplied ground cable's ring lug under the lower M3×8 head, at the bottom corner nearest the motor (verify on bench — the photo, not LDO's prose, is the source).

Parts:

  • Nitehawk-SB V2 ×1, CW2 PCB Spacer ×1 (supplied printed), M3×8 SHCS ×2

Check

The board sits parallel on its spacer, the 10-pin header faces forward, and the ground lug is under a screw head, tail free.

What you're looking at

The Nitehawk-SB V2 toolboard is the larger board in this photo; the triangular board beside it is the Stealthburner Fan Adapter, fitted next. The two mate through a keyed board-to-board header when the orange body closes. The printed spacer sets the standoff.

Tip

handle the board by its edges. A screw that will not start means a cocked insert. The ground wire's motor end waits for Step 08.53.

Source: LDO wiring guide § Wiring the Toolhead PCB

← PreviousStep 08.42 — Fit the part-cooling blower

Next →Step 08.44 — Mount the fan adapter PCB on the back of the 5015

docs.title: Step 08.44 — Mount the fan adapter PCB on the back of the 5015
docs.text: Ch 08 › E — Nitehawk-SB V2 and the fan adapter44 / 65

docs.title: Step 08.44 — Mount the fan adapter PCB on the back of the 5015
docs.text:
Step 44 of 65 · Chapter 08 — Toolhead: Stealthburner, Clockwork 2, Revo HF, Nitehawk-SB V2

Do: Mount the adapter to the rear of the Stealthburner main body, onto the back of the 5015 fan, with two M3×10 FHCS through its end holes. Whether these share or replace the M3×6 FHCS from 08.42 is undrawn (verify on bench; no LDO photo of the mounted adapter has been found).

Parts:

  • Stealthburner Fan Adapter PCB (SBurnerFanAdapter_V2.0) ×1, M3×10 FHCS ×2

Check

Board flat against the fan; its P1 header points at the toolboard's header when the body is offered up.

What you're looking at

The fan adapter is the PCB that collects both fans and the LED chain on the body side and hands them to the toolboard through a single board-to-board header, so the orange body lifts off with three plugs still made up.

Source: SB V2 fan adapter pinout

← PreviousStep 08.43 — Bolt the Nitehawk-SB V2 to the Clockwork 2

Next →Step 08.45 — Check the fan-voltage solder jumpers before anything is powered

docs.title: Step 08.45 — Check the fan-voltage solder jumpers before anything is powered
docs.text: Ch 08 › E — Nitehawk-SB V2 and the fan adapter45 / 65

docs.title: Step 08.45 — Check the fan-voltage solder jumpers before anything is powered
docs.text:
Step 45 of 65 · Chapter 08 — Toolhead: Stealthburner, Clockwork 2, Revo HF, Nitehawk-SB V2

Do: Confirm both selectors, silkscreened 24V V_HEF 5V and 24V V_PCF 5V, are on the 24 V side. Both your fans are 24 V per the Rev D 350 BOM. LDO's 5 V conversion cuts the trace and solders a bridge: do neither. Cut nothing.

Parts:

  • fan adapter PCB, magnifier

Check

By meter: both selectors continuous from the middle pad to 24V, open to 5V. The factory trace is too thin to see. (verify on bench — factory default is 24 V)

What you're looking at

The two three-pad groups are solder jumpers: each chooses 24 V or 5 V for its fan port, by which outer pad joins the middle. From the factory that join is a hair-thin PCB trace, not a solder blob. Both fans are 24 V.

Source: SB V2 fan adapter pinout

← PreviousStep 08.44 — Mount the fan adapter PCB on the back of the 5015

Next →Step 08.46 — Plug the fans and the LED chain into the adapter

docs.title: Step 08.46 — Plug the fans and the LED chain into the adapter
docs.text: Ch 08 › E — Nitehawk-SB V2 and the fan adapter46 / 65

docs.title: Step 08.46 — Plug the fans and the LED chain into the adapter
docs.text:
Step 46 of 65 · Chapter 08 — Toolhead: Stealthburner, Clockwork 2, Revo HF, Nitehawk-SB V2

Do: Three JST-PH2.0 3-pin plugs, one per port:

Parts:

  • hotend fan lead, 5015 lead, LED chain lead

Check

All three plugs fully home, latch engaged, no wire in tension. P2 to the axial, P4 to the blower.

What you're looking at

Three JST-PH2.0 3-pin plugs, one per port; the middle pin on each fan port is the tacho line, reporting real RPM to Klipper. The classic error is swapping P2 and P4: both fans run, but the machine cools the hotend instead of the print.

Port What plugs in Pinout, silkscreen order P2 4010 axial hotend fan + / A1 (tacho) / − P3 Neopixel LED chain 5V / GND / RGB P4 5015 part cooling blower − / A2 (tacho) / +

If you ever re-crimp a fan lead, take the polarity from the silkscreen next to the port, not from the fan's wire colours.

Conflict

LDO's graphic nhsbv2_pcb_pinout.jpg labels the Fan/RGB header PA15 → HEF and PD0 → PCF; the adapter silkscreen and the Rev D+ Klipper config say the opposite, [fan] on nhk:PA15 tacho nhk:PD2, [heater_fan hotend_fan] on nhk:PD0 tacho nhk:PD1. Two of three agree, so wire by port function, P2 axial and P4 blower. If Ch 13's Verify Fans spins the wrong fan, swap the pin: values in printer.cfg. Do not re-crimp connectors. src

Good stopping point · ~20 min since the last one

the Nitehawk-SB V2 and the fan adapter are mounted, both fan-voltage selectors are verified at 24 V, and the three PH2.0 fan and LED plugs are in. Do not mate the board-to-board header yet — that happens with the Stealthburner body at Step 08.62 — and do not cut or bridge a voltage-selector pad.

Source: SB V2 fan adapter pinout
