docs.title: Step 09.7 — Learn the DIN clip motion once
Step 09.7 — Learn the DIN clip motion once
docs.text:
Step 7 of 36 · Chapter 09 — Electronics bay

Do: Practise on a spare clip: hook the fixed side over one rail edge, rotate the part down flat with that hook engaged, then press until the sprung side snaps over the other edge.

Parts:

  • one spare printed pcb_din_clip ×1

Check

The clip sits square on the rail, does not rock, and slides along the rail with firm thumb pressure but not under its own weight.

What you're looking at

A DIN clip is the sprung foot that grips the rail: one side a fixed hook, the other a spring latch. Every clipped component in this chapter goes on the same way, and pressing one on flat-first breaks the latch.

Good stopping point · ~25 min since the last one

printer on its top, rear T-nuts pre-loaded, deck panel verified, both DIN rails on and all five wire ducts cut and stuck. Nothing is clipped to a rail yet. Leave the printer where it is if you can; standing it back up costs you the T-nut access.

Source: Voron manual p.168 · LDO wiring guide § Installing the DIN rails and wire ducts · Video: Part 7 @0:28:22

Step 09.8 — Do not build the Pi bracket

A deliberate skip. The manual mounts the Raspberry Pi on its own printed bracket because its reference machine uses a separate controller board; the Leviathan has a dedicated Pi area with its own standoffs, so both pages are dead here.

Step 09.9 — Do not fit a 5 V PSU
docs.text:
Step 9 of 36 · Chapter 09 — Electronics bay

Do: Skip both pages. There is no RS25-5 in the kit and no space allocated for one.

No RS-25-5 or second supply in the kit boxes; the Pi power lead and 3/4 HAT adapter are bagged for 09.23.

docs.title: Checkpoint 09
docs.text: Ch 09Checkpoint

docs.title: Checkpoint 09
docs.text:
Checkpoint · Chapter 09 — Electronics bay

What you should have now — The two DIN rails, the 24 V PSU, the SSR, the mains WAGO mount and the power inlet panel, plus the XY endstop pod that goes on the gantry. Nothing here is size-dependent. Most of what this chapter adds is hidden under the deck at this camera - use the bay renders in the chapter for the layout. The CAD also has no Leviathan, no Pi bracket and no LDO nozzle probe, so the front rail is emptier here than yours will be.
  • Two DIN rails run left-to-right, each bolted with one M5×10 BHCS into each bed extrusion, all four plastic end caps fitted.
  • Five wire ducts VHB'd down; the rear duct runs rearward of the deck's wire opening, and the opening is clear.
  • Meanwell LRS-200-24 selector set to 115 V, on the rear rail via its two printed brackets — and no support bracket fitted.
  • Omron SSR on its metal bracket, latched to the rear rail left of the PSU, LOAD (1/2) and INPUT (3+/4−) identified and reachable.
  • Every Leviathan voltage-selection jumper removed and bagged.
  • Leviathan on the front rail with the Pi 4B mounted on it, heatsink fitted, SD card in, and the 3/4 HAT power adapter seated.
  • USB adapter on the front rail with the partial cover and the supplied grounding cable attached to its exposed point; frame end left loose for Ch 10.
  • IEC inlet module (one part, not two) in power_inlet_IECGS_1mm, panel bolted to the rear extrusion hard against the rear-left Z-motor mount; three WAGO 221-415 clamps in the mains WAGO mount to its right.
  • Nozzle probe assembled — collar home, PCB on two M2×10, shaft free — and mounted on M3×25 SHCS in the bed extrusion's side slot, pin rising through the deck's rear notch and ~1.5 mm clear of the plate's rear edge. If the 5 mm shaft is out (un-notched, 09.29), it is bagged and labelled probe shaft — refit before 13.24.
  • XY endstop PCB on the pod, pod on the gantry, full X and Y travel with no fouling.
  • Bed WAGO breakout built and mounted; the plate still lifts off the deck from above.
  • Nothing wired. Nothing plugged in. Duct lids off, skirts and bottom panel off. Multimeter on the bench.

← PreviousStep 09.36 — Check the bay against LDO's layout and hand it to Ch 10

Next →Ch 10 — before you start

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Fitting the p.169 support bracket "because it's in the manual". LDO explicitly skips it; the two printed brackets are the mount. Bolting an unneeded L-bracket to the frame just puts a screw where a cable wants to go.
  • Leaving the Leviathan's voltage jumpers in. The one mistake in this chapter that destroys hardware. They come out before the board is installed, not before it is wired.
  • Setting the PSU selector after the bay is full. Once the PSU is on the rail behind a wire duct the switch is nearly invisible. Set it at 09.14, before it goes on the rail.
  • Fitting the V1 USB adapter cover. It hides the grounding point that Rev D+ exists to expose, and the ESD path silently ends up broken.
  • Closing the bay, or plugging the cord in "just to see the PSU light". Both belong after Checkpoint #1 in Ch 10 (survey §5.2 W8).
  • Over-driving M2 self-tapping screws into ASA. Two turns too far strips the boss and the DIN clip or the Z endstop PCB never sits solid again.

docs.title: Next
docs.text:
Ch 10 — Wiring: above-deck, below-deck, mains and Checkpoint #1 (LDO wiring guide, in its own order, plus manual p.194–195 for drag-chain slack). Nothing in this bay gets energised until that checkpoint passes.

Source: LDO wiring guide § General Placement · survey §7.5

Good stopping point · ~15 min since the last one

bay fully populated, tagged and checked against LDO's layout, printer still on its head, mains-safety hardware staged in one labelled bag, meter beside it. Do not start Ch 10 in a leftover ten minutes: mains work is a fresh session with a clear head, and it ends at LDO's Checkpoint #1.

docs.title: Before you start Chapter 09
docs.text: Ch 09Before you start

docs.title: Before you start Chapter 09
docs.text:
Before you start · Chapter 09 — Electronics bay

Fits out the space under the deck panel: two DIN rails and five wire ducts, the Meanwell 24 V PSU, the Omron SSR, the Leviathan mainboard carrying the Raspberry Pi 4B, the Nitehawk USB adapter, the mains inlet and WAGO blocks, and both endstops. Everything is mounted and nothing is wired — that unlocks Ch 10, which is one continuous harness job ending at Checkpoint #1.

What you're building in this chapter. The bay is the space under the deck panel, and this chapter fits it out without connecting a single wire. Two DIN rails — the standard 35 mm slotted steel rail that industrial gear clips onto — run left to right across the deck, and five slotted wire ducts loop around them to carry the harness Ch 10 will lay in. On the rear rail go the PSU (the Meanwell supply that turns mains into the 24 V everything runs on) and the SSR (a solid-state relay: the contactless electronic switch that lets a low-voltage board turn the mains bed heater on and off). On the front rail go the Leviathan — this kit's mainboard, driving all five steppers, both heaters, the fans and the endstops, with the Raspberry Pi bolted on top of it — and the USB adapter that terminates the toolhead umbilical. Round the rear frame go the IEC inlet module (socket, switch and fuse in one) and three WAGO lever connectors that distribute live, neutral and earth. Both endstops — the frame-mounted nozzle probe that sets Z zero and the XY endstop PCB in its pod on the gantry — are built and mounted here too.

Left and right in this chapter are always the printer's own — the way you would say them standing at the front of the upright machine, display towards you. With the printer on its head, work from the printer's rear (the edge the deck notch points to — 09.4 — with the A/B motors hanging from the gantry's rear corners above it) and look down into the bay: the front edge is far from you, and your left is the printer's left. That is exactly the view in LDO's placement photo (display at the top of the frame) and in the manual's p.169/p.171 insets (labelled Front at the top). Stand at the front of the inverted printer instead and everything below is mirrored — and the bay is not symmetric.

Time: 2.5–4.0 h hands-on, first build (survey §7.2).

Sessions: 7 × ~30 min (first-build estimate; each Pause: line carries its own segment minutes).

Prerequisites:

  • Ch 01–03. Frame squared, deck panel and deck supports in (manual p.28–30), build plate on with its three cables hanging free below the deck.
  • Ch 06. Gantry installed — step 09.33 mounts the XY endstop pod to it.
  • Batch B07 — Electronics bay + lighting. Plate B07-P1 carries power_inlet_IECGS_1mm (moved out of B08 — index correction #11); the manual fits the inlet panel at p.156/167, i.e. in this chapter, so B07-P1 must be printed before you start or steps 09.10–09.12 stall. The COB light-strip mounts on plate B07-P2 are not consumed here; they are Ch 10. No part of B08 is needed in this chapter.
  • Batch B00 heat-set pass. The inlet panel and the bed WAGO mount both need inserts before assembly (survey §5.2 W3).

Tools

  • 2.5 mm flat-blade screwdriver (supplied — this is the tool for every plug-type terminal in the bay)
  • PH1 (M2 self-tapping) and PH2 (PSU and SSR terminals) screwdrivers
  • Hex 2 / 2.5 / 3 mm
  • Soldering iron + brass M3 heat-set tip
  • Hacksaw or fine-tooth saw + file (DIN rail), side cutters or a fine saw (wire duct)
  • Steel rule ≥300 mm, marker, digital caliper
  • Multimeter (used properly in Ch 10; keep it on the bench from now on)

Consumables: 3M VHB tape (supplied, for the wire ducts), IPA + lint-free cloth, masking tape and marker for labelling.

Printed parts

Parts arrive in the bins named below (see the bin map in print/README.md#bins); check the bin label's list before you start.

Looks like STL Bin Qty Colour Electronics_Bay/lrs_200_psu_bracket_x2 09-bay 2 Black Electronics_Bay/wago_221-415_mount_3by5 09-bay 1 Black Electronics_Bay/pcb_din_clip_x3 09-bay 1 file = 3 clips (spares — kit supplies 4) Black Electronics_Bay/PSU_stabilizer_50mm 09-bay 1 — fit only if needed, see 09.16 Black Nitehawk-SB-V2/usb_adapter_mount_partial_cover 09-bay 1 Black Skirts/power_inlet_IECGS_1mm 09-bay 1 (batch B07-P1) Black

Supplied printed by LDO — do not print these: Leviathan Bracket Left ×1, Leviathan Bracket Right ×1, NH Adapter Mount ×1, DIN Clip ×4, LDO Nozzle Probe ×1, Bed WAGO Mount ×1. src

Read first

  • Remove every voltage-selection jumper from the Leviathan before it goes anywhere near the rail (step 09.19). Mixing voltages on the shared 24 V supply permanently destroys the controller and whatever is plugged into it. Jumpers go back in Ch 10, one at a time, after each component's voltage is confirmed. src
  • Nothing is wired in this chapter. Mains wiring is the one step in this build that can kill you, and it is done as one deliberate sequence in Ch 10 that ends at LDO's Checkpoint #1 — continuity within each colour group, no continuity between L, N and PE, PSU selector confirmed, all with the cord unplugged. Leave the C13 cord in its bag. (survey §4.4 #8)
  • The manual pages p.148–172 describe a different machine — a BTT Octopus, a mini12864, a 5 V PSU and a separate Pi bracket. Use them for the DIN-rail technique and the mounting geometry only; every part that differs carries a ⚠ callout at its step. src
  • Do not close the bay. Skirts and the bottom panel go on in Ch 11, only after Checkpoint #1 passes. Fitting them now costs an hour of re-opening plus the safety check you skipped (survey §5.2 W8).
  • Test-fit every roll-in T-nut. Extrusion and T-nut tolerances on this kit are tight; a forced nut galls the slot. src
  • Bench-only work for a print-idle window (the index's while it prints rows assume you use them): 09.10 and 09.34's inserts, 09.14–09.15 (PSU selector and brackets), 09.17 (SSR on its bracket), 09.19–09.23 (Leviathan brackets, jumpers, Pi, HAT adapter), 09.25 (USB-adapter clip) and 09.27–09.29 (nozzle probe) need no printer. If you did the two heat-set jobs in Ch 08's iron session, 09.10 and 09.34 start with a confirm.

What you're looking at

Who is in the room (00a.2): one adult at the machine from 10.1 to 10.23. She is out of the room for Sections 1 and 2 and back for 10.24; she reads the meter aloud in Section 8, with the printer unplugged.

docs.title: Step 10.10 — Read the SSR terminal numbers before you wire it
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 1 — Mains: inlet → switch → PSU → SSR → bed heater10 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.10 — Read the SSR terminal numbers before you wire it
docs.text:
Step 10 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do: Read the SSR body: the pair silkscreened 1 LOAD 2 is the AC switching side, 3 + INPUT 4 − the DC control side. Note which end the yellow indicator LED sits at, and match LDO's photo.

Parts:

  • Omron SSR on its DIN bracket (fitted Ch 09)

Check

You can point at terminal 1, 2, 3 and 4 without hesitating, and the LED is on the same side as in the photo.

What you're looking at

The SSR is the black brick on the DIN rail: a solid-state relay, so the mainboard can switch a mains bed heater with a small DC signal. Its four screws are two separate circuits, 1/2 the mains it switches and 3 +/4 − the control side.

Note: how LDO tags its cables. Every pre-made lead in the kit is tagged, and the two kinds of tag say different things. A TO … tag names the far end's destination: TO SSR sits at the WAGO end of SSR to Wago; TO MB, TO MB HV and TO TOOLHEAD sit at the PSU ends of the board supply, the HV stepper supply and 24V power. The other end of each of those carries the rail name it lands on — 24V, HV, 24V IN, SSR SIG — not a destination. Read a TO tag as "this cable is going to …", a rail tag as "this is the … rail", then check the connector type and the red/black polarity at both ends. src

Note: the SSR body is also marked EARTH THE MOUNTING RAIL. LDO's build does not run a separate PE to the DIN rail. If your local rules require an earthed rail, that is a mains change — have it specified by whoever signs off your mains work.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: "The SSR connection is critical, an incorrect connection can cause catastrophic damage." Nothing else in this chapter carries that warning. src

Source: LDO Rev D photo S4 24 V/SSR mapping · LDO wiring guide § Connecting 24V · Video: Part 8 @1:29:57

Step 11 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do:

  1. Strip the bare end tagged TO SSR to 11 mm and land it in a spare port of the brown L WAGO.
  2. Land the ferruled end on SSR terminal LOAD 2, PH2 tight.

Parts:

  • SSR to Wago cable ×1 (one end tagged TO SSR)

Continuity from the C14 L pin, rocker ON, through to SSR terminal 2. Nothing on terminal 1 yet.

What you're looking at

The SSR to Wago cable is one of the kit's pre-made mains leads: a bare stripped end for the WAGO lever, and a ferruled end for the relay, its crimped sleeve turning stranded wire into a tube a screw can clamp.

docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 1 — Mains: inlet → switch → PSU → SSR → bed heater12 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.12 — Bed harness into the bed WAGO breakout
docs.text:
Step 12 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do:

  1. Bed L and extension into the first WAGO, N and Bed N into the second, BED TH into the 2×2 splicer.
  2. Loosen the M4×6 BHCS three turns, slide the PE ring under the serrated washer, retighten.

Parts:

  • the three cables hanging from the plate (Bed L, N, BED TH) plus the bed PE ring terminal, the kit's two braided extension leads (tagged Bed L and Bed N), bed WAGO mount with 2× WAGO 221-412 and the 2×2 XH splicer (fitted Ch 09)

Check

L, N, PE and TH leave the bed WAGO mount. Ring terminal will not rotate by hand; plate lifts 20 mm with no lead tight.

What you're looking at

Four things come down from the build plate: the silicone heater pad's two mains leads, its earth ring terminal, and the bed thermistor. The bed WAGO mount splits them out; the 2×2 splicer PCB joins the thermistor pair to the mainboard cable.

Never L and N in one block

each 2-way WAGO is one node, so a block is all-Live or all-Neutral. Do not take the M4×6 BHCS out; back it out three turns only. It is the screw Step 03.6 left in place for this moment.

docs.title: Step 10.13 — Measure the bed heater before you connect it
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 1 — Mains: inlet → switch → PSU → SSR → bed heater13 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.13 — Measure the bed heater before you connect it
docs.text:
Step 13 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do:

  1. Meter on Ω. Measure Bed L → Bed N at the free ends of the two extensions.
  2. Measure Bed L → the aluminium plate and Bed N → the aluminium plate, touching the M4×6 PE screw head.

Parts:

  • multimeter, the Bed L and Bed N extension leads (free ends still unconnected below the WAGO breakout)

Check

All three readings must land in these bands.

What you're looking at

You are measuring the heater pad before it can ever be energised. Across its own two leads it should read a few tens of ohms; to the aluminium plate it is bonded to, nothing at all. The photo identifies which lead is which.

Why 'tens of ohms', and how to compute your own target

LDO does not publish the pad's wattage on the Rev D BOM, so derive the number yourself: R = V² ÷ P, using the mains voltage the pad is wound for and the wattage printed on the pad's own label. Worked examples — not your value: 750 W at 120 V → 19.2 Ω; 750 W at 230 V → 70.5 Ω. Read your own label, do the division, and expect the meter to land within a few ohms of it.

Measurement Expected Bed L → Bed N a stable reading in the tens of ohms. Not 0 Ω. Not OL. Bed L → plate / PE OL on your meter's highest Ω range Bed N → plate / PE OL on your meter's highest Ω range

A dead short means the pad is damaged and must not be connected. OL on L → N means an open pad or 125 °C thermal fuse — but first re-seat both leads in their WAGO levers and measure again, because an unseated core reads the same. Either way, do not go on until the number is right.

Source: LDO wiring guide § Wiring the bed heater · LDO Rev D 350 BOM · LDO wiring guide image bed_heater_wires_revd.jpg

Do: Run the Bed L lead from the bed WAGO breakout down through the deck opening, along the duct, to SSR terminal LOAD 1. PH2, tight.

Parts:

  • Bed L cable ×1

Terminal 1 = bed, terminal 2 = mains Live, LDO's convention from the photo.

What you're looking at

Terminal 1 is the relay's output, live only while the SSR is switched on. Landing the bed's Live lead here is what makes the heater controllable instead of permanently connected to the mains.

docs.title: Step 10.15 — Bed Neutral and bed PE → the WAGO bus
docs.text:
Step 15 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do: Bed N into a spare port of the blue N WAGO. Bed PE into a spare port of the yellow PE WAGO.

Parts:

  • Bed N and Bed PE leads

Check

Continuity from the C14 earth pin, through the PE WAGO, to bare aluminium on the build plate.

What you're looking at

The heater's return path, Neutral, and the plate's earth both go straight to the bus, unswitched; only the Live side passes through the relay. That earth connection keeps the aluminium plate safe to touch if the heater pad ever fails onto it.

docs.title: Step 10.16 — Frame PE
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 1 — Mains: inlet → switch → PSU → SSR → bed heater16 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.16 — Frame PE
docs.text:
Step 16 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do:

  1. Sandwich the ring terminal between the two M5 locking washers and screw the stack into a bottom-rail extrusion slot, on bare metal. Scrape the anodising under the washer.
  2. Land the other end in the yellow PE WAGO.

Parts:

  • FRAME PE cable ×1, M5 locking washer ×2, M5×10 BHCS + M5 roll-in T-nut (verify on bench)

Check

From the C14 earth pin to a far frame corner: under 2–3 Ω. Probe a screw head, T-nut or bare cut end, never anodising.

What you're looking at

FRAME PE is the single green/yellow lead that bonds the whole aluminium frame to earth. Anodising, the hard oxide layer on the extrusions, is an insulator, so the ring terminal must bite through to bare metal. The two locking washers do the biting.

Good stopping point · ~30 min since the last one

every mains connection made and pull-tested: SSR LOAD 1/2, bed L/N/PE, frame PE. Cord still out of the room and the DC side untouched. Next segment is LDO's Checkpoint #1 — start it only when you have an uninterrupted 25 minutes.

docs.title: Step 10.17 — De-energise and set up
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 2 — Checkpoint #1, exactly as LDO writes it17 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.17 — De-energise and set up
docs.text:
Step 17 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

(no image — see text)

Do: Confirm the C13 power cord is not plugged into the inlet and is not in the room. Set the meter to continuity/beeper and test it by shorting the probes.

Parts:

  • multimeter

Check

The meter beeps on a dead short. No cord anywhere near the machine.

What you're looking at

LDO's own words: "Incorrect wiring of AC/mains can be dangerous — therefore, always double check your work, and then triple check it once more." Do all seven steps in order. Do not skip ahead to the 24 V section.

Who is in the room (00a.2): one adult at the machine for 10.17–10.23. She is out of the room until 10.24; at 10.23 nobody but the person with a hand on the switch is within reach of the machine.

Nothing to look at on the machine; this step is about the meter and the absent cord. Continuity mode makes the meter beep whenever a conductive path joins its two probes, and that beep is the instrument for every measurement in this section.

Source: LDO wiring guide § Checkpoint 1

← PreviousStep 10.16 — Frame PE

Next →Step 10.18 — Colour groups are shorted

docs.title: Step 10.18 — Colour groups are shorted
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 2 — Checkpoint #1, exactly as LDO writes it18 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.18 — Colour groups are shorted
docs.text:
Step 18 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

(no image — see text)

Do:

  1. One colour at a time, park one probe on the first node in its list and walk the other probe along every node after it.
  2. Rocker ON for the L and N lists, either position for PE.

Parts:

  • multimeter on continuity (beeper), then on Ω for the frame and plate rows

Check

Every row beeps. Where a resistance is given, switch to Ω and read it.

What you're looking at

You are proving that each conductor colour is one electrical node from the inlet pin to its last destination: out to the PSU screws, the relay, the bed and the frame. A core that never seated in its lever looks perfect from outside.

PE — green/yellow (rocker on or off — the earth path is never switched)

From the C14 E pin to … Expected every occupied port of the PE WAGO beeps, < 1 Ω PSU screw 3 FG (⏚) beeps, < 1 Ω bed PE ring — probe the head of the plate's M4×6 screw beeps, a few Ω or less frame PE ring — probe its screw head, then a T-nut or bare cut end at a far corner beeps, < 2–3 Ω PSU chassis — a bare case screw beeps, a few Ω or less (the case is bonded to FG inside the supply)

N — blue (rocker ON)

From the C14 N pin to … Expected every occupied port of the N WAGO beeps PSU screw 2 N beeps bed N — the pad's N lead at its bed-WAGO port beeps

L — brown (rocker ON, fuse fitted)

From the C14 L pin to … Expected the fuse — drawer in: it sits between the L pin and every row below, so those rows prove it in circuit (10.5 proved L pin → brown through it). To read it alone: drawer out, probe cap to cap — beeps; OL is a blown fuse — then refit the drawer before the next row beeps every occupied port of the L WAGO beeps PSU screw 1 L beeps SSR LOAD 2 beeps

Bed L branch — a node of its own until the SSR conducts

From SSR LOAD 1 to … Expected the Bed L extension's bed-WAGO port, and the pad's Bed L lead beeps SSR LOAD 2 silent — that is step 10.21

A node that does not beep is a core that did not seat in its WAGO lever, or a screw terminal clamped on insulation. Re-strip and re-seat it, then repeat that colour's whole list.

Source: LDO wiring guide § Checkpoint 1

← PreviousStep 10.17 — De-energise and set up

Next →Step 10.19 — L, N and PE are isolated from each other

docs.title: Step 10.19 — L, N and PE are isolated from each other
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 2 — Checkpoint #1, exactly as LDO writes it19 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.19 — L, N and PE are isolated from each other
docs.text:
Step 19 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

(no image — see text)

Do:

  1. Probe L→N, L→PE, N→PE at the WAGO blocks, rocker on, then again off.
  2. Probe the same three pairs at the PSU screws: 3 FG ↔ 1 L, 3 FG ↔ 2 N, 1 L ↔ 2 N.

Parts:

  • multimeter

Check

Silence on all nine measurements, and OL on your meter's highest Ω range.

What you're looking at

The mirror image of the previous check: the three buses must have no path between them at all. Live touching Neutral is a short across the mains; Live touching earth is what makes the metalwork lethal.

If L→N beeps: something is bridging the mains. The candidates are a stray strand at a WAGO or a shorted SSR — with the relay open, the bed pad itself cannot bridge L to N. Lift the brown lead off SSR LOAD 2 to take the whole bed branch out of the picture and re-measure: silent now means the fault is on the SSR/bed side; still beeping means a strand at a block.

Tip

a momentary tick on 1 L ↔ 2 N as the PSU's input filter charges from the meter is normal; a steady beep is not.

Source: LDO wiring guide § Checkpoint 1

docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 1 — Mains: inlet → switch → PSU → SSR → bed heater2 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.2 — Set the PSU input-voltage selector
docs.text:
Step 2 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do: Find the red slide switch in the cut-out on the PSU's long side. With the flat screwdriver, slide it so the window shows 115 for a US 110/120 V supply, 230 for a 230 V supply.

Parts:

  • Meanwell LRS-200-24 ×1

Check

Read the number in the window out loud and compare it to your wall socket.

What you're looking at

The grey brick is the Meanwell LRS-200-24, the 24 V supply for everything except the bed heater. The second photo is the small red slide switch in its side, which sets 115 V or 230 V mains.

The yellow warning label on the PSU lid says the same thing: "AC INPUT VOLTAGE CAN BE SELECTED BY SWITCH, CHECK INPUT VOLTAGE AVOIDING DAMAGE BEFORE POWER ON."

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: EU kits may ship the Meanwell RSP-200-24 instead. That unit has power-factor correction and a universal AC input — there is no selector and nothing to set. If your PSU has no red switch, you have the RSP; skip this step. src

Source: Voron manual p.181 · LDO wiring guide § Preparing the power supply unit · LDO wiring photo psu_switch.jpg

docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 2 — Checkpoint #1, exactly as LDO writes it20 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.20 — The switch actually switches
docs.text:
Step 20 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

(no image — see text)

Do: With the meter across the C14 L pin and a brown WAGO node, toggle the rocker.

Parts:

  • multimeter

Check

Beeps with the rocker on, silent with it off. Repeat for N. If either stays connected, go back to step 10.5.

What you're looking at

The rocker in the inlet module is the machine's only mains isolator, so it has to genuinely break both poles rather than just one. This check watches the meter change state as you toggle it.

Source: LDO wiring guide § Checkpoint 1

docs.title: Step 10.21 — The SSR is open when unpowered
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 2 — Checkpoint #1, exactly as LDO writes it21 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.21 — The SSR is open when unpowered
docs.text:
Step 21 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do: Measure SSR LOAD 1 → LOAD 2 with nothing energised.

Parts:

  • multimeter

Check

No beep, and INPUT 3/4 are still empty.

What you're looking at

With nothing on terminals 3 and 4 the relay's semiconductor switch must be off, so its two mains terminals should have no path between them. The close-up shows the terminals you are probing. It is a Rev C bay, so read only the SSR body.

Source: LDO wiring guide § Checkpoint 1 · LDO wiring photo SSR_Close_Up.jpg

docs.title: Step 10.22 — Re-check the voltage selector
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 2 — Checkpoint #1, exactly as LDO writes it22 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.22 — Re-check the voltage selector
docs.text:
Step 22 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do: LDO: "Check again that the power supply voltage input switch is set to the correct value: 115V vs 230V." Look at the window a second time, now that the PSU is wired and the light is worse.

Parts: none.

Check

The number in the window matches your mains. If you have the EU RSP-200-24 there is no switch and nothing to check.

What you're looking at

The same red slide switch as step 10.2, read a second time now that the PSU is wired in place and half in shadow. It is the one setting that destroys the supply on first switch-on.

Source: LDO wiring guide § Checkpoint 1 · LDO wiring photo psu_switch.jpg

Next →Step 10.23 — First power-on, then off again

docs.title: Step 10.23 — First power-on, then off again
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 2 — Checkpoint #1, exactly as LDO writes it23 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.23 — First power-on, then off again
docs.text:
Step 23 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

(no image — see text)

Do:

  1. Rocker OFF, cord into the inlet then the wall.
  2. Everyone back; stand aside, hand on the rocker, switch ON. Look, listen and smell ten seconds.
  3. Rocker OFF, unplug wall then inlet, cord out of the room.

Parts:

  • C13 power cord ×1. No meter

Check

All three observations during the ten seconds.

What you're looking at

The only moment in this chapter when mains is present. The rocker lamp and the PSU's indicator LED are the two observations that say the mains half works; ten seconds of looking, listening and smelling is the whole test. Nothing is measured live.

Who is in the room (00a.2): one adult, standing to the side, hand on the switch. Nobody else within reach of the machine; she is out of the room.

Observe Expected Inlet rocker illuminates PSU indicator LED lights green Noise / smell none. Any buzz, click-cycling or smell → rocker OFF, then pull the plug at the wall

Everything from here to the end of the chapter is done dead.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: this is the only power-on in the chapter. The Leviathan, Pi and toolboard are all still unpowered — the PSU's DC terminals are empty. Never meter a live block: the PSU's +V/−V screws share an uncovered block with live N and L. Keep your free hand behind your back. src

Good stopping point · ~25 min since the last one

Checkpoint #1 passed end to end and the machine was powered once and switched off. Cord unplugged and back out of the room. Everything from here is done dead.

Source: LDO wiring guide § Checkpoint 1

← PreviousStep 10.22 — Re-check the voltage selector

Next →Step 10.24 — PSU → Leviathan board supply

docs.title: Step 10.24 — PSU → Leviathan board supply
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 3 — 24 V distribution24 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.24 — PSU → Leviathan board supply
docs.text:
Step 24 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do:

  1. TO MB end onto the PSU +V/−V, 24V end onto the Leviathan's Vin 24V / Board. Red to +, black to −.
  2. Tag the cable. Tags and wire colours are the only end markers (verify on bench).

Parts:

  • 24V PSU to MB cable ×1 (ends tagged 24V and TO MB), multimeter, cable tag

Check

0 V across PSU +V and −V, still 0 V ten seconds later. Polarity read twice, both ends. Cable tagged at the board end.

What you're looking at

24V PSU to MB is the kit lead that feeds the Leviathan's own electronics, and Vin 24V / Board is the screw-terminal pair on the mainboard that accepts it. The board has a second, separate supply input for the stepper drivers, which is wired next.

Source: LDO Rev D photo S4 24 V/SSR mapping · LDO wiring guide § Connecting 24V · LDO Leviathan V1.3 guide (manual p.8)

← PreviousStep 10.23 — First power-on, then off again

docs.title: Step 10.25 — PSU → Leviathan HV stepper supply
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 3 — 24 V distribution25 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.25 — PSU → Leviathan HV stepper supply
docs.text:
Step 25 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do: TO MB HV end onto the PSU's +V / −V terminals, alongside the board supply. HV end onto the Leviathan terminal silkscreened Vin 24-48V / HV-Steppers.

Parts:

  • HV to MB HV cable ×1 (ends tagged HV and TO MB HV)

Check

Polarity. Both PSU-side cables share the same +V/−V pair: each ferrule fully under its screw, no strand crossing between +V and −V.

What you're looking at

Vin 24-48V / HV-Steppers is that second input, feeding only the two HV stepper drivers, the TMC5160 chips that run the A and B motors. On this build both inputs come from the same 24 V PSU; the port simply also accepts up to 48 V.

Source: LDO Rev D photo S4 mainboard/PSU wired · LDO wiring guide § Connecting 24V

docs.title: Step 10.26 — PSU → USB adapter PCB (toolhead 24 V)
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 3 — 24 V distribution26 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.26 — PSU → USB adapter PCB (toolhead 24 V)
docs.text:
Step 26 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do: TO TOOLHEAD end onto the PSU +V/−V. 24V IN end onto the USB adapter PCB on its DIN clip. This is what powers the Nitehawk down the umbilical.

Parts:

  • 24V power cable ×1 (ends tagged TO TOOLHEAD and 24V IN)

Check

Polarity at the USB adapter end matches the silkscreen. The adapter PCB's cover is the partial cover; see step 10.57.

What you're looking at

The USB adapter PCB on its DIN clip is the bay-side end of the toolhead link: 24 V and USB arrive on this side as two separate cables and leave on the other side as one umbilical. This step is the 24 V half.

Source: LDO Rev D photo S6 gantry-cable mapping · LDO wiring guide § Connecting 24V

← PreviousStep 10.25 — PSU → Leviathan HV stepper supply

Next →Step 10.27 — Leviathan HEATBED → SSR INPUT

docs.title: Step 10.27 — Leviathan HEATBED → SSR INPUT
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 3 — 24 V distribution27 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.27 — Leviathan HEATBED → SSR INPUT
docs.text:
Step 27 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do: SSR SIG end onto the SSR's INPUT 3&4: red to INPUT 3, black to INPUT 4. To SSR end onto the Leviathan's HEATBED terminals.

Parts:

  • SSR to MB cable ×1 (ends tagged SSR SIG and To SSR)

Check

Red on 3, black on 4, and red on the Leviathan HEATBED +. Trace the pair from board to relay with a finger.

What you're looking at

HEATBED on the Leviathan is a low-current DC output; it never carries bed power, it only tells the relay when to conduct. This polarised red/black pair is the entire control link between the firmware and a mains heater.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: reversed INPUT 3/4 means the SSR never fires and the bed stays cold. The dangerous failure is the other one — a shorted relay, which leaves the bed permanently live with no thermal control; that is what 10.21 and 10.78 test for. src

Source: LDO Rev D photo S4 24 V/SSR mapping · LDO wiring guide § Connecting 24V

← PreviousStep 10.26 — PSU → USB adapter PCB (toolhead 24 V)

Next →Step 10.28 — Set the FAN2 and FAN3 jumpers to 24 V

docs.title: Step 10.28 — Set the FAN2 and FAN3 jumpers to 24 V
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 3 — 24 V distribution28 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.28 — Set the FAN2 and FAN3 jumpers to 24 V
docs.text:
Step 28 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do: Fit a jumper on Fan2 and one on Fan3, both in the 24 V position. Leave Fan0, Fan1 and Probe bare.

Parts:

  • 2 of the jumpers removed in Ch 09

Check

Exactly two jumpers on the board, both on the 24 V pins, on Fan2 and Fan3. Count them.

What you're looking at

The jumper block from step 10.3, now being set. A jumper across a port's 24 V pins selects that port's output voltage. The diagram shows the end state: five headers, Fan2 and Fan3 fitted at 24 V, three left bare.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: on a Nitehawk build the hotend, part fan and probe all live on the toolboard, so the Leviathan's probe and Fan0/Fan1 ports stay unused — that is why they stay unjumpered. src · BOM

Source: LDO Leviathan V1.3 guide (manual p.7) · LDO Rev D 350 BOM · Leviathan repo wiring_V1.3.jpg

← PreviousStep 10.27 — Leviathan HEATBED → SSR INPUT

Next →Step 10.29 — Meter the 24 V rail for shorts

docs.title: Step 10.29 — Meter the 24 V rail for shorts
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 3 — 24 V distribution29 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.29 — Meter the 24 V rail for shorts
docs.text:
Step 29 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

(no image — see text)

Do:

  1. With the PSU unplugged, measure +V → −V at the PSU on the Ω range.
  2. Repeat across the Leviathan's Vin 24V, its Vin 24-48V and the USB adapter's 24 V input.

Parts:

  • multimeter

Check

Finite resistance that rises, hundreds of ohms climbing into the kΩ, the same at all three inputs. Nothing reads 0 Ω or beeps continuously.

What you're looking at

A resistance sanity check across the 24 V rail you have just wired, with no power anywhere. A shorted rail reads like a piece of wire; a healthy one climbs as the boards' input capacitors charge from the meter's own test current.

Good stopping point · ~25 min since the last one

24 V distribution complete: board supply, HV stepper supply, USB-adapter feed, HEATBED→SSR control pair, Fan2/Fan3 jumpers at 24 V, and every rail metered with no short. Nothing above deck touched yet.

Source: LDO wiring guide § Connecting 24V · survey §5.2 W8

← PreviousStep 10.28 — Set the FAN2 and FAN3 jumpers to 24 V

docs.title: Step 10.3 — Confirm the Leviathan voltage-selection jumpers are off
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 1 — Mains: inlet → switch → PSU → SSR → bed heater3 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.3 — Confirm the Leviathan voltage-selection jumpers are off
docs.text:
Step 3 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do: Find the jumper block silkscreened Voltage selection for Z-Probe and Fans, next to the fan headers. All five positions, Probe, Fan0, Fan1, Fan2, Fan3, must be bare.

Parts:

  • Leviathan mainboard ×1

Check

Five empty jumper pairs. Count them.

What you're looking at

The Leviathan is LDO's mainboard: it drives six motors, reads the bed thermistor and endstops, and supplies the Raspberry Pi with 5 V. Its jumper block is five pin pairs choosing 24 V or 5 V for the probe port and four fan ports.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: this build uses an active toolboard, so the Leviathan's own probe port and Fan0/Fan1 stay unused and unjumpered for the whole build. A 24 V jumper on a port feeding a 5 V device destroys the device. src · Leviathan V1.3 manual p.7

Source: LDO wiring guide § Preparing the mainboard · LDO Leviathan V1.3 guide (manual p.7) · Leviathan repo wiring_V1.3.jpg

docs.title: Step 10.30 — Insulate the inductive probe
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 4 — Above deck: probe, endstops, nozzle probe, lighting30 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.30 — Insulate the inductive probe
docs.text:
Step 30 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do:

  1. Wrap at least two layers of fibreglass tape around the front and sides of the probe body, offset slightly up from the bottom edge.
  2. Do not cover the back or the bottom.

Parts:

  • Omron inductive probe (fitted to the X carriage in Ch 05/07), fibreglass tape 2×12 cm ×1

Check

The sensing face and the back are bare, and the tape does not bulge past the probe's lower rim.

What you're looking at

The inductive probe is the small Omron sensor on the X carriage that senses the metal bed for gantry levelling; it never sets Z=0. The fibreglass tape is a heat shield against the hotend beside it, front and sides only.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: LDO note p.143 — the tape is a heat shield against the hotend, not a spacer. Too much of it and the probe stops triggering. src

Source: Voron manual p.143 · LDO wiring guide § Insulating the Z-probe · LDO wiki probe insulation photo

← PreviousStep 10.29 — Meter the 24 V rail for shorts

docs.title: Step 10.31 — Read the XY endstop cable labels
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 4 — Above deck: probe, endstops, nozzle probe, lighting31 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.31 — Read the XY endstop cable labels
docs.text:
Step 31 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do: Read the two 3-pin connectors' labels.

Parts:

  • XY endstop cable ×1 (4-pin JST-XH one end, two 3-pin JST-XH the other)

Check

Read the two 3-pin connectors and match one row.

What you're looking at

One cable carries both limit switches: a single 4-pin plug at the gantry end that splits into two 3-pin plugs at the mainboard end. The photo is LDO's side-by-side of a correctly labelled cable and one from the mis-labelled batch.

Labels read Meaning XES and YES correct cable — go to step 10.33 X Stop and Y Stop known bad batch — do step 10.32 first

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: a mis-pinned cable will not damage the Leviathan, but X and Y homing simply will not work and you will not find out until Ch 13. Check now. src

Source: LDO wiring guide § Wiring the XY endstop · LDO XY endstop reconnecting guide

← PreviousStep 10.30 — Insulate the inductive probe

Next →Step 10.32 — Repin the XY endstop cable (only if labelled X Stop / Y Stop)

docs.title: Step 10.32 — Repin the XY endstop cable (only if labelled X Stop / Y Stop)
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 4 — Above deck: probe, endstops, nozzle probe, lighting32 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.32 — Repin the XY endstop cable (only if labelled X Stop / Y Stop)
docs.text:
Step 32 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do:

  1. On X Stop, press the position 3 retention tab down, pull the wire out, bend the tab up, and insert it at position 2.
  2. On Y Stop, move the wire from 2 to 3. Light force only.

Parts:

  • XY endstop cable ×1, tweezers or the supplied 2.5 mm flat screwdriver

Check

Meter on continuity, against LDO's map:

What you're looking at

Inside a JST housing each crimped wire is held by a small springy retention tab; press the tab flat and the wire slides out, bend it back up and it locks into its new position. The photo shows that tab.

JST-XH 4P pin goes to 4 X Stop pin 2 3 X Stop pin 1 2 Y Stop pin 1 1 Y Stop pin 3

All four beep, and each repinned wire survives a light tug.

Source: LDO XY endstop reconnecting guide · LDO guide image retention_tab.jpg

← PreviousStep 10.31 — Read the XY endstop cable labels

Next →Step 10.33 — XY endstop cable → the gantry PCB

docs.title: Step 10.33 — XY endstop cable → the gantry PCB
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 4 — Above deck: probe, endstops, nozzle probe, lighting33 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.33 — XY endstop cable → the gantry PCB
docs.text:
Step 33 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do: Plug the 4-pin end into the XY endstop PCB. Leave the two 3-pin ends free; they reach the Leviathan in step 10.45. Dress the cable along the right Y extrusion toward the rear-right, ready for the Y chain.

Parts:

  • XY endstop cable ×1, XY endstop PCB (on the right XY joint — bagged in Ch 05, mounted at Ch 09 Steps 09.32–09.33)

Check

The connector is fully home and the cable leaves the PCB without loading the switch bodies.

What you're looking at

The XY endstop pod is the small PCB on the right XY joint carrying both the X and the Y microswitch. X homes to the right and Y to the rear, so the pod sits where both limits are hit.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: the kit uses one XY microswitch PCB, not the manual's hall-effect pods. Manual p.162 and p.169 are skipped entirely. src

Source: LDO Rev D photo S6 gantry-cable mapping · LDO wiring guide § Wiring the XY endstop · LDO Build Notes p.162, p.163, p.169

← PreviousStep 10.32 — Repin the XY endstop cable (only if labelled X Stop / Y Stop)

Next →Step 10.34 — Nozzle-probe (Z endstop) cable

docs.title: Step 10.34 — Nozzle-probe (Z endstop) cable
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 4 — Above deck: probe, endstops, nozzle probe, lighting34 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.34 — Nozzle-probe (Z endstop) cable
docs.text:
Step 34 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do: Plug the 3-pin connector onto the nozzle-probe PCB. Route the lead across the deck to the wire opening, following LDO's build-plate mapping; it drops through alongside the bed cables.

Parts:

  • Z endstop cable ×1, nozzle-probe PCB (assembled and mounted in Ch 09)

Check

Press the 5 mm shaft down with a finger: it moves freely, clicks the D2F, and springs back.

What you're looking at

The nozzle probe is LDO's mechanical Z endstop: a sprung 5 mm pin below the bed that the nozzle itself presses down onto a D2F microswitch, on the little PCB Ch 09 mounted. This, not the inductive probe, is what sets Z=0.

Caution

The small GT2 pulley used as the shaft collar, built in Ch 09, has a set screw that stops the shaft falling out. It must not grip the shaft.

Good stopping point · ~25 min since the last one

probe taped, XY endstop cable read (and repinned if needed) and plugged into the gantry PCB, nozzle-probe lead run to the deck opening. Both cables are loose on the gantry, not yet in a chain.

Source: LDO wiring guide § Assembling the nozzle probe · LDO wiring photo z_stop_final.jpg · Video: Part 8 @1:49:54 (differs: Euclid probe (Klicky fitted later, Part 11); this kit uses the Omron inductive probe + LDO nozzle probe, Klicky bagged · BTT Octopus + separate Raspberry Pi; this kit is a Leviathan with the Pi mounted on it)

docs.title: Step 10.35 — Assemble the eight COB light-strip mounts
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 4 — Above deck: probe, endstops, nozzle probe, lighting35 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.35 — Assemble the eight COB light-strip mounts
docs.text:
Step 35 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

(no image — see COB README)

Do:

  1. Melt two inserts into one half of each mount, plus the Z chain guide's two and the retainer bracket's.
  2. Close the halves with two M3×6 FHCS. Four mounts per strip: three 100 mm plus one 50 mm.

Parts:

  • cob_light_strip_mount_100mm ×6, cob_light_strip_mount_50mm ×2, M3×5×4 heat-set inserts ×16, M3×6 FHCS ×16 — plus, for the same sitting, the z_chain_guide (2 inserts) and the [a]_z_chain_retainer_bracket (p.204 heat-set icon; count its bosses, verify on bench)

Check

The halves close flush and no mount rocks on glass. Guide and bracket inserts flush, an M3 screw starting by hand in each.

What you're looking at

COB light strips are the chamber lighting: a continuous line of LEDs under one phosphor rather than separate dots. Each printed mount is a two-piece clamshell that grips the strip and bolts to a frame extrusion.

Source: LDOVoron2 STLs/COB Light Strip · LDO wiring guide § Routing the LED strips

← PreviousStep 10.34 — Nozzle-probe (Z endstop) cable

docs.title: Step 10.36 — Mount the COB strips left and right
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 4 — Above deck: probe, endstops, nozzle probe, lighting36 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.36 — Mount the COB strips left and right
docs.text:
Step 36 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do:

  1. Slide four mounts into the top-left extrusion's inner face and four into the top-right, evenly spaced.
  2. Fasten each with two M3×8 SHCS into hammerhead nuts. Press the strips into their channels, leads to the rear.

Parts:

  • COB LED strips ×2, assembled mounts ×8, M3×8 SHCS ×16, M3 hammerhead T-nut ×16

Check

Both strips are level, fully seated, and their leads meet near the rear centre of the ceiling with slack to spare.

What you're looking at

The strips go on the inner faces of the two top side extrusions, aimed down into the chamber. The diagram is LDO's routing plan for both strips and for the leads that meet at the rear.

Source: LDO wiring guide § Routing the LED strips · LDO wiring photo led_route.png

docs.title: Step 10.37 — Mount the LED junction PCB on its spacer
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 4 — Above deck: probe, endstops, nozzle probe, lighting37 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.37 — Mount the LED junction PCB on its spacer
docs.text:
Step 37 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do: Stack the PCB on the printed spacer and bolt the sandwich to the inner face of the rear top extrusion. Plug the left and right strip leads into two of the three ports.

Parts:

  • 3×2 XH splicer PCB ×1, 2x3 Splitter Spacer ×1 (LDO-supplied printed), M3×8 SHCS ×2, M3 hammerhead T-nut ×2

Check

The spacer is fitted. LDO calls it out twice: bolting the bare PCB against the extrusion shorts it. Nothing on the PCB's underside touches aluminium.

What you're looking at

The 3×2 splicer PCB is a passive junction board: the two strip leads plug into two ports, the third carries one cable down to the mainboard. The printed spacer holds the bare board off the extrusion, which would otherwise short its underside.

Source: LDO wiring guide § Routing the LED strips · LDO wiring photo led_splitter_placement.jpg

← PreviousStep 10.36 — Mount the COB strips left and right

docs.title: Step 10.38 — Route the LED lead down to the deck and close the slots
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 4 — Above deck: probe, endstops, nozzle probe, lighting38 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.38 — Route the LED lead down to the deck and close the slots
docs.text:
Step 38 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do:

  1. Run the junction PCB's third lead along the top rear extrusion slot, down a rear vertical extrusion, and into the deck.
  2. Press the 6 mm slot covers over every slot the cable occupies. Do this now.

Parts:

  • extrusion slot covers, 6 mm — up to 9

Check

No cable is visible outside a covered slot, and nothing crosses the gantry's Z travel.

What you're looking at

Extrusion slot covers are the flexible plastic strips that press into an empty extrusion groove; here they hide and protect the LED cable along its whole route down to the deck. Ch 11's top panel and Z-belt covers close this path for good.

Alternative: you may instead route through the Z-motor A opening; if you do, print the alternate Z-belt cover z_belt_cover_a_led.stl for Ch 11. Decide now, not in Ch 11. src

Source: LDO wiring guide § Routing the LED strips · LDO wiring photo led_final.jpg · LDOVoron2 z_belt_cover_a_led.stl · survey §5.2 W5 · Video: Part 9 @0:17:48

docs.title: Step 10.39 — Chamber thermistor, if your batch includes one
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 4 — Above deck: probe, endstops, nozzle probe, lighting39 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.39 — Chamber thermistor, if your batch includes one
docs.text:
Step 39 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

(no image — see text)

Do: Nothing on the Leviathan: the chamber thermistor lands on the toolboard's CT port, a Ch 08 step. If yours is still loose, dress its tip into free chamber air, away from the hotend and out of the toolhead's travel.

Parts:

  • chamber thermistor (batch-dependent)

Check

Your batch BOM says whether the part is in the kit. The Klipper config's [temperature_sensor chamber_temp] reads nhk:PB2, i.e. the toolboard, not the mainboard.

What you're looking at

The chamber thermistor is a small temperature sensor left hanging in free air inside the enclosure, reporting how hot the chamber has become. On a Rev D+ machine it belongs on the toolboard's CT port, not on any of the Leviathan's four thermistor inputs.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: the Leviathan has four thermistor inputs and it is tempting to put the chamber sensor on one of them. Do not — leviathan-printer-rev-d-sbv2.cfg expects it on the toolboard, anchored by the zip-tie loop on the CW2 cable cover. src

Good stopping point · ~35 min since the last one

eight COB mounts built, both strips mounted and plugged into the junction PCB on its spacer, LED lead routed and every occupied extrusion slot covered. Do not leave a slot open: Ch 11's top panel and Z-belt covers close this route for good.

Source: leviathan-printer-rev-d-sbv2.cfg · Nitehawk-SB V2 doc § Port and pin definitions · Video: Part 9 @1:36:20

docs.title: Step 10.4 — Fit the AC inlet into the printed plug panel
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 1 — Mains: inlet → switch → PSU → SSR → bed heater4 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.4 — Fit the AC inlet into the printed plug panel
docs.text:
Step 4 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do: Nothing to build. On the rear extrusion's panel, confirm the earth pin is at the top with the printer upright, the switch faces out, and both M3×10 FHCS are in. If not, go back to Ch 09 Steps 09.10–09.11.

Parts:

  • none — already done in Ch 09
  • this step only confirms it

Check

The inlet sits square with no rock, the fuse drawer opens freely, the rocker clicks both ways, and no spade terminal is connected.

What you're looking at

power_inlet_IECGS_1mm is the printed panel that carries mains into the machine. The module in it combines three parts: the C14 inlet, the on/off rocker, and the fuse drawer. The manual page is drawn for the stock separate inlet and does not match your frame.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: LDO note p.156 — the panel is power_inlet_IECGS_1mm (1.0 mm AC inlet with integrated switch), never the manual's stock plug panel. src

Good stopping point · ~15 min since the last one

printer on its side, PSU selector set, Leviathan jumpers off, the Ch 09 inlet panel confirmed. No mains wiring started. Do not start the inlet-to-WAGO run until you can finish it: the next segment ends with the whole inlet→WAGO→PSU chain terminated.

Source: Voron manual p.156 · LDO Build Notes p.156 · LDO wiring guide § Preparing the inlet · Video: Part 7 @0:15:11

docs.title: Step 10.40 — Tag every stepper cable before you plug anything in
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 5 — Leviathan connections40 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.40 — Tag every stepper cable before you plug anything in
docs.text:
Step 40 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do: Transcribe the table below onto tags and fit one to each motor cable at the board end. Positions are given "as if standing in front of an upright printer and looking towards it."

Parts:

  • cable tags (supplied) ×7

Check

Seven tags written, six cables tagged, and you can trace each cable back to the motor it came from without guessing.

What you're looking at

Six identical 4-pin motor cables arrive at the board and nothing about them says which corner each came from. LDO's mapping photo names every port on the Leviathan; the diagram shows both HV-STEPPER ports and STEPPER-0..3 by corner, and which ports stay empty.

Stepper Physical position Controller port A rear right of gantry HV-STEPPER-1 B rear left of gantry HV-STEPPER-0 Z0 front left STEPPER-0 Z1 rear left STEPPER-1 Z2 rear right STEPPER-2 Z3 front right STEPPER-3 (not used) — STEPPER-4

Source: LDO Rev D photo S1 stepper mapping · LDO wiring guide § Connecting steppers · Video: Part 6 @0:25:08

← PreviousStep 10.39 — Chamber thermistor, if your batch includes one

Next →Step 10.41 — A motor → HV-STEPPER-1

docs.title: Step 10.41 — A motor → HV-STEPPER-1
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 5 — Leviathan connections41 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.41 — A motor → HV-STEPPER-1
docs.text:
Step 41 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do: Plug the A motor, rear right, into the TMC5160 port LDO's diagram labels HV-STEPPER-1. Match your board against S1_mapping.jpg rather than the silkscreen, which the Leviathan V1.3 manual writes as Stepper X and Stepper Y.

Parts:

  • A motor cable ×1 (4-pin JST-XH)

Check

Connector fully home, latch engaged, cable dressed into the duct with no tension on the header.

What you're looking at

HV-STEPPER-1 is one of the two high-voltage driver sockets on the Leviathan: a TMC5160, the strongest driver pair on the board, reserved for the two CoreXY motors. The 4-pin plug carries the motor's two coils, two wires each.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: never plug or unplug a stepper with power on, and never spin a connected motor fast by hand or shove the gantry — a fast move generates back-EMF the driver has to absorb. The slow, driver-disabled (M84) hand moves that Ch 13 and Ch 06b ask for are fine. src

Source: LDO Rev D photo S1 steppers wired · LDO wiring guide § Connecting steppers

docs.title: Step 10.42 — B motor → HV-STEPPER-0
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 5 — Leviathan connections42 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.42 — B motor → HV-STEPPER-0
docs.text:
Step 42 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do: Plug the B motor, rear left, into HV-STEPPER-0, the other 5160 port.

Parts:

  • B motor cable ×1

Check

A and B are in the two 5160 ports and nowhere else. A 2209 would badly under-drive the motor.

What you're looking at

HV-STEPPER-0 is the other TMC5160 socket. A and B are the two rear-corner motors that between them produce every X and Y move, so both belong on the high-current drivers; the five STEPPER-n sockets alongside are weaker TMC2209s.

If your B motor cable is too short to follow the mapping photo, LDO publishes an alternate route: alternate B-motor mapping and B-motor cable wiring. Take the alternate route rather than pulling the cable tight. src

Source: LDO Rev D photo S1 stepper mapping · LDO wiring guide § Connecting steppers

docs.title: Step 10.43 — Z0–Z3 → STEPPER-0 to STEPPER-3
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 5 — Leviathan connections43 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.43 — Z0–Z3 → STEPPER-0 to STEPPER-3
docs.text:
Step 43 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do: Working left to right along the 2209 header row as S1_mapping.jpg shows it, STEPPER-3, STEPPER-2, STEPPER-1, STEPPER-0, plug in Z3 front right, Z2 rear right, Z1 rear left, Z0 front left. Leave STEPPER-4 empty; the extruder lives on the toolboard.

Parts:

  • Z motor cables ×4

Check

Four connectors, four tags, and each tag's physical position matches the corner its cable physically runs to. STEPPER-4 is empty.

What you're looking at

STEPPER-0 to STEPPER-3 are four of those TMC2209 sockets, one per Z motor, Z0–Z3 being the four corners that lift the gantry independently. STEPPER-4 would carry the extruder on a normal build; here the extruder motor is driven by the toolboard instead, so it stays empty.

Verification deferred: the definitive test is STEPPER_BUZZ per motor in Ch 13. If a corner buzzes that you did not name, swap the two cables — do not edit the config.

Source: LDO Rev D photo S1 steppers wired · LDO wiring guide § Connecting steppers

Next →Step 10.44 — Bed thermistor → TH1

docs.title: Step 10.44 — Bed thermistor → TH1
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 5 — Leviathan connections44 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.44 — Bed thermistor → TH1
docs.text:
Step 44 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do: Before plugging it in, measure it against the table in step 10.76. Then plug it into the Leviathan thermistor port silkscreened TH1. Polarity does not matter on a thermistor.

Parts:

  • Bed TH cable ×1 (2-pin JST-XH)

Check

TH1, not TH0. TH0 is the hotend port and is unused on a Nitehawk build; the config reads the bed on PA2 = TH1.

What you're looking at

TH1 is a two-pin thermistor input. A thermistor is just a resistor whose value changes with temperature, so the port only measures resistance and there is no polarity to get wrong. The bed's sensor lands here; TH0 beside it is the hotend input, unused on this build.

Source: LDO Rev D photo S5 build-plate mapping · LDO wiring guide § Connecting build plate · LDO Leviathan V1.3 guide (manual p.9)

← PreviousStep 10.43 — Z0–Z3 → STEPPER-0 to STEPPER-3

docs.title: Step 10.45 — XY endstops → X-ENDSTOP and Y-ENDSTOP
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 5 — Leviathan connections45 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.45 — XY endstops → X-ENDSTOP and Y-ENDSTOP
docs.text:
Step 45 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do: XES / X Stop into the port labelled X-ENDSTOP; YES / Y Stop into Y-ENDSTOP. LDO's mapping photo labels the three endstop headers Z STOP / Y STOP / X STOP in that order along the board.

Parts:

  • the two 3-pin ends of the XY endstop cable

Check

Both fully seated. Press each microswitch on the gantry PCB with a fingertip and feel a distinct click.

What you're looking at

The two 3-pin ends of the cable from step 10.31 finally reach the board. Each endstop port watches one switch open or close a circuit to ground, and that transition is what tells Klipper the axis has reached its limit.

Source: LDO Rev D photo S6 gantry-cable mapping · LDO wiring guide § Connecting the gantry cables

docs.title: Step 10.46 — Nozzle probe → Z-ENDSTOP
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 5 — Leviathan connections46 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.46 — Nozzle probe → Z-ENDSTOP
docs.text:
Step 46 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do: Plug the nozzle-probe lead into the port labelled Z-ENDSTOP.

Parts:

  • Z endstop cable ×1 (3-pin)

Check

Z-ENDSTOP, not Z-PROBE. The Leviathan's Z-PROBE header stays empty for the whole build; the inductive probe is on the toolboard's PROBE port, read as nhk:PC15.

What you're looking at

Z-ENDSTOP and Z-PROBE are two different headers a few millimetres apart on the same board. The mechanical nozzle probe belongs on Z-ENDSTOP; Z-PROBE stays empty for the entire build, because the inductive probe is wired to the toolboard instead.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: the stock config's comment says "Connected to Z-PROBE" above a nhk: pin. The comment is stale; the pin is authoritative. src

Good stopping point · ~30 min since the last one

six steppers tagged and plugged on their mapped ports, STEPPER-4 empty, bed thermistor on TH1, XY endstops and the nozzle probe on their headers. No chain work started.

Source: LDO Rev D photo S6 endstops wired · LDO wiring guide § Connecting the gantry cables · leviathan-printer-rev-d-sbv2.cfg

docs.title: Step 10.47 — Electronics-bay fan pair → FAN2
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 5 — Leviathan connections47 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.47 — Electronics-bay fan pair → FAN2
docs.text:
Step 47 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do: Bolt the splicer PCB to its printed spacer and mount the sandwich to a frame extrusion in the bay. Plug both 6020 fans into it and run the PCB FAN cable to the Leviathan port FAN2, pin PF7.

Parts:

  • 6020 fans ×2, 3×2 XH splicer PCB ×1, 2x3 Splitter Spacer ×1, M3×8 SHCS ×2, M3 hammerhead T-nut ×2, PCB FAN cable ×1

Check

The spacer is fitted, same short-circuit rule as the LED junction.

What you're looking at

The two 6020 fans are 60 × 20 mm blowers that move air through the electronics bay. The 3×2 splicer PCB joins them into one lead so a single Leviathan fan port drives both; its printed spacer keeps the bare board off the extrusion.

Tip

if the fans are not mounted yet, coil their leads and zip-tie them clear of the gantry; they go on with the skirts in Ch 11.

Item Cable label Controller position PCB fan PCB FAN FAN2 / PF7 LED strip LED STRIP LED-Strip / PE6 Filter fan FILTER FAN FAN3 / PF9

Source: LDO Rev D photo S7 fan/LED mapping · LDO wiring guide § Connecting the fans and the LED strip

docs.title: Step 10.48 — Filter fan → FAN3
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 5 — Leviathan connections48 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.48 — Filter fan → FAN3
docs.text:
Step 48 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do: Plug the board end into FAN3, pin PF9. Route the free end up through the deck opening toward the Nevermore position at the rear of the chamber and leave 150 mm of slack coiled there.

Parts:

  • FILTER FAN cable ×1

Check

The cable is at the board and the free end is parked where Ch 11 will need it.

What you're looking at

FAN3 is the port reserved for the Nevermore: the recirculating activated-carbon filter that scrubs ASA fumes inside the chamber. The filter itself is built in Ch 11, so only its cable is placed and parked now.

Source: LDO Rev D photo S7 fans wired · LDO wiring guide § Connecting the fans and the LED strip

docs.title: Step 10.49 — LED strip → LED-Strip
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 5 — Leviathan connections49 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.49 — LED strip → LED-Strip
docs.text:
Step 49 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do: Plug the lead from the ceiling junction PCB into the Leviathan port silkscreened LED-Strip, pin PE6.

Parts:

  • LED STRIP cable ×1 (2-pin JST-XH)

Check

LED-Strip, not Neopixel. LED-Strip is a dimmable 350 mA constant-current output; Neopixel is data. The Stealthburner LEDs are addressable and hang off the toolboard, not this port.

What you're looking at

LED-Strip is a dimmable constant-current output that powers plain LEDs directly, up to 350 mA. The Neopixel header next to it instead sends a data signal to addressable LEDs; that is what the Stealthburner logo uses, and it runs from the toolboard, not from here.

Source: LDO Rev D photo S7 fan/LED mapping · LDO wiring guide § Connecting the fans and the LED strip · LDO Leviathan V1.3 guide (manual p.5)

docs.title: Step 10.5 — Verify the pre-wired inlet before you trust it
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 1 — Mains: inlet → switch → PSU → SSR → bed heater5 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.5 — Verify the pre-wired inlet before you trust it
docs.text:
Step 5 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do: Compare your pre-wired inlet against LDO's diagram: the fuse sits in series with Live; Live and Neutral pass through the rocker; the Earth spade is neither switched nor fused. Three wires leave: brown L, blue N, green/yellow PE.

Parts:

  • AC inlet assembly ×1

Check

Meter on continuity, nothing plugged in. Every row of the table matches.

What you're looking at

LDO's internal map of the inlet module: which spade tab feeds which, the fuse in series with Live, the rocker breaking both Live and Neutral. The green/yellow wire is protective earth, the conductor that bonds the metalwork so the machine stays safe to touch.

C14 pin → wire rocker expect E → green/yellow either beeps L → brown ON only beeps N → blue ON only beeps L → brown, fuse pulled ON open; refit the fuse

Any deviation from that pattern means the inlet is miswired — stop and fix it before anything else. src

Source: LDO wiring guide § Preparing the inlet · LDO wiki inlet layout diagram

← PreviousStep 10.4 — Fit the AC inlet into the printed plug panel

Next →Step 10.6 — Mount the plug panel to the rear frame

docs.title: Step 10.50 — DSI ribbon: Raspberry Pi ↔ touchscreen
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 5 — Leviathan connections50 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.50 — DSI ribbon: Raspberry Pi ↔ touchscreen
docs.text:
Step 50 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do:

  1. Build the touchscreen module: Ch 11 Steps 11.5–11.6.
  2. Down to the Pi's DISPLAY: lift the latch, ribbon in contacts forward, blue tab rear, close the latch once.
  3. Service loop; tape the module to the front extrusion.

Parts:

  • FFC ribbon cable ×1, 4.3" capacitive DSI display ×1 — plus, for the module built in this step, mount.stl (B08-P3), [a]_faceplate (B02), M3×5×4 heat-set inserts ×2, M3×8 SHCS ×2 and the screen's four M2.5×6 screws (all counted in Ch 11's tables)

Check

Both latches closed evenly, ribbon square, no fold or crease, no bare contacts outside either connector. Match the photo (verify on bench).

What you're looking at

The FFC is the flat flexible ribbon carrying the display signal, DSI, between the Raspberry Pi and the 4.3" touchscreen. It has no polarity key, so the bare metal contacts on one face are the only clue to which way round it goes.

Tip

if the mount is not printed yet, seat the screen end only, tape the Pi end's bare contacts, and connect it at 11.8 instead.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: "Incorrect orientation of the FFC cables can result in damage to your Raspberry Pi and/or touchscreen." An FFC has no polarity key — the metal contacts are the only clue. At the Pi, forward is toward the front of the printer. src

Source: LDO Rev D photo VS8 mapping · LDO wiring guide § Setting up the touch screen · LDO BTT 4.3" rotate guide

← PreviousStep 10.49 — LED strip → LED-Strip

docs.title: Step 10.51 — Ethernet: Raspberry Pi ↔ rear keystone
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 5 — Leviathan connections51 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.51 — Ethernet: Raspberry Pi ↔ rear keystone
docs.text:
Step 51 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do: Plug one end into the Pi's RJ45. Run the cable through the duct to the rear-right of the bay and plug the other end into the keystone insert. Leave the insert loose; its panel is a Ch 11 part.

Parts:

  • Ethernet patch cable ×1, Keystone CAT6 insert ×1

Check

Both plugs click. The run does not cross the PSU's AC terminals or lie against the SSR.

What you're looking at

A keystone insert is the snap-in module that turns an opening in a printed panel into a proper RJ45 socket on the machine's outside. This step runs the Pi's network cable to it, so no lead dangles out of the bay.

Source: LDO Rev D photo VS8 Ethernet/USB wired · LDO wiring guide § Connecting the FFC cable, Ethernet cable, USB cable and frame PE

docs.title: Step 10.52 — USB: Raspberry Pi ↔ Leviathan
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 5 — Leviathan connections52 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.52 — USB: Raspberry Pi ↔ Leviathan
docs.text:
Step 52 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do: Plug USB-A into a Pi port and USB-C into the Leviathan's USB port. Keep it short and dress it flat; this loop is only 60 mm and a long cable will foul the DIN clips.

Parts:

  • short USB-A to USB-C cable ×1

Check

Both ends seated. The Leviathan has exactly one USB-C socket, so there is nothing to get wrong.

What you're looking at

This short cable is the whole link between the Raspberry Pi, the host that plans the motion, and the Leviathan, the MCU that executes it. The photo shows the finished set of Pi connections in LDO's bay.

Note: the Leviathan can alternatively talk over UART on its dedicated 5-pin Raspberry Pi power/UART port. Ch 12 decides. Wire USB now — the Rev D+ config addresses the mainboard as /dev/serial/by-id/..., which is USB. src · Leviathan V1.3 manual p.5

Source: LDO Rev D photo VS8 Ethernet/USB wired · LDO wiring guide § Connecting the FFC cable, Ethernet cable, USB cable and frame PE · LDO Leviathan V1.3 guide (manual p.5)

docs.title: Step 10.53 — USB: Raspberry Pi ↔ USB adapter PCB
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 5 — Leviathan connections53 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.53 — USB: Raspberry Pi ↔ USB adapter PCB
docs.text:
Step 53 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do: Plug one end into a second Pi USB port and the other into the USB adapter PCB on its DIN clip. This carries the toolboard's USB data; the 24 V it also needs arrived in step 10.26.

Parts:

  • USB cable ×1 (supplied)

Check

Both ends seated. The USB adapter PCB now has 24 V in, USB in, and the umbilical socket, still empty.

What you're looking at

The second Pi USB lead is the data half of the toolhead link; the 24 V half went on in step 10.26. The adapter PCB merges the two into the single umbilical socket.

Good stopping point · ~40 min since the last one

bay fans, filter fan and LED strip on their Leviathan ports, the touchscreen module built (Ch 11 Steps 11.5–11.6, done from 10.50) with its DSI ribbon latched at both ends and taped to the front extrusion, Ethernet and both USB links made. The umbilical is still unconnected at both ends.

Source: LDO Rev D photo VS8 mapping · LDO wiring guide § Connecting the FFC cable, Ethernet cable, USB cable and frame PE

docs.title: Step 10.54 — Identify your umbilical and its two connectors
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 6 — Toolhead umbilical and the drag chains54 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.54 — Identify your umbilical and its two connectors
docs.text:
Step 54 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do: Confirm the toolboard end is an Amass XT30(2+2)-F, the partially overmolded variant, and the bay end a Micro-Fit 3.0. Nominal bend radius 28 mm, max operating temperature 105 °C.

Parts:

  • toolhead umbilical cable ×1

Check

Both connectors are undamaged and the sheath is unnicked over its whole length.

What you're looking at

The umbilical is the thick cable between the bay and the toolhead, carrying 24 V and USB together. The Amass XT30(2+2) at the toolboard end is a four-contact power-plus-signal connector; the Micro-Fit 3.0 at the bay end is the latching rectangular one.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: never plug or unplug the Micro-Fit end with the machine powered — it can take out the Nitehawk or the Pi. src

Source: Nitehawk-SB V2 doc § Umbilical cable · Nitehawk-SB V2 doc § Cable pinout — adapter side · LDO board doc image nk36_cable_comparison.jpg · Video: Part 8 @1:35:03 (differs: no toolboard — loom to the mainboard; this kit runs a Nitehawk-SB V2 on one USB+24 V umbilical)

docs.title: Step 10.55 — Connector types on the V2 toolboard
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 6 — Toolhead umbilical and the drag chains55 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.55 — Connector types on the V2 toolboard
docs.text:
Step 55 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do: Before you touch anything on the toolhead, confirm what Ch 08 fitted:

Parts:

  • none — verification only

Check

Every toolhead connector is the small PH2.0 housing, not the larger XH2.5.

What you're looking at

The Nitehawk-SB V2 is the toolboard: the small PCB on the toolhead driving the hotend, fans, LEDs, probe and accelerometer, so only one cable crosses the moving gantry. V2 uses the finer JST-PH2.0 housings where the Rev D guide still names the coarser XH2.5.

Port Rev D wiring guide says Rev D+ / Nitehawk V2 actually is PROBE not specified JST-PH2.0 3P, 24 V only TH0 (hotend thermistor) "JST-XH2.5 two pin" JST-PH2.0 2P, 2.2 kΩ pull-up Endstop (X/Y) not specified — only "the endstop port isn't used in a standard Rev D build" JST-PH2.0 4P — unused in a standard build HE0 (hotend heater) screw terminal / E0508 ferrule unchanged

TH0 is the one real conflict: JST-XH2.5 is the only connector the Rev D guide names for the toolhead, and for the SB fans it names JST-PH2.0.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: the Rev D wiring guide has not been updated for this. Trust the V2 board doc. src — survey §4.1 ③

Source: Nitehawk-SB-V2 repo nhsbv2_pcb_pinout.jpg · Nitehawk-SB V2 doc § Connector variants — toolboard side · Nitehawk-SB V2 README § Change list from Nitehawk-SB V1 · Video: More Extras! @2:00:45 (differs: no toolboard — loom to the mainboard; this kit runs a Nitehawk-SB V2 on one USB+24 V umbilical)

docs.title: Step 10.56 — The fan-adapter header is keyed and reversed
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 6 — Toolhead umbilical and the drag chains56 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.56 — The fan-adapter header is keyed and reversed
docs.text:
Step 56 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do: The board-to-board interface between the Stealthburner fan adapter and the toolboard is a 2×5, 10-pin header on V2, with reversed gender and keying. V1 used 2×4, and every Rev D photo online shows that old arrangement.

Parts:

  • none — verification only

Check

The Stealthburner front drops on and the header seats with no gap. If it does not, it is backwards; do not press harder.

What you're looking at

The fan-adapter PCB is the small board inside the Stealthburner front carrying the part-cooling and hotend fans; it mates to the toolboard through a pin header, not a cable. The photo is the V2 header: 2×5 pins, keyed, reversed in gender from V1.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: a V1 fan adapter PCB physically cannot be reused on a V2 toolboard. src — survey §4.1 ④

Source: Nitehawk-SB-V2 repo sbv2_fan_adapter_pcb_pinout.jpg · Nitehawk-SB V2 doc § Pinout — fan adapter PCB

docs.title: Step 10.57 — The USB adapter cover is the partial cover
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 6 — Toolhead umbilical and the drag chains57 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.57 — The USB adapter cover is the partial cover
docs.text:
Step 57 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do: Confirm the cover on the USB adapter PCB is the V2 partial cover, which deliberately leaves one mounting point exposed. The printed-parts guide still points at the V1 usb_adapter_mount.stl / cw2_captive_pcb_cover.stl; that cover encloses the point you need.

Parts:

  • usb_adapter_mount_partial_cover.stl (Nitehawk-SB-V2 repo) ×1

Check

One mounting hole on the USB adapter PCB is uncovered. A fully enclosed cover is the V1 part; reprint from the V2 repo.

What you're looking at

The printed cover clips over the USB adapter PCB in the bay. The V2 version deliberately leaves one mounting hole open so a grounding wire can be bolted to it; the V1 cover encloses that hole.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: "A newly designed cover exposes one of the mounting points to connect a grounding point." src — survey §4.1 ⑤

Source: Nitehawk-SB-V2 repo usb_adapter_gnd.jpg · Nitehawk-SB V2 doc § Printed parts

docs.title: Step 10.58 — Fit the ESD grounding path
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 6 — Toolhead umbilical and the drag chains58 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.58 — Fit the ESD grounding path
docs.text:
Step 58 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do:

  1. Confirm, do not redo: both short-cable lugs under screws, the long cable's ring on the USB adapter's mounting point.
  2. Land its free end on bare frame metal: ring under a serrated washer into a T-nut, anodising scraped.

Parts:

  • the long supplied grounding cable's free end (its ring terminal is already on the USB adapter from 09.25), M3 screw + serrated washer + T-nut for the frame end (LDO does not name the fastener — verify on bench), multimeter

Check

Meter on Ω: extruder motor body → toolboard ground lug < 2–3 Ω; USB-adapter ground lug → C14 earth pin < 2–3 Ω.

What you're looking at

Detail photos: toolboard ground routing · USB-adapter ground point

ESD, electrostatic discharge, is the static filament and moving belts build up, and it kills toolboards. The two supplied cables build one continuous path from the extruder motor body, through the toolboard and umbilical, to the USB adapter and out to the earthed frame.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: use the supplied grounding cable. LDO: "using larger O ring connectors may cause inadvertent shorting of the PCB boards."

Caution

If your kit did not include the grounding cables, or your board doc predates the update: stop, post the three images above in #ldo_motors on the Voron Discord and wait for LDO's answer before improvising. The scheme was undocumented until the board doc was updated 2026-07-10. src — survey §4.1 ⑤

Good stopping point · ~25 min since the last one

the three Rev D+ toolhead deviations verified (PH2.0 housings, keyed 2×5 fan-adapter header, V2 partial cover), both ESD grounding cables confirmed and the bay cable landed on the frame, each half continuity-checked (the end-to-end reading waits for 10.67). Toolhead is closed and the umbilical is still loose.

Source: Nitehawk-SB-V2 repo grounding_scheme.jpg · Nitehawk-SB-V2 repo toolboard_ground_routing.jpg · Nitehawk-SB V2 doc § ESD hardening

docs.title: Step 10.59 — Fit the X drag chain
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 6 — Toolhead umbilical and the drag chains59 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.59 — Fit the X drag chain
docs.text:
Step 59 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do: Slide the T-nut into the top slot of the X extrusion. Mount the chain's fixed end to it with the M3×6 FHCS, and clip the moving end onto the CW2 chain anchor on the toolhead.

Parts:

  • drag chain 10×10 R18 ×1 (cut to length), M3 roll-in T-nut ×1, M3×6 FHCS (verify on bench), CW2 chain anchor tilted (LDO-supplied printed, fitted Ch 08)

Check

Push the toolhead through its full X travel by hand. The chain rolls, never drags on the extrusion, and never reaches full extension.

What you're looking at

A drag chain is an articulated conduit letting a cable follow a moving part without flexing in the same spot twice. The X chain runs along the top of the X extrusion, fixed at one end, clipped to the toolhead anchor at the other.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: the kit ships 2-hole chain ends — print *_2hole variants, never *_3hole. src
