docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 6 — Toolhead umbilical and the drag chains60 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.60 — Fit the Y drag chain
docs.text:
Step 60 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do:

  1. T-nut into the right Y extrusion, chain fixed end onto it, moving end onto the right XY joint's cable bridge, the orange arch from Step 05.38.
  2. Secure the bundle to the chain's strain relief with small zip ties.

Run the gantry front to back over full Y travel: the chain articulates freely and the loop stays clear of the bed extrusions.

The Y chain does the same job one level out: fixed to the right Y extrusion, moving with the right XY joint, so the toolhead umbilical and the endstop cable can travel front to back. Everything it serves lives on the right.

docs.text:
Step 61 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do: Bundle the A and B motor cables along the small extrusion between the two drive units, tying every 60–80 mm. Both bundles feed into the Z chain next.

Parts:

  • zip ties ×4–6

Check

No cable can reach a moving belt or pulley. Ties are snug, not crushing.

What you're looking at

The A and B motor leads run from the two rear drive units along the small extrusion between them, then join everything else in the Z chain. The ties keep the cables out of the belts and pulleys.

docs.title: Step 10.62 — Fit the Z chain guide and the Z chain
docs.text:
Step 62 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do:

  1. Bolt the guide to the rear-bottom frame extrusion with the M5 T-nut and M5×10 BHCS, at deck level as p.201 shows.
  2. Attach the chain's lower end to the guide with two M3×10 FHCS, manual p.202.

Parts:

  • Z chain guide (batch B05) ×1 with its two M3×5×4 inserts already melted in at 10.35, M5 roll-in T-nut ×1, M5×10 BHCS ×1, drag chain 10×15 R28 ×1, M3×10 FHCS ×2

Check

The guide is square to the extrusion and the chain hangs in a clean vertical loop.

What you're looking at

The Z chain is the largest of the three, 10 × 15 mm links on a 28 mm bend radius, because it carries the entire gantry harness down to the deck. The printed guide bolts to the frame and holds the chain's lower run.

docs.title: Step 10.63 — Fit the Z chain bottom anchor
docs.text:
Step 63 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do:

  1. After 10.64, dry-fit the anchor's channel over the chain and keep the extrusion where it runs straight at both Z extremes (verify on bench).
  2. M5 T-nut into that slot, chain into the channel, M5×10 BHCS through.

Parts:

  • Z chain bottom anchor (batch B05) ×1, M5 roll-in T-nut ×1, M5×10 BHCS ×1

Through full Z travel: the chain slides through the anchor without snagging, the loop stays open at the bottom, nothing stretches at the top.

What you're looking at

The bottom anchor is a printed clip with an open channel: the chain runs through it, so it is a mid-run keeper, not a chain end. p.203 shows it bolted to a horizontal extrusion, the chain passing vertically through its channel.

p.203 gives the fastener, not the extrusion. The candidates are the frame's rear-bottom extrusion and the gantry's rear beam; the dry-fit decides.

docs.title: Step 10.64 — Fit the Z chain retainer bracket and set the wire path
docs.text:
Step 64 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do:

  1. Bolt the bracket to the A drive with two M3×12 SHCS and the chain's upper end into its inserts with two M3×10 FHCS.
  2. Guide the wire bundle behind the Z belt and over the A drive, zip-tied.

Parts:

  • [a]_z_chain_retainer_bracket ×1 (batch B02, plate B02-P3; B02 prints 2 and Ch 06 Step 06.26 bags both — the second is a spare (verify on bench)) with its M3×5×4 inserts already melted in at 10.35 (p.204 carries the heat-set icon; count the bosses on your part), M3×12 SHCS ×2, M3×10 FHCS ×2, zip ties ×2

Check

Move the gantry through full Z travel. The bundle never touches the Z belt and the chain's top end never twists.

What you're looking at

The orange [a]_z_chain_retainer_bracket bolts to the A drive at the top of the loop and carries the chain's moving end up and down with the gantry. The manual page also fixes the wire path: behind the Z belt and over the drive.

Good stopping point · ~35 min since the last one

X, Y and Z chains all mounted at both ends, A/B motor cables bundled, retainer bracket on the A drive. Chains are empty and latched. Do not part-fill a chain and walk away — the next segment fills all three in one go.

docs.title: Step 10.65 — Lay the harness into the chains
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 6 — Toolhead umbilical and the drag chains65 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.65 — Lay the harness into the chains
docs.text:
Step 65 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do:

  1. Pry each latch only on its screwdriver-icon side, lay cables in, press each latch shut.
  2. Fill in order: umbilical alone in X, umbilical plus XY endstop cable in Y, both plus A and B motor bundles in Z.

Parts:

  • umbilical ×1, XY endstop cable ×1, A and B motor bundles, 2.5 mm flat screwdriver

Check

Every latch clicked shut. With the gantry mid-travel, you can pinch each cable inside a link and slide it a few millimetres.

What you're looking at

Every drag-chain link has a hinged latch down one side, marked with a small screwdriver icon on the side you may pry. With the latches open the chain is an open trough, so cables are laid into it rather than threaded through it.

Note: the umbilical's nominal bend radius is 28 mm and the X and Y chains are R18. LDO ships this combination and rates the cable for drag-chain use, but it is the cable most likely to fail first — which is exactly why the next two steps exist.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: LDO note p.194–195 — "When running wires in the cable chain, it is important to keep the wires loose. Pulling the wires tight inside the cable chain will result to excessive wire fatigue and possible pre-mature wire breaks." This is the most-repeated warning in the whole LDO documentation set. src

Source: Voron manual p.195 · Voron manual p.194 · LDO Build Notes p.194–195 · Video: More Extras! @2:18:20 (differs: no toolboard — loom to the mainboard; this kit runs a Nitehawk-SB V2 on one USB+24 V umbilical)

docs.title: Step 10.66 — Zip-tie both ends of every chain
docs.text:
Step 66 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do:

  1. Tie to the small tab on each end link, at all six chain ends.
  2. If a tab is in the way, cut it off and tie around the end link itself.

Parts:

  • zip ties ×12

Check

Six tie points. Pull the umbilical at each end: the strain lands on the zip tie, not the connector.

What you're looking at

Each end link of a chain has a small tab moulded on for a zip tie. The tie is a strain relief: pull on the umbilical and the load stops at the tie instead of arriving at the XT30 or Micro-Fit connector.

Source: Nitehawk-SB V2 doc § Working with cable chains · Nitehawk-SB-V2 repo cable_chain_ties.jpg · Video: More Extras! @2:35:55 (differs: no toolboard — loom to the mainboard; this kit runs a Nitehawk-SB V2 on one USB+24 V umbilical)

docs.title: Step 10.67 — Umbilical → USB adapter PCB
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 6 — Toolhead umbilical and the drag chains67 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.67 — Umbilical → USB adapter PCB
docs.text:
Step 67 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do: With the machine unplugged and confirmed dead, push the Micro-Fit connector into the USB adapter PCB until the latch clicks.

Parts:

  • umbilical Micro-Fit 3.0 end

Check

Latch engaged, connector square, no bend tighter than 28 mm. ESD path: extruder motor body → C14 earth pin, < 2–3 Ω.

What you're looking at

The bay end of the umbilical finally lands on the adapter PCB that has been waiting since steps 10.26 and 10.53. The Micro-Fit's latch is the click you are listening for.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: leave enough slack at the toolhead that the V2's secondary USB port stays reachable without pulling the toolhead off. That port is the whole point of the "+" in Rev D+ (USB passthrough for a future eddy-current probe); designing it out now costs you a re-route later. src — survey §4.1, sixth item

Good stopping point · ~25 min since the last one

every cable laid into its chain, all six chain ends zip-tied, every latch clicked shut, umbilical Micro-Fit seated in the USB adapter. Gantry moves through full X, Y and Z travel by hand.

docs.title: Step 10.68 — Dress the below-deck runs into the ducts
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 7 — Cable management68 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.68 — Dress the below-deck runs into the ducts
docs.text:
Step 68 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do:

  1. Push every below-deck run down into a wire duct.
  2. Keep the mains group in its own duct run, separate from the signal group. Cross them at right angles where they must cross.

Parts: none.

Check

No cable lies loose on the deck. Nothing rests on the PSU's AC terminal block or the SSR.

What you're looking at

Wire ducts are the slotted channels screwed to the deck: a cable presses in between the fingers and a lid clips over later. The bay carries two independent runs, a mains group and a signal group, meeting only where they cross at right angles.

Tip

mains group = inlet, WAGO bus, PSU AC, SSR load. Signal group = endstops, thermistor, USB, Ethernet, DSI.

Source: LDO Rev D photo VS9 finished bay · LDO wiring guide § Finish line

docs.title: Step 10.69 — Strain-relieve the deck opening
docs.text:
Step 69 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

(no image — see text)

docs.title: Step 10.7 — Populate and label the WAGO bus
docs.text:
Step 7 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do: Label the three blocks left to right N, L, PE, with the label maker.

Parts:

  • the three WAGO 221-415 blocks in their mount (populated and mounted at Step 09.13 — nothing to snap in here), label maker

Check

Three labelled 5-way blocks, all levers up, all fifteen ports empty.

What you're looking at

WAGO 221 blocks are lever-clamp connectors. The three 5-way blocks are the machine's mains bus, one each for Neutral, Live and earth. They are physically identical, so "the blue N WAGO" means the block labelled for that wire colour, never the block's own colour.

docs.title: Step 10.70 — Tag every cable at the board end
docs.text:
Step 70 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

(no image — see text)

Do: Walk every cable that reaches the Leviathan, the PSU, the SSR or the USB adapter and read its tag aloud: what it is, where its far end goes. Tag anything that has none.

Parts:

  • cable tags (supplied), for whatever is missing

Check

You could disconnect the whole board and put it back tomorrow from the tags alone.

What you're looking at

The same cable tags as step 10.40. Every cable should already carry one from the step that landed it; this is the walk that finds the ones you missed. The tags are the only documentation of a Rev D+ bay that will ever exist.

docs.title: Step 10.71 — Leave the duct covers off
docs.text:
Step 71 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

(no image — see text)

Do: Nothing. LDO's "Finish Line" tells you to cover the ducts; do not. Leave them off until Checkpoint 10 passes and Ch 13 has driven every motor, heater and fan at least once.

Parts:

  • duct covers — not fitted

Check

Every duct is open and every terminal is reachable with a meter probe.

What you're looking at

Duct covers are the snap-on lids for the channels from step 10.68. They are the last thing to fit, not the first: the bay has to stay reachable with a meter probe until Ch 13 has driven every motor, heater and fan at least once.

docs.title: Step 10.72 — Walk the bay against LDO's finished photo

docs.title: Step 10.72 — Walk the bay against LDO's finished photo
docs.text:
Step 72 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do:

  1. Compare your bay to the photo, one cable at a time, in the table's order.
  2. Any difference from the photo gets explained by a step in this chapter, or fixed.

Every difference from the photo is one you can name and point to a step for. STEPPER-4, TH0, Z-PROBE, FAN0 and FAN1 stay empty.

What you're looking at

LDO's finished Rev D bay again, the same photo step 10.1 set as the target. Yours differs in exactly one place: the USB adapter with the umbilical, the Rev D+ addition. Everything else should now match, cable for cable.

# walk this 1 inlet 2 WAGO bus 3 PSU 4 SSR LOAD and INPUT pairs 5 bed breakout 6 the three 24 V feeds 7 six steppers 8 TH1 9 three endstop headers 10 FAN2 / FAN3 / LED-Strip 11 the Pi's three links 12 the umbilical

Good stopping point · ~20 min since the last one

below-deck runs dressed into the ducts with mains and signal separated, deck opening strain-relieved, every cable tagged, duct covers still off, bay walked against LDO's photo. Do not fit the covers or any skirt.

Next →Step 10.73 — Confirm dead

docs.title: Step 10.73 — Confirm dead
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 8 — Pre-power-on meter sweep73 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.73 — Confirm dead
docs.text:
Step 73 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

(no image — see text)

Do: Cord out of the inlet and out of the room. Meter on DC V across the PSU's +V and −V.

Parts:

  • multimeter

Check

0 V, and it stays 0 V for ten seconds. The bulk caps are discharged.

What you're looking at

Everything here is measured unplugged. Nothing in this section powers anything on.

A PSU holds charge in its bulk capacitors after the cord comes out. Reading 0 V across its DC output, and watching it stay there for ten seconds, is what proves the machine is safe to probe.

Source: LDO wiring guide § Checkpoint 1

← PreviousStep 10.72 — Walk the bay against LDO's finished photo

Next →Step 10.74 — 24 V rails

docs.title: Step 10.74 — 24 V rails
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 8 — Pre-power-on meter sweep74 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.74 — 24 V rails
docs.text:
Step 74 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

(no image — see text)

Do: Measure the rail once, then each 24 V input against its own ground to prove it is landed, then each side of the rail against the C14 earth pin.

Parts:

  • multimeter on Ω

Check

Every row.

What you're looking at

The authoritative 24 V table, now that the umbilical and toolboard are on the rail too. A healthy rail reads a resistance that rises; a shorted one behaves like a piece of wire. The last two rows check the rail against earth.

Node Expected PSU +V → −V finite, rising as caps charge. Never 0 Ω Leviathan Vin 24V + → − the same reading — same node Leviathan Vin 24-48V + → − the same reading — same node USB adapter 24 V in + → − the same reading — same node, now with the umbilical and toolboard on it PSU +V (or any Vin +) → PE OL PSU −V / any GND → PE a few Ω — expected. This is the ESD bond from 10.58: USB-adapter GND to the frame, frame to PE. It reads OL only if that cable is missing or its washer sits on anodising

A continuous beep on a + → − row is a reversed ferrule or a stray strand — find it now. A beep on −V → PE is not a fault; a +V → PE beep is.

Source: LDO wiring guide § Connecting 24V

← PreviousStep 10.73 — Confirm dead

Next →Step 10.75 — 5 V rail

docs.title: Step 10.75 — 5 V rail
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 8 — Pre-power-on meter sweep75 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.75 — 5 V rail
docs.text:
Step 75 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

(no image — see text)

Do: Measure at the Pi's 40-pin GPIO header, at the end nearest the microSD slot: pin 2 or 4, 5 V, to pin 6, GND, the outer row's first three pins.

Parts:

  • multimeter on Ω

Check

Finite, and not 0 Ω. Exactly two jumpers on the board, Fan2 and Fan3, both on the 24 V pins.

What you're looking at

There is no 5 V power supply in this kit: the Leviathan makes 5 V itself and sends it to the Pi through the 5-pin power/UART port and the HAT adapter. This check confirms that rail is not shorted.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: LDO notes p.152, p.172 and p.190 are all SKIP — the manual's 5 V PSU does not exist in this kit and the Pi is never powered over its own USB-C. src

Source: LDO Build Notes p.152, p.172, p.190 · LDO Leviathan V1.3 guide (manual p.5)

Next →Step 10.76 — Thermistors at room temperature

docs.title: Step 10.76 — Thermistors at room temperature
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 8 — Pre-power-on meter sweep76 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.76 — Thermistors at room temperature
docs.text:
Step 76 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

(no image — see text)

Do:

  1. Leave the bed thermistor plugged in; write its 10.44 reading in the table.
  2. Measure the hotend thermistor at the toolboard's TH0 if the toolhead is still open, and the chamber thermistor at CT if your batch has one.

Parts:

  • multimeter on Ω, room thermometer

Check

Read your room temperature, then compare against Klipper's own curve for that part:

What you're looking at

A thermistor is a resistor whose value falls as it gets hotter; both of this machine's are the same ATC Semitec part, nominally 100 kΩ at 25 °C. Measuring them cold catches a crushed or broken lead before any heater runs.

Derived from the [thermistor ATC Semitec 104NT-4-R025H42G] definition in Klipper's temperature_sensors.cfg (100 kΩ at 25 °C), which is the curve the printer will actually use.

Room temp Expected resistance 15 °C ≈ 162 kΩ 18 °C ≈ 140 kΩ 20 °C ≈ 127 kΩ 22 °C ≈ 115 kΩ 25 °C ≈ 100 kΩ 28 °C ≈ 87 kΩ 30 °C ≈ 79 kΩ

Within ±15 % of the row for your room is fine. 0 Ω means a crushed lead; OL means a broken one or an unseated crimp.

Source: Klipper temperature_sensors.cfg · LDO wiring guide § Connecting build plate

← PreviousStep 10.75 — 5 V rail

Next →Step 10.77 — Protective-earth bonding

docs.title: Step 10.77 — Protective-earth bonding
docs.text: Ch 10 › Section 8 — Pre-power-on meter sweep77 / 79

docs.title: Step 10.77 — Protective-earth bonding
docs.text:
Step 77 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

(no image — see text)

Do: With one probe on the C14 earth pin, touch the other to each row below. On the frame and the plate, probe a screw head, a T-nut or a bare cut end, never an anodised face.

Parts:

  • multimeter on Ω

Check

Every metal thing you can touch is bonded; nothing that carries current is, except the 24 V negative, bonded on purpose.

What you're looking at

The last earth check. Every piece of metal a hand can reach must have a low-resistance path back to the inlet's earth pin, and nothing that carries current may have any path at all.

Point Expected PE WAGO, any port < 1 Ω PSU 3 FG (⏚) terminal < 1 Ω Frame, at a far corner — screw head or T-nut < 2–3 Ω Build plate — the M4×6 PE screw head a few Ω or less Extruder motor body (via the ESD ground and the umbilical, 10.67) a few Ω or less Bed heater L or N OL +24 V — PSU +V or any Vin + OL −V / GND — PSU −V or any Vin − a few Ω — expected, the ESD bond from 10.58

A failed row here is a missing PE lead, anodising under a washer, or a probe on anodising. Fix it before Ch 11 closes the bay.

Step 78 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

(no image — see text)

What you're looking at

The same four terminals as step 10.10, now with all four cables attached, plus one measurement the earlier check could not make: mains side to control side must be open, the relay's isolation barrier being all that stands between mains and mainboard.

Not 0 Ω SSR 1 or 2 → SSR 3 or 4 OL — mains and DC control are galvanically isolated SSR 1 → SSR 2 wire colours bed cable on 1, brown WAGO cable on 2 SSR 3 wire colour red

If mains-to-control is not open, the SSR's isolation barrier is gone. Replace it; do not power the machine.

Step 79 of 79 · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Checkpoint · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Do not start Ch 11 until every line is ticked.

  • PSU voltage selector matches your mains — verified twice (10.2, 10.22)
  • LDO's Checkpoint #1 passed in full: every node of each colour traced end to end — C14 pin to PSU screw, SSR, bed and frame — L/N/PE mutually isolated at the WAGOs and at the PSU screws, switch switches, SSR open, then one hand-on-the-switch power-on and off again (10.17–10.23)
  • Bed heater reads tens of ohms L→N and OL to the plate (10.13)
  • SSR: bed on LOAD 1, mains L on LOAD 2, red on INPUT 3, black on INPUT 4; load and control sides isolated (10.14, 10.27, 10.78)
  • Protective earth reaches the frame, the build plate and the extruder motor body from the C14 earth pin — probed on bare metal, never anodising (10.16, 10.58, 10.67, 10.77)
  • No 24 V node and no 5 V node reads 0 Ω; +24 V → PE reads OL and −V → PE reads a few Ω through the ESD bond; exactly two jumpers on the Leviathan, Fan2 and Fan3, both at 24 V (10.28, 10.74, 10.75)
  • Both thermistors read within ±15 % of the room-temperature table (10.44, 10.76)
  • Six steppers on their mapped ports, tagged; STEPPER-4 and Z-PROBE empty (10.40–10.43, 10.46)
  • All three Rev D+ toolhead deviations verified: PH2.0 connectors, keyed 2×5 (10-pin) fan header seated with no gap, V2 partial cover with the grounding cable fitted (10.55–10.58)
  • Every cable in every chain can be slid by hand; all six chain ends zip-tied; gantry moves through full X, Y and Z travel with no snag (10.65, 10.66)
  • Duct covers off, skirts off, bottom panel off; touchscreen module built (Ch 11 Steps 11.5–11.6) with its DSI ribbon latched at both ends, once, and taped to the front extrusion for Ch 11 Step 11.7 (10.50)

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Skipping the meter because "it looks right." Every mains fault in this chapter is invisible and silent until the moment it is not. Checkpoint #1 takes twenty-five minutes.
  • SSR INPUT 3 and 4 swapped. The bed never heats. (LOAD 1 and 2 swapped changes nothing electrically — keep LDO's convention anyway so the photos stay comparable.) The dangerous SSR fault is a shorted relay, which 10.21 and 10.78 test for; LDO calls this connection critical and it is the only one they do.
  • Reading the anodised frame with the meter. The oxide layer is an insulator; a perfectly bonded frame reads OL on its flat faces. Probe a screw head, a T-nut or a bare cut end (10.16, 10.77). Likewise, −V to PE reading a few ohms is the ESD bond doing its job, not a short (10.74).
  • Probe plugged into the Leviathan's Z-PROBE header. On a Nitehawk build the probe lives on the toolboard's PROBE port. The stock config's comment says otherwise and the comment is wrong.
  • Chamber thermistor on a Leviathan TH port. The Rev D+ config reads it as nhk:PB2. Put it on the toolboard's CT port.
  • Cables pulled tight in the chains. They will survive assembly and fail in three months, mid-print, usually the umbilical at a connector. Loose, and zip-tied at both ends of every chain.
  • Forcing a PH2.0 housing into the wrong V2 header, or pressing the fan-adapter 2×5 (10-pin) header in backwards. Both are physically possible and both destroy something. The key is the check — if it needs force, it is wrong.
  • LED routing left until the panels are on. The slot covers and the Z-belt cover choice both have to happen before Ch 11 closes the top (survey §5.2 W5).

docs.title: Before you start Chapter 10
docs.text:
Before you start · Chapter 10 — Wiring and Checkpoint #1

Builds every harness — mains, 24 V, motion, sensors, lighting, toolhead umbilical — and ends at the gate that must pass before the machine is ever plugged in.

What you're building in this chapter. Four systems, in this order. The mains side — the C14 inlet with its integrated switch and fuse, a three-block WAGO bus for Live, Neutral and earth, the 24 V PSU, and the solid-state relay that lets firmware switch a mains bed heater — goes in first and is then proved with a meter before anything is plugged in. The 24 V side fans out from the PSU to the Leviathan mainboard, to its separate high-voltage stepper supply, and to the USB adapter PCB that feeds the toolhead. The signal side is everything the machine senses and lights with: six motor cables on their mapped driver sockets, the XY endstop pod on the gantry, the mechanical nozzle probe that sets Z=0, the bed thermistor, two COB light strips and their junction PCB, the bay and filter fans, and the Pi's screen, network and USB links. Finally the three drag chains — X, Y and Z — are mounted and filled, so every cable can follow the moving gantry for years without fatiguing. The chapter ends unplugged, open and metered, with LDO's Checkpoint #1 behind you.

Time: 5.0–7.0 h hands-on, first build (survey §5.1, §7.2).

Sessions: 14 × ~30 min (Pause segments below; every minute figure in this chapter is a first-build estimate derived from the Time range and the step count).

Prerequisites:

  • Ch 03 — Build plate. Plate bolted down; heater, thermistor and PE leads hanging loose below deck.
  • Ch 06 — Z axis. Gantry in, Z belts on. The gantry must move by hand over its full Z travel — that is what sets the chain slack.
  • Ch 07 — A/B belts. Probe wires already dressed along the X extrusion (manual p.143).
  • Ch 08 — Toolhead. Stealthburner + CW2 + Nitehawk-SB V2 assembled, all toolhead-side connectors seated, USB-adapter PCB stack built.
  • Ch 09 — Electronics bay. DIN rails, wire ducts, Leviathan on its brackets, Raspberry Pi mounted on its standoffs with the HAT power adapter, nozzle-probe PCB assembled and mounted, bed WAGO mount fitted, SSR on its DIN bracket, USB-adapter PCB on its DIN clip — and the inlet panel with its IEC module fitted and mounted on the rear extrusion (Steps 09.10–09.12), plus the mains WAGO block built and mounted (Step 09.13). Nothing in this chapter builds those; 10.4–10.7 only confirm and label them.
  • Print batches: B05 (Z joints + Z chain), B07 (electronics bay + lighting — the eight COB mounts and the 3×5 WAGO mount), which also carries power_inlet_IECGS_1mm on plate B07-P1 (moved out of B08 — index correction #11). One B08 part is needed early: mount.stl (plate B08-P3) plus the B02 [a]_faceplate, at Step 10.50 — the touchscreen module has to exist before its ribbon is latched, so Ch 11 Steps 11.5–11.6 are done from there. Both are pre-kit prints. Nothing else from B08 is needed before Ch 11.

Tools

  • Multimeter — mandatory. Continuity/beeper, a resistance range to at least 2 MΩ (a 20 MΩ range is preferred — it turns an OL pass into a number you can write down), and a DC volts range. No multimeter, no power-on.
  • 2.5 mm flat-blade screwdriver (supplied) — WAGO levers, plug-type terminals, drag-chain latches
  • PH2 Phillips — PSU terminal block and SSR terminals
  • Hex 2 / 2.5 / 3 / 4 mm
  • Flush cutters, small long-nose pliers, tweezers (endstop repin)
  • Soldering iron + brass M3 insert tip — all twenty inserts in one pass at step 10.35 (COB mounts ×16, Z chain guide ×2, Z chain retainer bracket ×2), so the iron is out once and never during an electrical segment
  • Label maker, or the cable tags supplied in the kit

Consumables: zip ties (of the 100 supplied, this chapter eats 30–40), VE0508 ferrules ×5 (spares), IPA and a lint-free cloth for the extrusion slots before the covers go on.

Printed parts

Parts arrive in the bins named below (see the bin map in print/README.md#bins); check the bin label's list before you start.

Looks like STL Bin Qty Colour power_inlet_IECGS_1mm.stl (Voron-2 STLs/Skirts/) 09-bay 1 Black — heat-set, fitted with its IEC module and mounted in Ch 09 (09.10–09.12); nothing to build here cob_light_strip_mount_100mm.stl (LDOVoron2 STLs/COB Light Strip/) 10-lights 6 Black cob_light_strip_mount_50mm.stl (LDOVoron2 STLs/COB Light Strip/) 10-lights 2 Black wago_221-415_mount_3by5.stl (Voron-2 STLs/Electronics_Bay/) 09-bay 1 Black — fitted in Ch 09, populated here z_chain_guide / z_chain_bottom_anchor (batch B05) 10-chains 1 / 1 Black [a]_z_chain_retainer_bracket_x2 (batch B02, plate B02-P3) 10-chains 2 printed, 1 fitted, 1 spare (verify on bench) Orange 2x3 Splitter Spacer — 2 LDO-supplied printed — do not print usb_adapter_mount_partial_cover.stl (Nitehawk-SB-V2 repo) 09-bay 1 Black — fitted in Ch 08/09, used here

Hardware (chapter totals)

Fastener / part Qty Note AC inlet, integrated switch + fuse 1 pre-wired; verify, don't rewire Meanwell LRS-200-24 PSU 1 24 V 8.8 A; 115/230 V selector on the side Omron SSR G3NB-210B-1 + DIN bracket 1 24–220 VAC 10 A WAGO 221-415 (5-way) 3 N / L / PE bus WAGO 221-412 (2-way) 2 bed L and bed N breakout, on the bed WAGO mount 3×2 XH splicer PCB 2 one for the 6020 fan pair, one as the LED junction 2×2 XH splicer PCB 1 bed thermistor breakout (fitted Ch 09) Drag chain 10×10 R18 2 X chain and Y chain Drag chain 10×15 R28 1 Z chain M3×5×4 brass heat-set insert 20 16 for the COB mounts, 2 for the Z chain guide, 2 for the Z chain retainer bracket (p.204 carries the heat-set icon but no count — count the bosses on your part, verify on bench) M3×6 FHCS 16 COB mount halves M3×8 SHCS 20 16 COB mounts to extrusion, 2 per splicer PCB ×2 M3 hammerhead T-nut, 2020 20 pairs with the M3×8 SHCS above M3×6 FHCS (chain ends, X and Y) (verify on bench) manual p.197, p.199 — 2-hole chain ends M3 roll-in T-nut, 2020 2 X and Y chain ends M3×10 FHCS 4 Z chain top and bottom ends (p.202) M3×12 SHCS 2 Z chain retainer bracket to the A drive (p.204) M5×10 BHCS + M5 roll-in T-nut 2 + 2 Z chain guide (p.201), Z chain bottom anchor (p.203) M5×10 BHCS + M5 roll-in T-nut (frame PE) 1 + 1 plus the two M5 locking washers below M5 locking washer 2 frame PE stack Extrusion slot cover, 6 mm up to 9 closes the slots the LED leads run in VE0508 ferrule 5 spares Zip ties 3×150 mm ~35 from the 100 supplied

Read first

  • Mains is the one step in this build that can kill you. Nothing gets plugged in until Checkpoint #1 passes with a meter. If your local regulations forbid you from wiring the mains side, stop at step 10.8 — the first mains run — and get Section 1 done by someone certified. src
  • Set the PSU's 115/230 V selector before anything else and check it again at Checkpoint #1. Getting it wrong destroys the PSU on the first switch-on. src
  • Keep every wire loose inside every drag chain. Taut wires fatigue and break — the single most-repeated LDO warning, and the umbilical is the cable it kills. src
  • Close nothing until Checkpoint #1 passes. No duct covers, no skirts, no bottom panel. Re-opening a closed bay costs an hour and tempts you to skip the meter (survey §5.2 W8).
  • Never plug or unplug a stepper, or the Micro-Fit umbilical connector, with power on. Back-EMF kills drivers; hot-plugging the umbilical can take out the Nitehawk or the Pi. src
  • Your Rev D+ toolboard is a Nitehawk-SB V2. The Klipper config and the USB serial-ID pattern both differ from the Rev D wiring guide — that is Ch 12's problem, but do not let anyone talk you into loading leviathan-printer-rev-d.cfg on this board (survey §4.1 ①②).

Sources for this chapter:

  • Voron 2.4r2 Assembly Manual, pinned commit de7e89d — p.143, p.156, p.181, p.194–195, p.197–204
  • LDO wiring guide, Rev D — every connector step below cites its own section anchor
  • LDO Build Notes (build FAQ) — the per-page SKIP notes for p.152, p.162–163, p.169, p.172, p.190, p.194–198
  • LDO Rev D printed-parts guide and Rev D 350 BOM
  • LDO Leviathan V1.3 guide — board silkscreen, jumper block, port map
  • Nitehawk-SB V2 board doc and the Nitehawk-SB-V2 repo at commit 42ae497 (pinout, grounding and cable-chain images)
  • LDO XY endstop reconnecting guide and BTT 4.3" screen rotate guide
  • leviathan-printer-rev-d-sbv2.cfg at commit 667521d — the pin assignments this chapter wires to
  • Klipper temperature_sensors.cfg at commit f0892d8 — the thermistor curve in step 10.76
  • Step images mirrored into assets/remote/10-wiring/ — LDOVoron2 at 8270e8c, the Nitehawk-SB-V2 images at 42ae497, and six diagrams from the LDO wiki. All are LDO Motors' work, mirrored with attribution for this non-commercial manual; owner, source URL, date and sha256 for each are in that folder's SOURCES.txt

Video coverage (Steve Builds, pre-release LDO kit — differs from Rev D+): Part 4 @1:43:50 (+13m), Part 6 @0:24:08 (+2m), Part 6 @0:25:44 (+22m), Part 6 @1:04:10 (+27m), Part 7 @0:08:36 (+16m), Part 7 @1:29:40 (+12m), Part 8 @0:53:06 (+37m), Part 8 @1:25:00 (+10m), Part 8 @1:34:41 (+3m), Part 8 @1:37:22 (+7m), Part 8 @1:43:45 (+11m), Part 9 @0:04:57 (+15m), Part 9 @0:45:19 (+3m), Part 9 @0:47:56 (+8m), More Extras! @0:43:01 (+4m), More Extras! @1:59:20 (+23m), More Extras! @2:18:10 (+53m)

Step 1 of 66 · Chapter 11 — Skirts, panels, Clicky-Clack door, filtration

Do:

  1. Lay every segment face-down on the flat reference; no corner should rock.
  2. Lay the ring out in the order above, inlet corner rear-left seen from the front, as Ch 09 bolted it.

Parts:

  • front run, three across: front_skirt_a_350, BTT mount, front_skirt_b_350
  • rear run, three across: power_inlet_IECGS_1mm in one corner, rear_center_skirt_350 in the middle because it has no belt-guard cut-out, keystone_panel in the other corner
  • each side, three down: side_skirt_a_350, side_fan_support, side_skirt_b_350
  • twelve segments in all, sharing one 67 × 20 mm cross-section, so a mis-ordered ring still bolts together
  • power_inlet_IECGS_1mm is already bolted to the frame and wired in Ch 09/10 and stays there

Check

Twelve segments, none rocking, the ring closing with front and rear runs equal and the two sides equal.

What you're looking at

Everything in Part A is done with the machine open and, in the build order, after Ch 12 Part 2: the boards were powered for the first time at Step 12.11 with the bay open, so "first power-up" here means Ch 13 — the first time the machine moves and heats (13.3). Work through it, then stop at the marker before 11.52. Three runs are off-machine: the touchscreen module (11.5–11.6) is built from Ch 10 Step 10.50, before its ribbon is latched; the Nevermore (11.26–11.41, after B09) and the Clicky-Clack sub-assembly (11.44–11.50, after B10) can be done any time after their batch has printed — for instance while Ch 12 flashes images.

The skirt is the band of printed segments around the base of the machine. It closes the electronics bay and carries the belt guards, fan grills, keystone panel, AC inlet and touchscreen. Twelve segments make the ring on a 350.

Tip

the built-in supports in the skirt front covers snap out; don't cut them. p.222–224 are drawn from the rear, so they mirror this layout. src

Do: Snap the CAT6 keystone into whichever of the two slots suits your cable run to the Pi's Ethernet port, and the orange blank into the other. Both clip in from the inside face, no fasteners.

Parts:

  • keystone_panel ×1, Keystone CAT6 insert ×1 (supplied), [a]_keystone_blank_insert ×1 (orange; the second is a spare)

Check

Both slots filled, both inserts flush with the outside face, neither rattling. The RJ45 opening faces out.

What you're looking at

The keystone panel is the rear skirt segment with two rectangular cut-outs for snap-in network modules. The CAT6 keystone is the RJ45 socket that Ch 10's Ethernet run plugs into from the inside; the orange blank fills the second slot.

Tip

if you want more of the LDO logo on the machine, ldo_bestagon_insert snaps into any of the skirt hexagons — print extras. src

Source: Voron manual p.217 · LDOVoron2 STLs/

docs.title: Step 11.11 — Build the electronics-bay fan modules
docs.text: Ch 11 › Part A — before first power-up11 / 66

docs.title: Step 11.11 — Build the electronics-bay fan modules
docs.text:
Step 11 of 66 · Chapter 11 — Skirts, panels, Clicky-Clack door, filtration

Do:

  1. Build both right-hand openings to the stack above, four M3×8 SHCS from outside into the inserts.
  2. Both airflow arrows into the bay. Leads uncut.
  3. Blank the left support with the remaining grills, no retainer (verify on bench).

Parts:

  • 60×60×20 mm 24 V fan ×2
  • side_fan_support ×2
  • [a]_fan_grill_a ×2 and [a]_fan_grill_b ×2, orange
  • [a]_fan_grill_retainer ×2, from 11.3
  • M3×8 SHCS ×4 per fan, 8 total
  • stack at each populated opening, from outside in: orange grill, support wall, then the retainer directly behind the wall with the fan captured in its frame and its leads toward the bay. The screws never pass through the fan, so the retainer's inserts must sit within ~8 mm of the grill face for an M3×8 to reach them (verify on bench)

Check

Two fans in the right-hand support, spinning freely, screws snug without crushing the fan bodies, arrows pointing into the bay. Left support: grills only.

What you're looking at

Each side_fan_support has two fan openings. This kit has two fans, two retainers and four grills, so both fans go in the right-hand support, the PSU side seen from the front, and the left support gets grills only. Grills a and b are mirrored.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: the kit contains two 60×20 fans, two retainers, four grills and one 3×2 splicer PCB. The manual draws fans in both supports; count the fans you have. LDO's Rev D bay photos S1, S4, S6 put both beside the PSU. No airflow direction is given; both extracting also works if matched. src · src

Tip

[a]_fan_grill_open_optional_x2 is an alternate grill with more open area and less filtering, if the bay runs warm. The two blank grills need their own fixing (verify on bench). src

Source: Voron manual p.225 · Voron manual p.228 · LDO Rev D 350 BOM · Voron-2 STLs/Skirts/

docs.title: Step 11.12 — Pre-load the skirt T-nuts
docs.text: Ch 11 › Part A — before first power-up12 / 66

docs.title: Step 11.12 — Pre-load the skirt T-nuts
docs.text:
Step 12 of 66 · Chapter 11 — Skirts, panels, Clicky-Clack door, filtration

Do:

  1. Roll every T-nut the ring needs into the frame extrusions before any segment goes up, each left loose at roughly its position.
  2. An M3 at each skirt-to-frame screw position, an M5 between the two M3 per side.

Parts:

  • M3 roll-in T-nut ×12 — front extrusion ×4 (p.218), rear ×4 (p.222), each side ×2 (p.226, p.229)
  • M5 roll-in T-nut ×2 — one per side, under the fan support, where p.226/p.229 show the larger M5×10 BHCS. The TFT mount's three M3 T-nuts went in at 11.7

Check

Every T-nut sits flat in its slot and slides with light finger pressure. None jammed, none dropped inside a closed extrusion end.

What you're looking at

A roll-in T-nut drops into an extrusion slot and rotates a quarter turn to lock, so it can be added after a frame is built. Once a skirt segment covers the slot, no nut can get in.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: "Due to the tight tolerances of the extrusions and roll-in t-nuts it is advisable to either test fit before assembly to identify the sides of the extrusions that fits the best or to pre-load the t-nuts into the extrusions." src

Good stopping point · ~15 min since the last one

three belt guards on their segments (the fourth waits for the plug panel at 11.14), keystone panel populated, the right-hand fan support built with both fans and the left one blanked, and every skirt T-nut pre-loaded in the right slot. The ring is still off the machine.

Source: Voron manual p.218 · Voron manual p.226 · Voron manual p.229 · LDO Build Notes p.218 · Video: Part 5 @4:24:04

docs.title: Step 11.13 — Mount the front skirt segments
docs.text: Ch 11 › Part A — before first power-up13 / 66

docs.title: Step 11.13 — Mount the front skirt segments
docs.text:
Step 13 of 66 · Chapter 11 — Skirts, panels, Clicky-Clack door, filtration

Do:

  1. Hang each front skirt on its T-nuts, belt-guard aperture over the front idler, and drive the M3×8 SHCS up from underneath.
  2. Snug them, back off a quarter turn, push both hard against the TFT module, then tighten.

Parts:

  • front_skirt_a_350 ×1, front_skirt_b_350 ×1, M3×8 SHCS (verify on bench)

Check

Front run reads as one continuous band: skirt–module–skirt with equal, tight joints and a flush top rail. No daylight at the front idler apertures.

What you're looking at

The front run is the most-looked-at part of a finished Voron: skirt, touchscreen module, skirt, reading as one continuous band. Snugging first and only then closing the joints is what makes the two seams disappear.

Source: Voron manual p.219

docs.title: Step 11.14 — Mount the rear skirt run
docs.text: Ch 11 › Part A — before first power-up14 / 66

docs.title: Step 11.14 — Mount the rear skirt run
docs.text:
Step 14 of 66 · Chapter 11 — Skirts, panels, Clicky-Clack door, filtration

Do:

  1. Belt guard onto the mounted plug panel, one M3×8 SHCS into its insert from outside.
  2. keystone_panel into the far rear corner, then rear_center_skirt_350 into the gap.
  3. Feed the Ethernet through the keystone, snug, push the joints closed, tighten.

Parts:

  • the fourth belt guard from 11.9 + M3×8 SHCS ×1 (p.222), keystone_panel ×1 (from 11.10, guard already on), rear_center_skirt_350 ×1, the already-fitted power_inlet_IECGS_1mm segment, M3×8 SHCS ×4 into the four M3 T-nuts pre-loaded at 11.12

Check

Rear run continuous and flush, all four guards on, the AC switch moving freely, RJ45 keystone square, nothing pinching the Ethernet or AC leads.

What you're looking at

The rear run has three segments. One of them, the power_inlet_IECGS_1mm panel carrying the AC inlet, has been on the machine since Ch 09 and never moves. p.222 is not a segment: it shows the last belt guard going onto that panel.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: the inlet segment is power_inlet_IECGS_1mm — the 1.0 mm AC inlet with the integrated switch. The 1.2 mm variants and power_inlet_filtered are wrong for this kit. p.222–224 are drawn from the rear, plug panel on the image-left, which is the printer's right; follow the panel on your frame, not the picture's side. src

Source: Voron manual p.222–224 · LDO Build Notes p.222–224 · Video: Part 6 @1:39:57

docs.title: Step 11.15 — Mount the first side skirt run
docs.text: Ch 11 › Part A — before first power-up15 / 66

docs.title: Step 11.15 — Mount the first side skirt run
docs.text:
Step 15 of 66 · Chapter 11 — Skirts, panels, Clicky-Clack door, filtration

Do:

  1. On the right-hand side seen from the front, fit side_skirt_a at the front and side_skirt_b at the rear, leaving the fan-support gap.
  2. Drive the M3×8 SHCS into the pre-loaded T-nuts, snug not tight. M5 T-nut stays empty for 11.16.

Parts:

  • side_skirt_a_350 ×1, side_skirt_b_350 ×1, M3×8 SHCS ×2 — the right-hand fan support from 11.11 (two fans) waits for 11.16

Check

Both segments parallel to the extrusion, top rails level with the front and rear runs, the gap matching the fan module's width.

What you're looking at

Each side run is three segments: side_skirt_a at the front, the fan support in the middle, side_skirt_b at the rear. The two skirts go on first and stay loose, because the fan support drops into the gap they leave.

Source: Voron manual p.226 · Voron manual p.227

docs.title: Step 11.16 — Drop in the fan module and close the side run
docs.text: Ch 11 › Part A — before first power-up16 / 66

docs.title: Step 11.16 — Drop in the fan module and close the side run
docs.text:
Step 16 of 66 · Chapter 11 — Skirts, panels, Clicky-Clack door, filtration

Do:

  1. Slide the support into the gap from outside, grills out, leads into the bay.
  2. Push the skirts against it to close both joints.
  3. Drive the M5×10 BHCS up into the M5 T-nut, then tighten this run.

Parts:

  • the right-hand fan support from 11.11, M5×10 BHCS ×1

Check

The whole side one band with flush joints, both fans spinning freely, no lead trapped between the support and the extrusion.

What you're looking at

The right-hand fan support from 11.11, both fans in it, is the middle segment of the side run. It is trapped rather than screwed at its ends, so pushing the two skirts against it closes both joints.

Source: Voron manual p.227 · Voron manual p.230

docs.title: Step 11.17 — Mount the second side skirt run
docs.text: Ch 11 › Part A — before first power-up17 / 66

docs.title: Step 11.17 — Mount the second side skirt run
docs.text:
Step 17 of 66 · Chapter 11 — Skirts, panels, Clicky-Clack door, filtration

Do: Repeat 11.15 and 11.16 on the left-hand side with the blanked support. p.229 shows the T-nuts, p.230 the fasteners; both draw fans in this support and yours has none.

Parts:

  • side_skirt_a_350 ×1, side_skirt_b_350 ×1, the left-hand side_fan_support with its two blank grills, M3×8 SHCS ×2, M5×10 BHCS ×1

Check

The ring closed all the way round, every joint tight, every top rail flush. Two fans right, two blank grills left.

What you're looking at

The same three-segment run on the left-hand side. Its middle segment is the second side_fan_support, no fans in it, just the two blank grills from 11.11. When it closes, the skirt ring is continuous all the way round.

Good stopping point · ~20 min since the last one

front, rear and both side skirt runs mounted, both bay fans trapped in the right-hand run, the left run blanked. The ring is complete all the way round; no run is half-fastened.

Source: Voron manual p.229 · Voron manual p.230

docs.title: Step 11.18 — Verify the bay-fan wiring
docs.text: Ch 11 › Part A — before first power-up18 / 66

docs.title: Step 11.18 — Verify the bay-fan wiring
docs.text:
Step 18 of 66 · Chapter 11 — Skirts, panels, Clicky-Clack door, filtration

Do:

  1. Ignore p.228 and p.231.
  2. Confirm Ch 10's wiring: both fans on the 3×2 splicer, the splicer on its printed spacer, the run on FAN2 / PF7.
  3. Dress the leads into the duct, clear of the blades.

Parts:

  • 3×2 XH splicer PCB ×1, its printed spacer (supplied printed by LDO)

Check

Both fans on one splicer; splicer on its spacer, not touching aluminium; PCB FAN plugged into FAN2/PF7; no lead within reach of a blade.

What you're looking at

The two manual pages describe a BTT Octopus controller this kit does not have. You are confirming Ch 10's wiring instead: both fans on one 3×2 splicer PCB, that PCB on its printed spacer, and the run landing on the Leviathan's FAN2 port.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: fan map for this build — PCB fan → FAN2/PF7; LED strip → LED-Strip/PE6; filter fan → FAN3/PF9. "Please remember to mount 3x2 splicing PCBs using the printed part to prevent a short with the extrusion." src

Source: Voron manual p.228 · Voron manual p.231 · LDO wiring guide § Connecting the fans and the LED strip

docs.text: Ch 11 › Part A — before first power-up19 / 66

docs.title: Step 11.19 — Fit the bestagon insert (optional)
docs.text:
Step 19 of 66 · Chapter 11 — Skirts, panels, Clicky-Clack door, filtration

(no image — see LDO STLs README)

Parts:

  • ldo_bestagon_insert ×1 (orange), or as many as you printed

Check

Insert flush and retained; the hexagon is not stressed white at the corners.

What you're looking at

The bestagon insert is a purely cosmetic orange plug that snaps into one of the hexagonal openings in a skirt segment. Nothing depends on it.

docs.title: Step 11.2 — Heat-set the skirt segments
docs.text: Ch 11 › Part A — before first power-up2 / 66

docs.title: Step 11.2 — Heat-set the skirt segments
docs.text:
Step 2 of 66 · Chapter 11 — Skirts, panels, Clicky-Clack door, filtration

Do: Press an insert into every boss the page highlights: the top rail boss and the pair inside each curved cut-out. Part flat, tongue flush to the insert height, insert square, same tip temperature as the earlier 153.

Parts:

  • M3×5×4 brass heat-set inserts — the page shows 2–3 per segment (verify on bench)

Check

Every insert flush or just below, none proud, no bulge on the show face. An M3×8 SHCS turns in freely by hand.

What you're looking at

Heat-set inserts are brass M3×5×4 sleeves melted into a printed boss to give it a real metal thread. The skirt segments take two or three each: one in the top rail, a pair inside each curved cut-out.

Tip

the iron is hot: do the rest now. Fan grill retainers ×8 at 11.3, TFT mount ×2 at 11.5, Nevermore ×6 at 11.28, Clicky-Clack latch ×1 at 11.49. src

Source: Voron manual p.212 · LDO Rev D printed-parts guide

docs.title: Step 11.20 — VHB the bottom-panel clips and hinges
docs.text: Ch 11 › Part A — before first power-up20 / 66

docs.title: Step 11.20 — VHB the bottom-panel clips and hinges
docs.text:
Step 20 of 66 · Chapter 11 — Skirts, panels, Clicky-Clack door, filtration

Do:

  1. Put the printer on its side, as at 10.1.
  2. Wipe all six pad faces with IPA and let it flash off.
  3. Cut six VHB pads to match, press one onto each, liners left on.

Parts:

  • bottom_panel_clip_x4 ×4, bottom_panel_hinge_x2 ×2, 3M VHB tape ×6 pads

Check

Six parts, six pads, each centred with no overhang onto a curved face, liners still on.

What you're looking at

3M VHB is a double-sided acrylic foam tape that reaches most of its strength within an hour and does not come off again. These six printed parts, four clips and two hinges, are what the bottom panel bonds to.

Source: Voron manual p.232

← PreviousStep 11.19 — Fit the bestagon insert (optional)

Next →Step 11.21 — Fit the bottom panel

docs.title: Step 11.21 — Fit the bottom panel
docs.text: Ch 11 › Part A — before first power-up21 / 66

docs.title: Step 11.21 — Fit the bottom panel
docs.text:
Step 21 of 66 · Chapter 11 — Skirts, panels, Clicky-Clack door, filtration

Do:

  1. Screw the hinges to the rear extrusion and the clips front and sides, one M3×8 SHCS each.
  2. Peel the film off both panel faces, pull the liners, and press the panel home, hinge edge at the rear.

Parts:

  • bottom panel (acrylic, black, 469×469×4 mm) ×1, the six taped parts from 11.20, M3×8 SHCS ×6, M3 T-nut ×6 (p.233 draws the screws straight into the extrusion — one nut per screw, verify on bench)

Check

Panel square, equal margins, no rock, every pad bonded. After an hour, release the front clips and swing it down, clearing the skirt ring.

What you're looking at

The bottom panel is the 4 mm acrylic floor of the electronics bay, and it is a door: VHB-bonded to two rear hinges and held by four snap clips, it unclips at the front and swings down for access through Ch 13.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: the bottom panel is the 4 mm acrylic, not the 3 mm deck panel. If you are holding a 469×469 panel and cannot tell which is which, caliper it — 3 mm is the deck (fitted back in Ch 02), 4 mm is this one. src

Tip

swing the door with the machine still on its side or up on blocks; confirm every duct is reachable, then close it.

Good stopping point · ~20 min since the last one

bay-fan wiring verified against Ch 10, bestagon insert decided, VHB pads pressed and the bottom panel hung on its rear hinges and front clips. Leave the VHB to cure undisturbed — do not swing the door open until it has; do not press a pad and walk away before the panel is on it.

Source: Voron manual p.232 · Voron manual p.233 · LDO Rev D 350 BOM

docs.title: Step 11.22 — Choose the Z belt cover variant
docs.text: Ch 11 › Part A — before first power-up22 / 66

docs.title: Step 11.22 — Choose the Z belt cover variant
docs.text:
Step 22 of 66 · Chapter 11 — Skirts, panels, Clicky-Clack door, filtration

Do: Check how Ch 10 routed the chamber LED wiring. Ch 10 used the extrusion slot, so the stock covers apply. If any LED wire passes through a Z-motor opening, print LDO's z_belt_cover_a_led for that corner, a 7 g, 25-minute part.

Parts:

  • z_belt_cover_a_x2 ×2 and z_belt_cover_b_x2 ×2 — or LDO's z_belt_cover_a_led in place of z_belt_cover_a

Check

You can state, per corner, which cover goes on and why. No cable crosses a stock cover's sealing face.

What you're looking at

A Z belt cover is a printed shroud that clips over each of the four Z belts at a frame corner, so nothing can be drawn into the belt. LDO's alternate _a_led version adds a cable slot for LED wiring routed through a Z-motor opening.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: "PAGE 234 Use the alternate Z-belt cover if you routed the LED wires through the Z-motor opening." src · part

Source: Voron manual p.234 · LDO Build Notes p.234 · LDOVoron2 z_belt_cover_a_led.stl

docs.title: Step 11.23 — Load each cover with a hammerhead nut
docs.text: Ch 11 › Part A — before first power-up23 / 66

docs.title: Step 11.23 — Load each cover with a hammerhead nut
docs.text:
Step 23 of 66 · Chapter 11 — Skirts, panels, Clicky-Clack door, filtration

Do: Drop an M3 hammerhead nut into the recess on the back of each cover and start an M3×6 BHCS into it from the front, two or three turns only, so the nut stays captive but free to rotate.

Parts:

  • Z belt covers ×4, M3 hammerhead T-nut ×4, M3×6 BHCS ×4

Check

Nut captive, screw started, nut still able to turn, the head still reachable with a 2 mm hex once the cover is on.

What you're looking at

A hammerhead T-nut drops straight into an extrusion slot from the face rather than rolling in from an end, then rotates a quarter turn under load to lock. Starting the screw keeps the nut captive in the cover's recess.

Source: Voron manual p.234

docs.title: Step 11.24 — Fit the first Z belt cover
docs.text: Ch 11 › Part A — before first power-up24 / 66

docs.title: Step 11.24 — Fit the first Z belt cover
docs.text:
Step 24 of 66 · Chapter 11 — Skirts, panels, Clicky-Clack door, filtration

Do:

  1. Pinch the Z belt flat and slide the cover in, belt through its slot, hammerhead nut into the channel.
  2. Hold the cover square, tighten the M3×6 BHCS. If the nut spins, back off and re-seat it squarely.

Parts:

  • one loaded cover from 11.23

Check

Cover flat against the extrusion, the Z belt running through freely with no rub, the cover not moving when pushed.

What you're looking at

The cover goes on with the belt already threaded through its slot, which is why the belt is pinched flat first. The click you feel is the hammerhead nut rotating and biting inside the extrusion channel.

Source: Voron manual p.235

docs.title: Step 11.25 — Fit the remaining three Z belt covers
docs.text: Ch 11 › Part A — before first power-up25 / 66

docs.title: Step 11.25 — Fit the remaining three Z belt covers
docs.text:
Step 25 of 66 · Chapter 11 — Skirts, panels, Clicky-Clack door, filtration

Do: Repeat 11.24 at the other three Z belt corners. Then run the gantry up and down its full travel by hand and watch each cover.

Parts:

  • the three remaining loaded covers

Check

Four covers on, all four belts running clear, no rubbing anywhere in the full Z travel.

What you're looking at

The remaining three corners are identical. The full-travel run afterwards is the real test: a cover that touches a belt makes noise now and cuts the belt edge over months.

Tip

p.237 is a page of Voron history, nothing to build.

Good stopping point · ~15 min since the last one

all four Z belt covers on, each with its hammerhead nut, and the gantry runs its full Z travel without touching one.

Source: Voron manual p.236 · Voron manual p.237

docs.title: Step 11.26 — Break out the Nevermore printed supports
docs.text: Ch 11 › Part A — before first power-up26 / 66

docs.title: Step 11.26 — Break out the Nevermore printed supports
docs.text:
Step 26 of 66 · Chapter 11 — Skirts, panels, Clicky-Clack door, filtration

(no image — see LDO Nevermore V5 Duo guide)

Do: The cartridge and the plenum each carry a built-in printed support. Push them out; they break at the interface. Do not cut them out with a knife.

Parts:

  • V2_Duo_Plenum, V2_Duo_Plenum_LID, Regular_Cartridge, Regular_Cartridge_Lid

Check

Both supports removed cleanly, no torn layers on the sealing faces, the cartridge lid slides freely in the cartridge grooves.

What you're looking at

The Nevermore is a recirculating activated-carbon filter that sits inside the chamber and scrubs the fumes ASA gives off. Four printed parts make it: a plenum holding two blower fans, its lid, and a magnetic cartridge with its own lid for the carbon.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: you are building the Regular cartridge, not the XL — the XL wants a larger carbon charge and a faster, louder fan. src

Source: LDO Nevermore V5 Duo guide § Preparation · Nevermore Micro repo

docs.title: Step 11.27 — Modify both 5015 fan enclosures
docs.text: Ch 11 › Part A — before first power-up27 / 66

docs.title: Step 11.27 — Modify both 5015 fan enclosures
docs.text:
Step 27 of 66 · Chapter 11 — Skirts, panels, Clicky-Clack door, filtration

(no image — see LDO Nevermore guide § Preparation)

Do:

  1. Pry the tabs holding each fan's enclosure together and separate it.
  2. With wire snips, remove the section of plastic the guide highlights from each housing.
  3. Use snips, not a blade.

Parts:

  • 5015 fan ×2 (supplied in the kit's Nevermore bag)

Check

Both fans modified identically, impellers still spin freely, no cracked housing, no swarf left inside the scroll.

What you're looking at

A 5015 blower is a 50 × 15 mm squirrel-cage fan: it makes pressure rather than free-air flow, which is what pushes chamber air through packed carbon. Both housings have to be opened and a section of plastic removed so they fit the plenum.

Source: LDO Nevermore V5 Duo guide § Preparation · Video: Extras! @2:30:00

docs.title: Step 11.28 — Heat-set the Nevermore parts
docs.text:
Step 28 of 66 · Chapter 11 — Skirts, panels, Clicky-Clack door, filtration

(no image — see LDO Nevermore guide § Preparation)

Do: Four inserts go into the fan mounting holes, one into the plenum, one into the cartridge. Six total.

Parts:

  • M3×5×4 heat-set inserts ×6

Check

All six flush and square; an M3 screw starts freely in each.

What you're looking at

Six inserts, three destinations: four in the fan mounting holes, one in the plenum for its lid screw, one in the cartridge for its lid screw. Nothing else on the Nevermore takes a threaded fastener.

docs.title: Step 11.29 — Cut the connector off the long-wire fan
docs.text: Ch 11 › Part A — before first power-up29 / 66

docs.title: Step 11.29 — Cut the connector off the long-wire fan
docs.text:
Step 29 of 66 · Chapter 11 — Skirts, panels, Clicky-Clack door, filtration

(no image — see LDO Nevermore guide § Preparation)

Do: Cut the JST connector off the longer-leaded fan. Keep the connector pigtail; it gets soldered back onto the bridge PCB at 11.33.

Parts:

  • the 5015 fan with the longer lead

Check

Connector cut free and set aside somewhere you will not lose it; both fan leads still long enough to route through the plenum.

What you're looking at

The fan with the longer lead has its plug cut off so both fans can be soldered to the bridge PCB, a small board that parallels them onto one lead. The cut-off pigtail is the only connector that mates with the FILTER FAN extension.

Good stopping point · ~15 min since the last one

Nevermore supports broken off, both 5015 enclosures trimmed, inserts melted, and the long-wire fan's connector cut off with the leads tinned. Nothing is glued and nothing is soldered to the bridge PCB yet.

docs.title: Step 11.3 — Heat-set the fan grill retainers and identify the bay fans
docs.text: Ch 11 › Part A — before first power-up3 / 66

docs.title: Step 11.3 — Heat-set the fan grill retainers and identify the bay fans
docs.text:
Step 3 of 66 · Chapter 11 — Skirts, panels, Clicky-Clack door, filtration

Do: Press four inserts into the corner bosses of each retainer. Find the two 60×20 fans and read the airflow arrow on each frame edge, not on the hub. You orient both the same way at 11.11.

Parts:

  • [a]_fan_grill_retainer ×2, M3×5×4 heat-set inserts ×8 (4 per retainer), 60×60×20 mm 24 V fan ×2

Check

Eight inserts flush; a fan sits flat on a retainer with all four holes lining up on the inserts.

What you're looking at

The fan grill retainer is the printed frame that sits inside a side_fan_support opening with a bay fan captured in it. Its four corner bosses take the inserts the grill screws bite into. The two 60 × 20 mm fans are the electronics-bay coolers.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: the kit ships exactly two 60×60×20 mm 24 V fans and one 3×2 XH splicer PCB, which joins them into a single "PCB FAN" run. Do not expect four. src · src

Source: Voron manual p.213 · LDO Rev D 350 BOM · LDO wiring guide § Connecting the fans and the LED strip

docs.title: Step 11.30 — Fit the first fan into the plenum
docs.text: Ch 11 › Part A — before first power-up30 / 66

docs.title: Step 11.30 — Fit the first fan into the plenum
docs.text:
Step 30 of 66 · Chapter 11 — Skirts, panels, Clicky-Clack door, filtration

(no image — see LDO Nevermore guide § Install Fans)

Do: Route the fan's wires from the right side of the plenum, right to left along the wire channel, with tweezers. Then seat the fan in the right side and pull the wire flat in the channel.

Parts:

  • the cut-lead fan from 11.29, plenum

Check

Fan seated fully with the impeller clear of the plenum wall; wire flat in the channel, not crossing the fan aperture.

What you're looking at

The plenum's wire channel is a moulded groove that carries both fans' leads to one corner. Routing the wire before seating the fan is the only order that works: once the fan is in, the channel is behind it.

Source: LDO Nevermore V5 Duo guide § Install Fans

docs.title: Step 11.31 — Fit the second fan and trim the leads
docs.text: Ch 11 › Part A — before first power-up31 / 66

docs.title: Step 11.31 — Fit the second fan and trim the leads
docs.text:
Step 31 of 66 · Chapter 11 — Skirts, panels, Clicky-Clack door, filtration

(no image — see LDO Nevermore guide § Install Fans)

Do: Route its wires from the left side of the plenum, right to left, and seat the fan in the left side. Now cut both fans' wires to equal length, roughly 30–40 mm proud of the enclosure.

Parts:

  • the second 5015 fan

Check

Both fans seated, all four wire ends the same length at 30–40 mm, both impellers spin freely.

What you're looking at

The second fan mirrors the first. Cutting all four wire ends to the same 30–40 mm now is what makes the bridge-PCB soldering at 11.33 tidy, and it also fixes the plenum's mounting position later.

Source: LDO Nevermore V5 Duo guide § Install Fans

docs.title: Step 11.32 — Bolt the fans to the plenum
docs.text: Ch 11 › Part A — before first power-up32 / 66

docs.title: Step 11.32 — Bolt the fans to the plenum
docs.text:
Step 32 of 66 · Chapter 11 — Skirts, panels, Clicky-Clack door, filtration

(no image — see LDO Nevermore guide § Install Fans)

Do: Drive the four M3×16 BHCS into the fan heat-sets from 11.28. Snug only; a 5015 housing distorts and the impeller rubs if you crank them.

Parts:

  • M3×16 BHCS ×4

Check

Both fans held with no rock; spin each impeller by hand and listen for rub.

What you're looking at

The M3×16 BHCS pass through the fan bodies into the heat-sets from 11.28. A 5015 housing is thin plastic and will distort if these are cranked, which shows up as the impeller rubbing.

Source: LDO Nevermore V5 Duo guide § Install Fans

docs.title: Step 11.33 — Solder the fans to the bridge PCB
docs.text: Ch 11 › Part A — before first power-up33 / 66

docs.title: Step 11.33 — Solder the fans to the bridge PCB
docs.text:
Step 33 of 66 · Chapter 11 — Skirts, panels, Clicky-Clack door, filtration

(no image — see LDO Nevermore guide § Install Fans)

Do:

  1. Solder both fans' wires and the pigtail to the bridge PCB, red to the top pads, black to the bottom.
  2. Arrange the wires as the guide's photo shows.
  3. Meter for a short between positive and negative.

Parts:

  • bridge PCB ×1, the connector pigtail saved at 11.29

Check

Continuity reads open between + and −; all six joints shiny and mechanically sound; PCB sits in its compartment without pressing on a wire.

What you're looking at

The bridge PCB is a small board that joins both fans and the saved pigtail into one 24 V pair, red to the top pads, black to the bottom. A solder bridge here puts a dead short across the mainboard's 24 V fan output.

Caution

A bad solder here shorts a 24 V rail. LDO: "A bad solder will result in permanently damaging the controller board." Do the meter check before anything gets plugged in. src

Good stopping point · ~20 min since the last one

both fans seated in the plenum, leads trimmed to length and soldered to the bridge PCB, and the pair metered for a short. The plenum is open and unglued.

Source: LDO Nevermore V5 Duo guide § Install Fans · Video: Extras! @2:36:20

← PreviousStep 11.32 — Bolt the fans to the plenum

docs.title: Step 11.34 — Glue the plenum magnets
docs.text: Ch 11 › Part A — before first power-up34 / 66

docs.title: Step 11.34 — Glue the plenum magnets
docs.text:
Step 34 of 66 · Chapter 11 — Skirts, panels, Clicky-Clack door, filtration

(no image — see LDO Nevermore guide § Nevermore Assembly)

Do: Drop a spot of super glue into each magnet pocket in the plenum and press a magnet in, one at a time, all with the same pole facing out. Press each fully home so none stands proud.

Parts:

  • 6×3 mm neodymium magnets, super glue

Check

All plenum magnets flush and the same polarity across the set: a spare magnet is attracted to every one the same way.

What you're looking at

The plenum and cartridge hold together on magnets rather than screws, so the cartridge can be pulled off to recharge the carbon. Every magnet in the plenum must go in with the same pole facing out, otherwise half of them will repel the cartridge.

Source: LDO Nevermore V5 Duo guide § Nevermore Assembly · Video: Extras! @2:59:56

← PreviousStep 11.33 — Solder the fans to the bridge PCB

docs.title: Step 11.35 — Close the plenum lid
docs.text: Ch 11 › Part A — before first power-up35 / 66

docs.title: Step 11.35 — Close the plenum lid
docs.text:
Step 35 of 66 · Chapter 11 — Skirts, panels, Clicky-Clack door, filtration

(no image — see LDO Nevermore guide § Nevermore Assembly)

Do: Slide the lid into the plenum body's grooves and secure with the M3×6 BHCS into the plenum heat-set. Add the optional M3×4 on the other side if you want it to look symmetric.

Parts:

  • V2_Duo_Plenum_LID, M3×6 BHCS ×1 (optional second M3×4 BHCS for symmetry)

Check

Lid fully home in both grooves, screw snug, no wire pinched at the lid edge.

What you're looking at

The lid slides into grooves in the plenum body and one screw holds it. It closes the fan compartment so the blowers push air through the cartridge rather than straight back out.

Source: LDO Nevermore V5 Duo guide § Nevermore Assembly

docs.title: Step 11.36 — Glue the cartridge magnets to match
docs.text: Ch 11 › Part A — before first power-up36 / 66

docs.title: Step 11.36 — Glue the cartridge magnets to match
docs.text:
Step 36 of 66 · Chapter 11 — Skirts, panels, Clicky-Clack door, filtration

(no image — see LDO Nevermore guide § Cartridge Assembly)

Do: Stick each magnet to the assembled plenum, mark the exposed face, and keep that orientation. Then glue them into the cartridge pockets one at a time, marked face out.

Parts:

  • 6×3 mm neodymium magnets, super glue, a marker

Check

Cartridge offers up to the plenum and snaps home; it holds against a firm shake; all magnets flush.

What you're looking at

This is the matching half of 11.34, and the reason for the marker: a magnet's polarity is invisible once it is glued in. Stick each one to the finished plenum first, mark the exposed face, and glue it that way round.

Source: LDO Nevermore V5 Duo guide § Cartridge Assembly

← PreviousStep 11.35 — Close the plenum lid

Next →Step 11.37 — Fill and close the cartridge

docs.title: Step 11.37 — Fill and close the cartridge
docs.text: Ch 11 › Part A — before first power-up37 / 66

docs.title: Step 11.37 — Fill and close the cartridge
docs.text:
Step 37 of 66 · Chapter 11 — Skirts, panels, Clicky-Clack door, filtration

(no image — see LDO Nevermore guide § Cartridge Assembly)

Do: Fill the cartridge with acid-free activated carbon pellets, then slide the lid into its grooves and secure with the M3×6 BHCS into the cartridge heat-set.

Parts:

  • Regular_Cartridge_Lid, M3×6 BHCS ×1, activated carbon pellets — not supplied

Check

Cartridge full but not packed so tight that airflow stops; lid home; no pellets loose in the grooves.

What you're looking at

The cartridge is the removable box that holds the activated carbon, acid-free pellets, which are not in the kit. An empty cartridge still has to be fitted and closed, or the plenum just stirs the chamber.

Caution

Media not in the kit. LDO: "NOT INCLUDED WITH THE KIT", and acid-free pellets are specified. Nevermore media is on the deferred list for this build, so install and wire the filter now and fill the cartridge later. Fit the empty, closed cartridge for now so the plenum is sealed. src

Good stopping point · ~20 min since the last one

plenum and cartridge magnets glued in matching polarity, both lids closed, cartridge filled. Never stop between gluing the plenum magnets and the cartridge magnets: the second set has to be matched to the first while you still know which way round they went.

Source: LDO Nevermore V5 Duo guide § Cartridge Assembly

← PreviousStep 11.36 — Glue the cartridge magnets to match

docs.title: Step 11.38 — Mount the plenum in the chamber
docs.text: Ch 11 › Part A — before first power-up38 / 66

docs.title: Step 11.38 — Mount the plenum in the chamber
docs.text:
Step 38 of 66 · Chapter 11 — Skirts, panels, Clicky-Clack door, filtration

Do: Roll one M3 T-nut into the inside face of each bed extrusion, not the top slot, and bolt the plenum on with two M3×12 SHCS. The fan leads were cut to length for this position at 11.31.

Parts:

  • M3 roll-in T-nut ×2, M3×12 SHCS ×2

Check

Plenum solid on the extrusions, sitting inboard and below the bed surface; nothing it can foul as the gantry descends; both screws snug.

What you're looking at

The plenum bolts to the inside faces of the two bed extrusions, low and inboard, where it is below the bed surface and out of the gantry's way. The photo is LDO's placement reference, with the two T-nuts already rolled in.

Source: LDO Nevermore V5 Duo guide § Installation for Voron V2.4 · LDO wiring photo nevermore_base_placement.jpg

← PreviousStep 11.37 — Fill and close the cartridge

docs.title: Step 11.39 — Attach the cartridge
docs.text: Ch 11 › Part A — before first power-up39 / 66

docs.title: Step 11.39 — Attach the cartridge
docs.text:
Step 39 of 66 · Chapter 11 — Skirts, panels, Clicky-Clack door, filtration

(no image — see LDO Nevermore guide § Installation for Voron V2.4)

Do: Slide the cartridge along until the magnets take, and let it pull itself home.

Parts:

  • cartridge from 11.37

Check

Cartridge seated square on the plenum with no gap at the joint; it comes off with a deliberate pull and not with an accidental knock.

What you're looking at

Nothing but magnets holds the cartridge on. That is the point: carbon is consumable, and this joint is the one you will open every few hundred hours.

Source: LDO Nevermore V5 Duo guide § Installation for Voron V2.4

docs.title: Step 11.4 — Do not build the mini12864 module
docs.text: Ch 11 › Part A — before first power-up4 / 66

docs.title: Step 11.4 — Do not build the mini12864 module
docs.text:
Step 4 of 66 · Chapter 11 — Skirts, panels, Clicky-Clack door, filtration

Do: Skip p.211, p.214, p.215 and p.216; they build a display module this kit does not have. Confirm you never printed mini12864_case_front, mini12864_case_rear, [a]_mini12864_case_hinge, [a]_mini12864_case_front_insert or [a]_btt_knob_light_shield.

Parts:

  • none. The M3×12 SHCS, M3×40 SHCS and the length of filament these pages call for stay in the bag

Check

No mini12864 parts in your bins. The front-centre ring position is filled by the BTT mount from B08.

What you're looking at

The four manual pages show the mini12864, the small monochrome LCD with a click-wheel that a stock Voron uses as its display. This kit ships a 4.3" colour touchscreen instead, so all four pages, and every part on them, are dead.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: "For Rev C/D please use The BigTreeTech touchscreen, print the mount from here." The mount STL is in the LDOVoronTrident repo — it is not in the Voron-2 tree. src · mount

Good stopping point · ~20 min since the last one

every skirt segment dry-fitted and checked for rock, inserts melted into the segments and the two fan grill retainers, and the mini12864 parts set aside unbuilt. Nothing is bolted to the frame yet.

Source: Voron manual p.211 · Voron manual p.214–216 · LDO Build Notes p.211, p.214–216 · LDO BTT Pi TFT4.3 mount README

docs.title: Step 11.40 — Connect the filter fan
docs.text: Ch 11 › Part A — before first power-up40 / 66

docs.title: Step 11.40 — Connect the filter fan
docs.text:
Step 40 of 66 · Chapter 11 — Skirts, panels, Clicky-Clack door, filtration

(no image — see LDO wiring guide § Connecting the Fans and the LED Strip)

Do: Mate the Nevermore's pigtail with the FILTER FAN extension and follow it back to the Leviathan. It lands on FAN3 / PF9. Confirm that header's voltage-selection jumper is set for 24 V before anything is powered.

Parts:

  • the kit's FILTER FAN extension wire

Check

Filter fan on FAN3/PF9; 24 V jumper confirmed; the lead is routed in the duct and cannot be caught by the bed or the gantry.

What you're looking at

The FILTER FAN extension is the kit lead already run to FAN3 in Ch 10 Step 10.48 and left coiled at the rear of the chamber. This step mates the Nevermore's pigtail to it. The Nevermore guide names an Octopus pin; this machine's port is FAN3 / PF9.

Caution

Rev D+ / LDO: the Nevermore guide was written for a BTT Octopus and tells you to use "Octopus Fan3 - Pinout PD13". This machine has a Leviathan. Use FAN3 / PF9 from the Rev D wiring guide's fan table. src

Source: LDO wiring guide § Connecting the fans and the LED strip · Video: Extras! @2:48:31

docs.title: Step 11.41 — Note the filter fan config for Ch 12
docs.text:
Step 41 of 66 · Chapter 11 — Skirts, panels, Clicky-Clack door, filtration

(no image — see LDO Nevermore guide § Configuration printer.cfg)

Do: Write the pin on a tag and tape it to the plenum. LDO's [heater_fan exhaust_fan] section is right in shape but its pin: PD13 is the Octopus pin and must become the Leviathan's PF9. Step 12.32 replaces it with [fan_generic nevermore] on the same pin.

Parts: none.

Tag on the plenum reading "FILTER FAN → FAN3 / PF9". Ch 12's config checklist has the Nevermore section on it.

What you're looking at

Nothing to build: you are writing down a pin number so Ch 12 does not have to re-derive it. LDO's published config section is right in shape but names the wrong board's pin.

docs.title: Step 11.42 — Fit the bowden retainer
docs.text: Ch 11 › Part A — before first power-up42 / 66

docs.title: Step 11.42 — Fit the bowden retainer
docs.text:
Step 42 of 66 · Chapter 11 — Skirts, panels, Clicky-Clack door, filtration

Do:

  1. Drop the hammerhead nut into the retainer's recess, start the M3×8 SHCS, and slide it onto the top rear extrusion.
  2. Position it so the PTFE curves smoothly into the toolhead umbilical, then tighten to lock.

Parts:

  • bowden_retainer ×1, M3 hammerhead T-nut ×1, M3×8 SHCS ×1

Check

Retainer solid on the extrusion; the PTFE passes through with light drag only; no sharp bend where the tube leaves the retainer.

What you're looking at

The bowden retainer is a small printed clamp on the top rear extrusion that holds the PTFE tube guiding filament from the spool into the toolhead umbilical. Its only job is to stop the tube kinking where it changes direction.

Source: Voron manual p.257 · Voron manual p.258 · Video: Part 9 @3:13:57

← PreviousStep 11.41 — Note the filter fan config for Ch 12

Next →Step 11.43 — Fit the spool holder arm

docs.title: Step 11.43 — Fit the spool holder arm
docs.text: Ch 11 › Part A — before first power-up43 / 66

docs.title: Step 11.43 — Fit the spool holder arm
docs.text:
Step 43 of 66 · Chapter 11 — Skirts, panels, Clicky-Clack door, filtration

Do:

  1. Press the two short PTFE lengths into the grooves along the arm.
  2. Roll the M5 T-nuts into the rear vertical extrusion at spool height, offer the arm up, and drive the M5×16 BHCS home.

Parts:

  • spool_holder ×1, PTFE tube offcuts ×2 (4 mm OD), M5 T-nut ×2, M5×16 BHCS ×2 (verify on bench)

Check

Arm level and solid enough for a full 1 kg spool, both PTFE inserts seated, a spool spinning with light finger pressure without binding.

What you're looking at

The spool holder is the printed arm that carries a 1 kg filament spool on the rear of the machine. The two short PTFE offcuts pressed into its grooves are the bearing surface the spool turns on.

Good stopping point · ~15 min since the last one

Nevermore mounted in the chamber, cartridge attached, filter fan connected to the Ch 10 lead, bowden retainer and spool holder arm fitted. Its config is [fan_generic nevermore] on PF9 (11.41) — Ch 12 Step 12.32 already wrote it; confirm it is there before you close this session.

Source: Voron manual p.259 · Video: Part 9 @3:11:11

docs.title: Step 11.44 — Assemble the Clicky-Clack door frame
docs.text: Ch 11 › Part A — before first power-up44 / 66

docs.title: Step 11.44 — Assemble the Clicky-Clack door frame
docs.text:
Step 44 of 66 · Chapter 11 — Skirts, panels, Clicky-Clack door, filtration

(no image — see KB3D install guide · mod README)

Do:

  1. Start an M5×16 BHCS halfway into each tapped end.
  2. Bring the access-hole pieces onto one tapped piece, tighten through the holes, square each corner.
  3. Three sides only, slide the acrylic in, then close the fourth.

Parts:

  • door frame extrusions, 2 × HFSFB5-2020-470-TPW (X, 470 mm) and 2 × HFSFB5-2020-530-LCH-RCH (Z, 530 mm) for a 350
  • M5×16 BHCS ×4
  • the 480 × 500 × 3 mm clear acrylic door panel
  • sort the four extrusions by eye: two show an M5 thread in the end face, the other two a round access hole through the side wall near each end (verify on bench — the KB3D guide names which; the Misumi suffixes are not decoded here)

Check

All four corners square, the acrylic fully home with no bow, no twist on a flat surface, and the hinge side written down.

What you're looking at

Clicky-Clack is the magnetic-latch front door: a 2020 aluminium frame around one clear acrylic panel, hung on lift-off hinges and closed by a magnetic handle and latch. The corners are blind joints, a screw through an access hole into a tapped end face.

Caution

You are using the plain acrylic panel from Fabreeko, not the NanoNest stack the KB3D guide illustrates. Skip the KB3D guide's NanoNest taping section entirely; the panel goes straight into the frame slot. src

Tip

hinges go on the left seen from the front, latch on the right. Mirror every left and right in 11.57 and 11.62–11.64 to reverse the swing.

Source: KB3D Clicky-Clack install guide § Frame Assembly · Clicky-Clack mod README · Fabreeko acrylic panel

← PreviousStep 11.43 — Fit the spool holder arm

docs.title: Step 11.45 — Fit the rubber panel retainer strip
docs.text: Ch 11 › Part A — before first power-up45 / 66

docs.title: Step 11.45 — Fit the rubber panel retainer strip
docs.text:
Step 45 of 66 · Chapter 11 — Skirts, panels, Clicky-Clack door, filtration

(no image — see mod README)

Do: Cut the strip to length for each side with 45° mitres at the corners, then press it into the extrusion groove alongside the acrylic. It takes up the clearance and stops the panel rattling.

Parts:

  • HSCPF3H-B-2000 retainer strip (supplied in the LDO frame kit)

Check

Strip seated all the way round with the mitres closed; the acrylic no longer moves in the frame when you tap it.

What you're looking at

The rubber retainer strip is an extruded profile that presses into the frame groove alongside the acrylic and takes up the clearance. Without it the panel rattles in its slot every time the door closes.

Source: Clicky-Clack mod README
